mcla_test_crash.help:
"Crash test for the Linux crash logger: MODE or MODE:SECONDS (5 seconds by default), a few "
    "seconds after the game has started. segv writes to address 0x10 on a worker thread; guest "
    "reads the guest's null page (the runtime logs 'Unhandled guest access violation' first, as for "
    "a real guest crash); stack runs a worker thread out of stack (it has a signal stack); abort "
    "calls abort(); terminate throws an exception nobody catches; illegal runs an illegal "
    "instruction; fpe divides by zero. The log must end with '!!! CRASH DETECTED !!!' (or '!!! "
    "ABORT DETECTED !!!') and a stack trace, and the game dies with the signal's status. Only works "
    "with the debug menu unlocked. Linux only."

precache_pipelines.help:
"Prepares the graphics pipelines the game compiles while it starts, and closes, without "
    "starting the game: no window, no graphics output. The launcher runs this at the end of its "
    "setup (after the shader packs are built), so that the first start has no shaders to compile "
    "and no pipeline pending. It fills the graphics driver's own cache for this PC; it does not "
    "have to be repeated until the driver, the game files or LARecomp change (the next run "
    "notices and does nothing when everything is current). Progress is printed to the console. "
    "Exit code 0 when the pipelines are prepared or need nothing."

precache_pipelines_backend.help:
"With precache_pipelines: which graphics API to prepare. Empty (or auto) is the one the game "
    "runs on (graphics_backend). d3d12 or vulkan prepares that one; one API per run."

precache_pipelines_force.help:
"With precache_pipelines: prepare even when the last run says the pipelines are current. For "
    "after the graphics driver's shader cache was cleared (Windows' Disk Cleanup does that)."

precache_pipelines_threads.help:
"With precache_pipelines: how many threads compile the pipelines. 0 uses every processor but "
    "one. A lower number leaves the PC more usable meanwhile, and the preparation takes longer."

shader_pack_threads.help:
"How many threads build the shader packs from your game files on the first start. 0 chooses "
    "by itself from the processor's cores and the free memory. A lower number leaves the PC more "
    "usable during the build, which then takes longer."

build_shader_packs.help:
"Builds the shader packs from your game files and closes, without starting the game: no "
    "window, no graphics. The launcher runs this at the end of its setup so that the first start "
    "has nothing to build. Progress is printed to the console; the log is logs/shader_build.txt. "
    "Exit code 0 when the packs are in place."

build_shader_packs_force.help: "With build_shader_packs: build even when the packs in place are current."

build_city_pack.help:
"Builds the city pack (the city's geometry, for ray traced shadows) from your game files and closes, without starting the game: no "
    "window, no graphics. The launcher runs this in its setup on a PC whose graphics card can ray trace, so that ray traced shadows are ready at the first start; "
    "the game builds it itself in the background when it is missing and ray traced shadows are on. Progress is printed to the console; the log is "
    "logs/city_pack_build.txt. Exit code 0 when the pack is in place."

build_city_pack_force.help: "With build_city_pack: build even when the pack in place is current."

build_city_hit.help:
"Builds the city hit data (the hit file and the texture file beside the city pack: the city's surfaces and pictures, for the ray traced effects "
    "that read them) from your game files and closes, without starting the game: no window, no graphics. It needs the city pack (build_city_pack first, or both on one command "
    "line). The launcher runs this in its setup on a PC whose graphics card can ray trace, so that those effects are ready at the first start; the game builds it itself in the "
    "background when it is missing and an effect that reads it is on. Progress is printed to the console like build_city_pack's; the log is logs/city_hit_build.txt. "
    "Exit code 0 when the hit data is in place."

build_city_hit_force.help: "With build_city_hit: build even when the hit data in place is current."

check_city_hit.help:
"Checks the city hit data and closes, without starting the game: is it in place and current for your game files and the city pack beside it? "
    "Stat only (a moment): exit code 0 and the result 'up to date', or 1 and 'not current' with the reason. With build_city_hit, the check runs after the build. Progress "
    "is printed to the console like build_city_pack's; the log is logs/city_hit_check.txt."

check_city_hit_deep.help:
"With check_city_hit: read the files back whole instead of checking the stamp (seconds, not a moment): the city pack, the hit file against "
    "it, and every picture of the texture file. Exit code 0 when all are whole, 1 with the counts of the problems when not."

mcla_native_gfx.help: "The D3D12 native graphics runtime. Not built on this platform."
comments: // The cvars native_gfx.cpp defines and the guest-side files Plume shares read.

mcla_native_gfx_decl_float.help: "Read the two 32-bit float vertex declaration types at their measured width."

mcla_native_gfx_depth32.help: "Give a guest kD24S8 depth surface a D32_FLOAT_S8X24 host format."

mcla_native_gfx_diag.help: "Native graphics diagnostics. Not built on this platform."

mcla_native_gfx_fetch_size_unit.help: "Bytes per unit of the vertex fetch constant's 24-bit size field. 0 uses 4."

larecomp_discord_rpc.help: "Enable Discord Rich Presence. Live: off clears the presence at once, on shows the game's current state at once."

larecomp_discord_rpc_log_state.help: "Log Discord RPC state changes with printf."

larecomp_discord_rpc_language.help:
"Rich Presence language. 'auto' follows the game (user_language); or force "
                      "en / pt / es. Discord itself does not translate presence text."

mcla_gpu_ab_interleave.help:
"Diagnostic (M6a): alternate the render thread's code under test between its old "
    "(A) and candidate (B) path every statistics window, and log each window's prepare time "
    "under its variant. Off: the candidate path always runs."

mcla_gpu_ao.help:
"Ambient occlusion: darkens creases, kerbs, the ground under cars and where objects meet, "
    "where nearby objects block sky light. off, high (half resolution, 2 slices), "
    "ultra (full resolution, 3 slices), or rt: ray traced occlusion, from the real geometry of the "
    "city and the cars, so what is off the screen or behind an edge still darkens. Needs a graphics "
    "card that traces rays; on any other it runs as ultra. Auto (the default) is off on integrated "
    "graphics, high on a mid-range card, ultra on a high-end card and ray traced on a high-end card "
    "that traces rays quickly. The pause menu "
    "and the launcher show the same words. A value that is none of these (the low of an older "
    "larecomp.toml) is ignored and the setting runs as auto. "
    "Costs graphics card time, ultra more than high. "
    "Also drawn behind the pause menu and on the map, so a change made there shows at once. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_intensity.help:
"How strong ambient occlusion looks: light, default, strong or max. Each is a set of four "
    "numbers: how strongly it darkens, how far it looks for things that block the sky light, how "
    "hard the measure is pushed, and how much it also darkens the part of a surface the sun lights; "
    "the stronger ones reach farther and make every crease, corner and under-car shadow darker. "
    "Only used while mcla_gpu_ao is not off (the pause menu's AO INTENSITY row). Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_fade_end.help:
"The distance, in the game's world units (about metres), where ambient occlusion has faded "
    "out entirely; it starts to fade at half of it. Fog, rain and particles are not darkened "
    "either way: they are drawn over the picture afterwards. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_car_reach.help:
"Diagnostic: how far what a car blocks of the sky light reaches on the road and the other things "
    "round it, as a share of the occlusion's radius (0.4 of the default 3 m is 1.2 m: the dark line "
    "where the tyres meet the road and the car's footprint, not a halo). The car's own body is "
    "darkened with the whole radius as before. 1 (or 0): a car blocks the sky light as far as a wall "
    "does. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_view.help:
"Diagnostic: shows a stage of the ambient occlusion as a grey picture instead of applying it "
    "(only while it is on): 1 the factor the picture is multiplied by (white: none), 2 the "
    "visibility, 3 the share of the light that is ambient, 4 the surface normals, 5 the distance "
    "(a log scale), 6 how much of the last frames each pixel kept (white: all it can, black: none, "
    "so it is new, a vehicle whose own motion is not known, or has no history yet; the history itself "
    "goes on as usual), 7 the occlusion's own part of the factor (the visibility with the ambient "
    "share, the strength and the distance fade; white: none), 8 the pixels it takes for vehicles "
    "(white). 0: "
    "off. Live."

mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_contact.help:
"Diagnostic (NOISE-NA6): one effect's share of mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_no_upscaler, for the ghost check's arms: the contact shadows' march and the ray traced sun rays of the car and the city (the occlusion's own history over the contact image). "
    "True (the default): it varies its noise every frame and resolves it with its own history, as the master switch says. False: it keeps the first fixes' fixed blue pattern while the others "
    "go on as the master switch says. The master switch off wins (nothing varies). Live."

mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_shafts.help:
"Diagnostic (NOISE-NA6): one effect's share of mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_no_upscaler, for the ghost check's arms: the sun shafts' ray starts (the blurred image's history). "
    "True (the default): it varies its noise every frame and resolves it with its own history, as the master switch says. False: it keeps the first fixes' fixed blue pattern while the others "
    "go on as the master switch says. The master switch off wins (nothing varies). Live."

mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_cone.help:
"Diagnostic (NOISE-NA6): one effect's share of mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_no_upscaler, for the ghost check's arms: the car reflection cone's turn (the denoise's third pass). "
    "True (the default): it varies its noise every frame and resolves it with its own history, as the master switch says. False: it keeps the first fixes' fixed blue pattern while the others "
    "go on as the master switch says. The master switch off wins (nothing varies). Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_history.help:
"Diagnostic: how many frames ambient occlusion averages to take its sampling noise out, 1 to "
    "64. Each frame's occlusion is found again in the next by the camera's motion and kept only "
    "where it is the same surface; more frames is smoother and slower to follow a moving shadow "
    "(a car's), fewer is noisier. 1: no averaging (two blur passes on every frame instead). Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_stable.help:
"Diagnostic: the occlusion's noise stays as small in a big picture as in a small one: its blur reaches "
    "as far in the picture at 4K (7x7 pixels) as it does at 720 lines (3x3), the wide blur of the pixels "
    "that have no history follows, and the noise's shift from frame to frame is a lattice of 13 frames that "
    "any 12 consecutive frames cover evenly. The bounce light's a-trous filter has more iterations in a "
    "bigger picture and its history is clipped to a wider box. False: the first version's 3x3 blur and 5x5 "
    "wide blur at every size, its additive recurrence, its 2 a-trous iterations and its clip of 1.25 "
    "deviations, for comparing. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_blue_noise.help:
"Diagnostic: the ambient occlusion's, the bounce light's and the contact shadows' sampling noise (which direction and how far along it each pixel "
    "looks) comes from a blue noise tile that has no lattice in it, so what the blur and the average over frames leave of the noise is a fine grain no "
    "pattern can be read from. False: the first version's interleaved gradient noise, a diagonal lattice whose leftovers show as thin diagonal lines on "
    "roads and kerbs, for comparing. Live."

mcla_gpu_noise_blue.help:
"Diagnostic: the other stochastic passes' sampling noise (the ray traced car occlusion's and reflection cones' directions, the sun shafts' ray starts, "
    "the fog's sample offsets, the sun shadow filter's disk turn and the city reflections' sun and lamp samples) comes from the blue noise tile stepped "
    "along the R2 sequence every frame, so what the filters and the average over frames leave of it is a fine grain no pattern can be read from. False: the "
    "first versions' interleaved gradient noise, a lattice whose leftovers show as thin diagonal lines, for comparing. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_rays.help: "Debug: Rays per traced AO pixel. 0 uses the GPU budget. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_reach.help: "Debug: Ray reach in metres. 0 takes the AO intensity radius share. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_range.help: "Debug: Maximum distance to a traced AO receiver in metres. 0 uses the scene's safe range up to 90 m. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_scale.help: "Debug: Traced AO size divisor. 1 renders full size, 2 half size, 4 quarter size, and 0 uses the governor. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_alpha.help: "Debug: How traced AO handles cut-outs. Auto uses exact alpha on strong RT GPUs and stochastic alpha otherwise. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_screen.help: "Debug: Screen-space contribution to traced AO. Auto uses it for fallback, off disables it, and on takes the darker term. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_interior.help: "Debug: Cockpit AO policy. Auto probes the cabin, screen keeps screen-space AO inside it, and rt always traces it. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_check.help: "Debug: Traced AO identity check. 0 draws the result, 1 writes open visibility, and 2 writes fully occluded visibility. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_view.help: "Debug: Traced AO debug image. 0 is the result, 1 raw, 2 filtered, 3 coverage, 4 history length, 5 rays, and 6 vehicle IDs. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_blend_car.help: "Debug: Keep the car pass's occlusion term in a traced AO frame for comparison. 0 combines only its sun term. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights.help:
"Debug (RT-LIGHTS-D1, perf/RT-DIRECT-SURVEY.md): ray traced visibility of the lights the deferred light pass draws, for the top K (a car's headlights, neon, the "
    "nearest street lamps): one ray from every pixel to a point of the light's disc, against the city's structures and the cars, filtered by the renderer's own temporal "
    "and a-trous filter, read by the light pass as a second shadow beside the shadow atlas (the two multiply: neither knows every caster). A street lamp the game lights "
    "is only ever taken away from, never added. off (the default), on (the pass runs, where the graphics card traces rays), auto (follows the RT SHADOWS row's level). "
    "Needs the deferred light pass to run (mcla_gpu_local_lights or the lamp shadows). Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_k.help: "Debug: how many lights get a ray (the top K), 1 to 9; 0 (the default) is the level's (3, and 6 at the largest LIGHT SHADOWS level). A group of three lights is one "\n    "set of images: 1 to 3 lights cost one group, 4 to 6 two, 7 to 9 three. Headlights come first, then neon, then the nearest street lamps. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_radius.help: "Debug: the radius of a light's disc in metres for mcla_gpu_rt_lights (the rays go to points of the disc, so a larger radius softens the edge of the shadow); 0 (the "\n    "default) is by kind of light: a headlight's lens 7 cm, a street lamp's head 25 cm, neon 45 cm. 0 to 2. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_rays.help: "Debug: rays to each light for every pixel the light reaches, for mcla_gpu_rt_lights, 1 to 4 (the strata of the light's disc: more rays, less noise, more cost). Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_view.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_lights, draw the visibility instead of the light: 1 the filtered visibility of each light that has a ray (red where the light is blocked, "\n    "green where it arrives), 2 the raw one (before the filter). 0 is the picture. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_check.help: "Debug: the identity test of mcla_gpu_rt_lights. 1: the pass traces its rays (and costs its time) but writes every visibility as 1, so the picture must be the same, "\n    "bit for bit, as with the pass off; 2: every visibility the light reaches is 0 (the lights with a ray vanish, a street lamp the game lights is taken away in full). 0 "\n    "is the pass. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_scale.help: "Debug: the size the ray traced light visibility is traced at, for mcla_gpu_rt_lights. 0 (the default): half of the occlusion's traced size on each axis where that is taller than 720 lines, else the "\n    "whole of it (the memory: 28 bytes a texel, 14 MiB at 1080p and at 4K, 25 MiB at 1440p); 1: always the whole traced size (about 4 times the rays and the memory at 1080p and 4K: the picture to compare with); 2: half wherever the size allows. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_lights_lamp_slot.help: "Debug (A/B, RT-LIGHTS-D1 review S2): which lights get a ray for mcla_gpu_rt_lights. 0 (the default): headlights first, then neon, then the nearest street lamps, so three cars with their headlights on "\n    "(a car's pair is one light) leave no ray for any street lamp. 1: with K of 2 or more and no street lamp among the picked lights, the last channel goes to the strongest street lamp in the light pass's list instead (the headlights and neon above it keep theirs). Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_history.help: "Debug: ray traced ambient occlusion history cap in frames. 1 disables temporal accumulation. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_denoise.help: "Debug: auto and ours use the built-in denoiser. Off sends the raw ray traced ambient occlusion signal to compose. Live."

mcla_gpu_rtao_raw_scale.help: "Debug: ray traced ambient occlusion trace divisor for DLSS Ray Reconstruction raw frames. 2 is half size, 1 is full size. Live."

mcla_gpu_noise_held.help:
"Diagnostic: a scene the harness holds still (the trailer toolkit's stills, scene_at) shows the same game frame number in every frame, so the noise of "
    "every stochastic effect (the occlusion, the sun rays, the reflection cone, the shafts, the shadow filter) stood on one sample for ever and its history "
    "averaged copies of it. True: the noise index also counts the frames the scene's number has been held, so a held scene keeps varying (a picture taken "
    "after the same number of frames is still repeatable). False: the scene's own number alone, for pictures that must match whatever number of frames was "
    "waited. Live."

mcla_gpu_noise_resolve_no_upscaler.help:
"Diagnostic: with no temporal upscaler running (plain MSAA, the default) the contact shadows' march, the ray traced sun rays of the car and the city, "
    "the sun shafts' ray starts and the car reflection cone's turn changed their noise every frame only while an upscaler averaged it; without one they held one pattern. "
    "True: the noise changes every frame here too, and each effect resolves it itself: the contact shadows and the sun rays through the occlusion's own history (reprojected by depth and the "
    "camera, 12 frames), the shafts and the reflection cone through a short history of their own. False: the first fixes' fixed blue pattern without an upscaler. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_fast_math.help:
"Diagnostic: the bounce light's sectors take the angle of each sample's horizon from a polynomial (Abramowitz and "
    "Stegun's, 6.8e-5 radians at the most, 0.0014 of one of the 32 sectors) in place of the hardware's acos, which "
    "costs less; every other saving of the occlusion's and the bounce light's shader passes is the same maths to a "
    "rounding error and has no switch. False: the hardware's acos (the shader as it was in that one respect), for "
    "comparing the cost and the picture. Live; the first frame after the change makes the other pipeline on the "
    "render thread (a debug switch: a hitch of tens of milliseconds, once)."

mcla_gpu_ao_gbuffer_normals.help:
"Diagnostic (G-buffer, GB-E; off by default since 2026-11-20: the G-buffer costs 0.04 to 0.2 ms of the graphics card for a small change to these passes, so it stays off until a feature that needs it lands): the ambient occlusion, the contact shadows and the bounce light take each pixel's surface normal from the G-buffer (the "
    "world normal of the surfaces whose shader has the G-buffer variant, turned into view space) in place of working it out from the depth's neighbours in "
    "every pass: no depth edge bends it, the passes read one image that a normal pass makes once a frame, and the bounce light's facing test reads the "
    "sample's normal instead of a second depth. A pixel the G-buffer holds no data for (impostors, billboards, the shaders no family covers yet) takes the "
    "depth's normal as before, and so does a frame without the plane (the pause menu's world, the garage, the map, a cutscene). While it is on and one of "
    "those effects is, the effects ask the G-buffer for its normal plane, so the main view's draws also write it (a small cost, paid only then). False: no "
    "plane is asked for and every pass works out the normal from the depth, the picture as it was (the A/B). Live; the first frame after the change makes "
    "the normal pass's pipeline in the background."

mcla_gpu_ao_half_above_1080.help:
"Diagnostic: above 1080 lines of render height (1440p, 4K, an upscaler's larger render size) the ambient "
    "occlusion's passes (depth chain, visibility, blur, history) run at half the picture's size, 720 lines for 1440p "
    "and 1080 for 4K, and the apply pass's depth-aware upsample puts the result back; 1080 lines and below are as "
    "they were. The occlusion's own 18 samples a pixel make a signal that has no more detail than that, so the picture "
    "is the same to within a thin edge and the passes cost a quarter. The contact shadows keep the picture's size "
    "(their own depth and images). False: every size at the size the quality says (the render size on ultra). With "
    "the bounce light on, mcla_gpu_ssgi_half decides instead (the bounce light's images give the visibility too). "
    "Live; the first frame after the change makes the images again."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_half.help:
"Diagnostic: above 1080 lines of render height the bounce light (every quality, high and ultra) runs at half the "
    "picture's size, like mcla_gpu_ao_half_above_1080 does the occlusion, and its colour chain takes one of the "
    "colour target's MSAA samples a pixel (the four pixels of a 2x2 block give the texel) instead of all of them: the "
    "bounce light is the lowest frequency signal of the picture (it gathers 5 to 16 metres and is filtered over up to "
    "30 pixels), so the picture is the same to within a thin edge and its passes cost a quarter and the images a "
    "quarter of the memory. 1080 lines and below are as they were. False: the sizes and the chain as before "
    "(mcla_gpu_ssgi_low says the old half size choice). Live; the first frame after the change makes the images again."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_lights.help:
"Diagnostic: the bounce light also takes the light the deferred light pass added in the last frame (neon, headlights, street lamps) as part of the "
    "radiance it gathers, reprojected into this frame with the camera's motion and the depth history, so a wall beside a neon car picks up its colour and a "
    "garage's wall lit by the headlights lights the floor. It needs the bounce light (mcla_gpu_ssgi) on and the extracted screen products "
    "(mcla_gpu_screen_extract). False: the colour chain as it was before, which sees the colour before the light pass only (the A/B). Costs two captures of "
    "the main colour at the bounce light's size (the colour before and after the light pass, only in a frame whose light pass ran) and a few more reads in "
    "the colour chain. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_lights_gain.help:
"Diagnostic: how much of the last frame's light (mcla_gpu_ssgi_lights) the bounce light takes as radiance, 0 to 8: 1 the light as it was lit, 0 none "
    "(the bounce light as it was), 2 twice as much. It is held under the same cap as every radiance the bounce takes (mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_clamp), so a "
    "larger gain mostly makes a dim lamp's light count as much as a bright one's. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_lights_floor.help: "Diagnostic: the room the bounce light's lights' share (mcla_gpu_ssgi_lights) has under the cap, as a luma floor in the scene colour's units (a white wall in full sun is about 1.3). At night the radiance cap is its own floor of 0.5, which cut a neon pool or a headlight's wall to a third of a sun-lit white wall before the bounce took it: the lights' share is now held under the larger of that cap and this floor, and by day, where the cap is over it, nothing changes to the bit. 0 is the cap alone (the A/B), the default 1.3 is one white wall in full sun, 4 the most. The colour chain's own cap, the source start and the apply's ceiling keep their floor. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows.help:
"Contact shadows: the short sun shadows the game does not draw (under a car's sills, at the foot "
    "of a kerb or a wall, under props on the pavement), found from the picture's depth and put only "
    "on the sun's light, so they never darken what the game's own shadows already cover. Early in the "
    "morning and in the evening, when the game draws no sun shadows at all, they are the only ones. "
    "They are left out at night and in rain. off, high (8 steps), ultra (16 steps) or auto (the "
    "default): off on an integrated graphics card, high on a discrete one with less than 5.5 GiB of "
    "video memory, ultra on the rest. The pause menu and the launcher show the same words. A value "
    "that is none of these (the low of an older larecomp.toml) is ignored and the setting runs as "
    "auto. They are worked out at the size the game is drawn at, so a "
    "higher render scale gives sharper shadows (only high, with the ambient occlusion not on ultra, "
    "works at half that size). Costs graphics card time, ultra more than high. Also drawn behind the "
    "pause menu and on the map. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_length.help:
"Diagnostic: how far toward the sun contact shadows look, in the game's world units (about "
    "metres), with the sun high. The length grows with a low sun (0.7 / tan of its elevation, 1 to 3 "
    "times). Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_strength.help:
"Diagnostic: how strongly contact shadows darken the sun's light where they apply, 0 to 2 "
    "(the sun's elevation and the wetness scale it further). Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_thickness.help:
"Diagnostic: how far in front of a step of the ray a surface may be and still hide it, in the "
    "game's world units: a thing nearer to the camera than that only overlaps on screen and hides "
    "nothing. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_vehicles.help:
"Diagnostic: how strongly contact shadows darken the ground under a car, 0 to 1. The game's sun "
    "shadow map holds only the player's car, so the ground under a traffic car is as lit as an open "
    "road; a ground pixel with a car's body above it and in the way of the sun (found from the "
    "picture's depth and the cars' pixels, seen through the gap under the car) gets the full contact "
    "shadow, as the player's car gets its sun shadow from the game. Cars the game's sun shadow map "
    "holds (the player's, and traffic with TRAFFIC SHADOWS) are left out. 0 is the contact shadows as "
    "they were (only a strip along the car's edges and its wheels). Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_fade.help:
"Diagnostic: how much of the contact shadows' ray a shadow stays fully dark over, 0.2 to 0.98: "
    "past that share of the ray's length it fades out, so that a shadow cut off by the ray's end "
    "does not end in a hard line. At 0.2 it looks like the first version's fade (a quarter of the "
    "shadow gone half way along the ray). Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_fast.help:
"Diagnostic: the cheaper contact shadows, to compare against the plain ones (false: the passes as "
    "they were). The march takes fewer steps where its ray covers few pixels on the screen (far "
    "pixels, a smaller picture; the squared spacing is kept), and the 3x3 filter that keeps shadow "
    "edges is done inside the apply pass, which saves a pass and a full size image write (only where "
    "the contact passes run at the picture's size: ultra, or the occlusion on ultra). With that, and in a "
    "frame that has the game's sun shadow mask, the march is also left out where the game's own shadow "
    "covers a pixel and its neighbours (the apply cannot use the result there: exactly the same picture). "
    "The picture is the same to within a shadow edge moving by a pixel. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_skip_stat.help:
"Diagnostic: with mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_fast and the game's sun shadow mask in the frame, every N frames (0: never) the contact march's "
    "skip is counted: a second march pass classifies every pixel (skipped under the game's own shadow, the sky or past the fade, turned from "
    "the sun, marching) with the mask's stored value at its centre, and the log gets the shares, the spread of those values (does the "
    "game's shade store exactly 0, which the skip needs?) and the model's march time for that share. That frame costs one more march and a "
    "readback of the picture. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_mask_gain.help:
"Diagnostic: what the game's sun shadow mask's stored value is multiplied by to give the sun's "
    "visibility (1 lit): the game's collector stores half of it and the lit shaders multiply by 2. "
    "Look at mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_view 3 (white where lit) if shadows are darkened twice or not "
    "at all. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_view.help:
"Diagnostic: shows a stage of the contact shadows as a grey picture instead of applying them "
    "(only while they are on, and instead of mcla_gpu_ao_view): 1 the factor the picture is "
    "multiplied by (white: none), 2 the contact visibility (black where the ray is hidden), 3 the "
    "sun's visibility (the game's shadow mask: white lit; white everywhere where the frame has none), "
    "4 the sun's share of the light, 5 the player's car's own sun shadow map's term alone (white; black where "
    "the map shadows the pixel: the wing, the mirrors, the sills and the wheels on the car and on the road "
    "near it; white everywhere in a frame without the map: car_shadow_map.h), 6 the sun's visibility the share "
    "of the light took (the game's mask on the world, the game's car sun image on a car, 1 on a car in a frame "
    "without that image), 7 the ray traced sun ray's term alone (white; black where the ray from the pixel toward the sun "
    "meets the player's car: its own parts on it, and its shadow on the road; white everywhere in a frame without it: "
    "car_rt_ao.h). 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_cabin_sun_shadow.help: "Diagnostic: cockpit sun shadow. 0 keeps original visibility, 1 exempts the car from its own screen-space blockers, 2 exempts its shadow map, 3 exempts its RT sun ray from its own body and tyres, 4 restores part of the combined sun loss. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_car_map_march.help:
"Diagnostic: with the player's car's own sun shadow map in the frame (car_shadow_map.h), the short march that "
    "the car's own pixels (and any vehicle's) take also runs on the pixels the map covers, and the pixel gets the darker "
    "of the two. False: where the map holds a part of the car at a vehicle's pixel the map is the truth about the car's "
    "own parts (a wing's plate and its posts, a mirror, a sill), which the march only guesses from the picture's depth "
    "(a thin part has no thickness there), so that pixel takes no march steps and its contact shadow is the map's. "
    "For comparing the two on the wing and the mirrors (view 5 shows the map's term). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi.help:
"Bounce light: the light a lit wall or the ground sends back onto the road, the sides of cars and "
    "the walls beside it, found from the picture, so a red wall tints the pavement by it and a street "
    "lamp's pool lights the wall next to it. It takes the place of part of the sky light the ambient "
    "occlusion darkens, so a lit area does not get brighter overall, and a flat surface stays as it "
    "was. Needs ambient occlusion (mcla_gpu_ao) on. off, high (a coarser search: 2 directions and 2 steps "
    "each; half resolution where the occlusion is high too), ultra (3 and 3 at full resolution) or auto (the "
    "default): high on the High class of graphics card (gpu_class.h), off on the others. The pause menu and the "
    "launcher show the same words. A value that is none of these (the low of an older larecomp.toml) is "
    "ignored and the setting runs as auto. Costs graphics card time, "
    "ultra more than high. Also drawn behind the pause menu and in the garage, not on the map. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_intensity.help:
"How strong the bounce light looks: light, default, strong, stronger or strongest. Each is a set of four "
    "numbers: how much of the light the surroundings send back the picture gets, the most it may add to a pixel "
    "(a guard against noise in the dark), how far it looks for lit surfaces (5 to 16 metres, past the ambient "
    "occlusion's own reach), and the brightest light it may bring (never whiter than a white wall in full sun). "
    "The stronger ones lift shadows and the sides of cars more and look farther. Only used while the bounce light "
    "(mcla_gpu_ssgi) is on (the pause menu's BOUNCE LIGHT STRENGTH row). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_strength.help:
"Diagnostic: replaces the level's strength of the bounce light (mcla_gpu_ssgi_intensity), 0 to 12: how much of "
    "the bounce light the picture gets (1: all that the surroundings send back by the picture's own colours; 0 "
    "runs the passes and adds nothing). -1: the level's. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_radius.help:
"Diagnostic: how far the bounce light's NEAR samples look, as a multiple of the ambient occlusion's radius "
    "(mcla_gpu_ao_intensity); the same samples give the occlusion's visibility, so a change moves that too. 1: the "
    "occlusion's own. (The far ring that reaches past them is mcla_gpu_ssgi_reach.) Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_reach.help:
"Diagnostic: replaces the level's reach of the bounce light (mcla_gpu_ssgi_intensity), 0 to 16 metres: a "
    "second ring of samples from the occlusion's radius out to this, into what the near samples left open (the "
    "occlusion's own look does not change). 0: no ring. -1: the level's. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_far_steps.help:
"Diagnostic: the far ring's samples on each side of each direction, 0 to 7 (0: no ring). -1: by the bounce "
    "light's quality (2 at ultra, 1 at high). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_clamp.help:
"Diagnostic: replaces the level's gain limit of the bounce light (mcla_gpu_ssgi_intensity), 0.05 to 10.2: the "
    "most the bounce may add to a pixel, as a multiple of that pixel's own colour (its largest channel; the hue "
    "stays; a soft limit that only guards a nearly black pixel's noise, so a shadow can gain several times "
    "its own light). The brightest the bounce can make a pixel is set by the cap, not by this. -1: the "
    "level's. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_low.help:
"Diagnostic: what the bounce light's high does (mcla_gpu_ssgi high or auto that comes to high) to be cheaper "
    "than ultra: 0 fewer directions (2 slices and 2 steps each instead of 3 and 3) at the occlusion's own "
    "size, 1 half the picture's size (the occlusion's slices and steps) even where the occlusion is high, 2 "
    "both. The same samples give the occlusion's visibility, so 1 and 2 also make the occlusion's own "
    "picture half resolution while the bounce light is on. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_view.help:
"Diagnostic: shows a stage of the bounce light's apply as a picture instead of applying it (only "
    "while the bounce light is on, and instead of the occlusion's and the contact shadows' views; the "
    "test's own views come first): 1 the factor the picture is multiplied by, in colour (the "
    "occlusion's plus the bounce), 2 the bounce each pixel gets (four times as bright as the others), "
    "3 the albedo estimate (the colour over the light the game's constants say fell on it, up to 1), "
    "4 that light, 5 how much of the colour is a surface (black: a source of light, which gets no "
    "bounce), 6 the change of the picture against the game's own (grey: none; lighter: brighter; "
    "darker). Shown at 0.3 of the value, except 6. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test.help:
"Diagnostic: the debug override of the bounce light (mcla_gpu_ssgi): forces its passes on, at the "
    "occlusion's own quality and whatever mcla_gpu_ssgi says (only while mcla_gpu_ao is not off). The "
    "scene colour at the occlusion's trigger is kept in a chain of images and the occlusion's main "
    "pass becomes a visibility bitmask that also finds what colour the blockers of each pixel's sky "
    "light are, then accumulated over frames and filtered. The occlusion's own look stays (its "
    "visibility now comes from the bitmask); the bounce is added to the picture as the setting adds it "
    "(mcla_gpu_ssgi_strength 0: not added), or shown by mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_view. Costs about as much "
    "as the occlusion again. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_thickness.help:
"Diagnostic: how thick the surfaces the bitmask finds are assumed to be, in the game's world units "
    "(about metres): a sample blocks the directions between its front and its back, the back being "
    "this far behind the front along the view ray. 0: solid, a sample blocks everything below its "
    "horizon (the occlusion's own horizon search, to within 1/32). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_clamp.help:
"Diagnostic: replaces the level's cap (mcla_gpu_ssgi_intensity), 0.25 to 15.75: the brightest radiance a "
    "sample of the scene colour may carry into the bounce, and the ceiling the bounce may fill a pixel up to, as a "
    "multiple of the frame's ambient plus sun light (never under 0.5): a street lamp, neon or the sun's disc is a "
    "source, not a surface that bounces light, and may light its neighbours no whiter than a white wall in full "
    "sun. -1: the level's. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_facing.help:
"Diagnostic: how much a sample's surface must face the pixel to light it, 0 to 1: 0 takes every "
    "surface to face the pixel, 1 weighs each by the slope of its depth along the slice (a roof seen "
    "from the ground, a wall seen from behind: nothing). Costs one more depth read per lit sector. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_view.help:
"Diagnostic: shows a stage of the bounce light test as a picture instead of the scene colour "
    "(only while mcla_gpu_ssgi_test is on, and instead of the other debug views): 1 the bounce light "
    "the main pass found (one frame, noisy), 2 the scene colour chain's level 0 (the colour the "
    "blockers are taken from: averaged over the samples, capped), 3 its level 1, 4 its level 2, 5 the "
    "bounce light cleaned by a 5x5 mean, 6 the visibility the bitmask found (one frame, noisy: the "
    "occlusion's own view 2 shows it after the denoise and the history), 7 the bounce light after the "
    "accumulation over frames (the history), 8 the bounce light after the a-trous filter too (what the "
    "picture's bounce will be made of), 9 how much of the history each pixel kept (white: all it can, "
    "black: none, so it is new, a vehicle whose own motion is not known, or has no history yet). Shown at "
    "0.3 of its value times mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_view_gain (view 9 at full white). 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_view_gain.help: "Diagnostic: the brightness of mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_view's picture, 0.1 to 16 times. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_history.help:
"Diagnostic: how many frames the bounce light test averages the bounce over, 2 to 64 (the "
    "occlusion's own visibility keeps mcla_gpu_ao_history). The bounce is found again in the last frame "
    "by the camera's and the vehicles' motion and kept only where it is the same surface; more frames is "
    "smoother and slower to follow a light that changed, fewer is noisier. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_history_clamp.help:
"Diagnostic: how far the bounce's history may be from this frame's 3x3 neighbourhood of the bounce, in "
    "standard deviations of that neighbourhood (never under 5% of its mean, and 15% of the history's own value "
    "wider on each side): the history is cut to that box. Narrow follows a changed light at once and keeps more "
    "noise (the first version, 1.25 with no share of the history, made the accumulated bounce 2.5 to 3.5 times as "
    "noisy); wide keeps the history longer and leaves a ghost of a car that went by. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssgi_test_atrous.help:
"Diagnostic: the iterations of the a-trous filter that takes the noise out of the bounce light after the "
    "history, for a picture of 720 lines, 0 to 3 (0: none; each iteration reaches twice as far: 5x5, 9x9, 17x17 "
    "pixels, and stops at depth edges and corners). A bigger picture gets one more for each doubling of its "
    "height (3 at 1080 and 1440 lines, 4 at 2160, at most 5), so the filter reaches as much of the picture; "
    "mcla_gpu_ao_stable false keeps this number at every size. The history itself is never filtered. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_census.help:
"Diagnostic: every Nth guest frame (and the first three frames with the main view), one block "
    "of log lines with the main view's draws around the game's mid-scene depth resolve, that "
    "resolve (where it is, how big, inside EndTiling or not), the light constants the occlusion "
    "uses (PS c26 ambient, PS c39 sun colour, VS c16 sun direction), the depth clear value, the "
    "lens the game's motion blur draw gives, what the history did and a statistic of the linear "
    "depth (read back from the graphics card, so the first three frames and every Nth one run the "
    "depth passes even with the occlusion off). Frames where the main view does not have exactly "
    "one qualifying resolve are logged as they come (the first 40). 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_paint.help:
"Diagnostic: how much of ambient occlusion a car's glossy paint takes. The colour of dark paint is nearly all the "
    "reflection of the sky, and a reflection is blocked only where the mirror ray is, not by the share of the sky a part "
    "cannot see, so a part that is partly covered (the uprights of a wing and the lid under it) lost most of its colour. On "
    "a car's pixels the occlusion's value (the image's, already raised to the look's power) is raised to this power: 1 "
    "darkens the paint like the world, smaller keeps more of its colour. The default, 0.3125, takes the default look's power "
    "(3.6) out again, so the paint is darkened by the share of the sky a part can see. Rounded to sixteenths, 1/16 to 1. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_gpu_based_validation.help:
"With mcla_gpu_debug_layer on D3D12, enable GPU-based validation before device creation. "
    "Diagnostic; requires the matching D3D12SDKLayers.dll and a restart."

mcla_gpu_car_dump.help:
"Debug: takes the triangles of every car the game draws in ONE frame out of the game's memory, puts them in world space with "
    "each draw's own matrices and writes them to car_dump_<frame>.obj next to the executable (one group per draw, for the car "
    "chosen by mcla_gpu_car_dump_id), with a census of the car draws (how many draws, vertices and triangles each car has and "
    "which shaders draw it) in the log under [car dump]. 0 (the default) is off. A number N dumps the first frame at or after the "
    "game's frame N that has a car in it. With the car self-reflections on (mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_test=1) it also checks the "
    "triangles against the picture of the cars the self-reflections keep, and logs how much of the car they cover and how close "
    "their distances are. Park the car, switch the upscaler off and use the game's own view (not the garage or the pause menu). A "
    "new value dumps again. It costs nothing while it is off and one slow frame when it dumps."

mcla_gpu_car_dump_id.help:
"Debug: which car mcla_gpu_car_dump writes to its OBJ file and checks first, by the number the game stamps into the stencil "
    "for it (1 to 23, handed out in drawing order each frame, so a car has no fixed number). 0 (the default) takes the player's "
    "car: the one nearest to the vehicle the player drives in the game's memory, else the one with paint draws nearest to the "
    "camera, else the one with the most body draws; the log says which. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_frame_log.help:
"Debug: logs one line under [car frame] whenever the player's car changes in the draw list the car effects share (its "
    "stencil ID, how many draws it has, how many are rigid parts and how many skinned): what was found, how it was found and what "
    "was left out. With this on the list is collected in every frame, whether a car effect (the car shadow map, the car ray tracing) "
    "asks for it or not, so the line shows by itself. A second line, 'keys', says when the car's meshes get new keys (a new key is a "
    "mesh the car effects read or build again): a few seconds after the car appears there should be none in a parked car; at most one "
    "line every few seconds. Never saved. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt.help:
"Ray traced car self-reflections: where the graphics card can ray trace (Direct3D 12 with ray tracing 1.1, Vulkan with ray queries), your car's reflection of "
    "its own body comes from its real shape, not from the picture of the car on the screen: a part the camera cannot see (the back of the "
    "wing, a mirror's far side) shows in the paint as it does in a mirror, and thin parts are exact. auto (the default) is on there while the "
    "car self-reflections are on; off keeps the screen-space version everywhere. A graphics card that cannot ray trace uses the "
    "screen-space version whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_mirror_rt.help:
"Ray traced side mirrors: where the graphics card can ray trace (Direct3D 12 with ray tracing 1.1, Vulkan with ray queries), the two side mirrors of your car show the real view behind - the cars beside "
    "you, your own flank and the sky and street the game's environment map holds - instead of the game's blurred sky, mostly in the first person cameras (cockpit, bumper), where "
    "the glass is big enough to read. auto (the default) is on on a strong graphics card; on switches it on on any card that can ray trace except a slow one that shares memory with the processor (it builds your car's ray tracing structures "
    "in every frame); off keeps the game's mirrors. A graphics card that cannot ray trace keeps the game's mirrors whatever this says. The pause menu's row is GRAPHICS, REFLECTIONS, RT SIDE MIRRORS. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_mirror_rt_pixels.help:
"Debug: the most pixels one side mirror's rectangle on the screen may cover for the ray traced side mirrors (mcla_gpu_car_mirror_rt), in thousands (0, the default: the graphics card's "
    "class decides: 160 on the High class, 64 on the Mid class). A mirror over it is left to the game. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_mirror_rt_strength.help: "Debug: the share of the game's own mirror glass the ray traced side mirrors replace (0.92, the default; 1 is all of it, 0 nothing). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_mirror_rt_world.help:
"Debug: what the ray traced side mirrors (mcla_gpu_car_mirror_rt) show where their ray finds none of the cars: auto (the default) is the city behind your car - the street, the buildings, the lamps, "
    "shaded like the city in the car's paint reflections - where RT CITY REFLECTIONS is on (its auto is on a graphics card that traces quickly) and the game's environment map where it is off; env is the environment map only "
    "(the mirrors as they were); city is the city on any card that can ray trace, whatever RT CITY REFLECTIONS says (a weaker card gets the smaller reach). The mirrors show the environment map until the city's data is ready, and "
    "a mirror of a few pixels (a chase camera) always shows it. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt_length.help:
"Diagnostic: how far the ray traced car self-reflection's ray reaches, in the game's world units (about metres); what it finds weighs "
    "less from 0.6 of it and nothing at it. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt_gloss.help:
"Diagnostic: the half angle, in degrees, of the cone the ray traced car self-reflection casts its rays over: the paint's gloss. A part of "
    "your car reflected in another has an edge as soft as the cone is wide at its distance (2.5 degrees: about a hand's width at 1 m); 0 is a perfect "
    "mirror (one ray, a razor edge). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt_denoise.help:
"Diagnostic: the passes of the filter that takes the grain out of the soft edge of a part of your car reflected in another (the ray traced car "
    "self-reflection) before the paint reads it: 2 (the default) two passes, 1 one pass, 0 none (the raw trace, to compare with). Each pass is "
    "applied only where the soft edge is wide enough to have grain, so a sharp edge stays sharp; there is none for a gloss of 0. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt_parts.help:
"Diagnostic: the parts the ray traced self-reflection's ray can hit, a sum of: 1 your car's body, 2 its glass, 4 its tyres, 8 its "
    "driver, 16 the other cars beside it (opponents, traffic, parked cars; mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars says how many are in the scene). 23 (the "
    "default): the body, the glass, the tyres and the other cars. 7 is your car alone. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_check.help:
"Debug: proves the player's car as ray tracing structures (car_rt_scene.h) on a graphics card that has them (Direct3D 12 with "
    "DirectX Raytracing 1.1, Vulkan with ray queries). After the ambient occlusion's passes one ray is traced from the camera through every vehicle pixel of its "
    "linear depth image and the hit's distance is compared with the pixel's; the log says every 120 frames, under [car rt], how many "
    "vehicle pixels the structures cover and how far the distances are apart. Only the pixels the scene is meant to hold are traced: "
    "the player's car and the other cars the frame kept (mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars); the pixels of other cars are counted apart as not in "
    "the scene by design (the driver is in the player's count and shows as a miss). It "
    "needs the ambient occlusion on, and it asks for the car's meshes to be built. Costs a ray a vehicle pixel; never saved. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_view.help:
"Debug: shows the car ray tracing check's picture over the scene (only while mcla_gpu_car_rt_check is on): 1 the error of each "
    "vehicle pixel's hit (green below 2%, yellow at 2%, red from 10%, magenta: nothing hit, grey-blue: a car outside the scene by design), "
    "2 the hit's normal as colour (x right, y up, z forward, times 0.5 plus 0.5), 3 another car's paint as the reflection pass reads it from the instance table (the "
    "hue of the car's paint row on its pixels; purple: the car has no paint row). With the check on the log also says whether the shader read the paint rows the host wrote "
    "(\"paint probe\"). 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_shadows.help:
"Ray traced sun shadows from the city's own triangles (the city pack, built from your game files by the launcher's setup or, "
    "if it is missing, by the game in the background). Rays go from every pixel toward the sun, spread over the sun's disc, through the city's buildings and the cars: a shadow is sharp "
    "where it touches what casts it and softer the farther it falls, and there are no cascade seams. They are added to the game's shadows through the contact shadows "
    "(mcla_gpu_contact_shadows must be on), within about 300 m, and darken only where the game's own shadow mask says the sun reaches. off, high, ultra or auto (the default): high on a "
    "discrete graphics card with 5.5 GiB of video memory or more that can ray trace, off on the rest. high keeps the buildings within 300 m (150 m on a card set to high by hand "
    "with less memory) in ray tracing structures and casts 2 rays a pixel; ultra 600 m and 4 rays. Needs a graphics card with ray queries (Direct3D 12 with DirectX Raytracing 1.1, "
    "or Vulkan with ray queries) and the city pack; without them the game's shadows stand. The pause menu's RT SHADOWS row (GRAPHICS > LIGHTING AND SHADOWS). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_sun.help:
"Debug: the size of the sun's disc for the ray traced city shadows, as a multiple of the real sun (0.53 degrees across), 0.25 to "
    "16. The real sun makes a penumbra 6 cm wide for a caster 10 m away; the few rays of a pixel and the filter turn that into noise farther off, so the default is 3. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_rays.help: "Debug: rays a pixel for the ray traced city shadows, 1 to 8; 0 (the default) is the level's (high 2, ultra 4). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_alpha.help:
"Debug: what the ray traced city shadows do with the city's cut-out triangles (fences, grates, neon cut-outs: "
    "4% of the city, kept apart in the city pack). exact (the default) reads the cut-out texture's alpha where the ray meets the triangle, from the city hit data and the "
    "city textures, and blocks the ray where it reaches mcla_gpu_city_rt_alpha_ref; where those are not built or the texture is not loaded yet it does what stochastic does. "
    "exclude leaves the cut-outs out, opaque makes them solid, stochastic makes half of the rays that meet one a blocker, chosen by a hash, which the filter and the "
    "upscaler average into a half tone. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_alpha_ref.help:
"Debug: the alpha at or above which a cut-out texel blocks a ray in the exact mode of mcla_gpu_city_rt_alpha, 0.02 to 0.98 "
    "(the game's alpha test keeps a texel above its reference, mostly 0.5 for the city's cut-outs; the city pack does not know a draw's own). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_alpha_view.help:
"Debug: with the exact mode of mcla_gpu_city_rt_alpha, shows through the contact shadows' view 7 "
    "(mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_view) which way each pixel's sun rays went through the cut-outs: white no cut-out met, 0.7 decided by the texture's alpha, 0.35 decided by the "
    "stochastic rule (no hit data, or the texture not loaded yet); the log says every 120 frames how many candidates were decided each way, how many blocked, and the "
    "levels read. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_radius.help:
"Debug: how far from the camera the city's sectors are kept at full detail in ray tracing structures, in metres, 25 to 1500; 0 "
    "(the default) is the level's and the class's (150 m on a smaller card, 300 m, 600 m at ultra). The far level of detail reaches at least four times as far. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_range.help:
"Debug: the farthest from the camera that ray traced city shadows are applied to, in metres, up to 1000; 0 (the default) is as far "
    "as the structures are the full detail the game drew there (never more than 700 m). A smaller number shows where the game's own shadows stand. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_check.help:
"Debug: proves the city's ray tracing structures on a graphics card that has them. Instead of the sun's rays, one ray is "
    "traced from the camera through every city pixel of the occlusion's linear depth image and the hit's distance is compared with the pixel's; the log says every 120 "
    "frames, under [city rt shadow], how many pixels hit, how many are within 1% and 5% of the depth, and the error's median and 95th percentile. Needs "
    "mcla_gpu_rt_shadows on and the contact shadows on. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_rt_view.help:
"Debug: with mcla_gpu_city_rt_check on, shows the check's picture through the contact shadows' view 7 "
    "(mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_view): white within 1% of the depth image's distance, grey within 5%, black otherwise (a miss or a wrong distance). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_hit_data.help: "Debug: asks for the city's hit data (the texture coordinates, vertex colours and materials of the city, in the GPU pool the structures are built over: mcla_city_hit.v1.pack beside the city pack) without any effect reading it, to test the pool: off (the default), high or ultra, which also brings the city's structures at that level (and, with no car in the picture, the city alone in the top level). The log says under [city hit] and [rt scene]. A hit file that is missing or stale leaves it off. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_hit_textures.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_city_hit_data on, asks for the city's textures to be resident as well, to test the loader without an effect reading them: off (the default), alpha (the cut-outs' textures of the sectors in the ring, what the ray traced shadows' exact alpha reads) or all (every texture of the sectors in the ring, what the reflections will read). The file is mcla_city_tex.v1.pack beside the hit file. The log says under [city tex] (the first texture, the video memory's pressure) and the city ray tracing census line has the textures' slots and accounted memory. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_hit_probe.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_city_hit_data on, a compute pass reads the city hit data's pool and tables through the ray tracing descriptor set every frame, the way the hit shading will, and every 240 frames the log says under [city hit] whether what it read is what was copied (a checksum of every block, the sector table's rows, the first material and texture rows). The proof of the pool's offsets and bindings on this backend. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_reflections.help: "Ray traced reflections of the real city in the car paint: the player's car, and the cars beside it, reflect the buildings, signs, lamp posts and lamp heads around them as the ray tracing finds them (where a reflected point is in the picture it takes the picture's own colour, elsewhere it is shaded from the building's own materials), instead of the game's blurred environment map; the sky stays the map. off, high, ultra or auto (the default): high on a strong ray tracing graphics card, off on the rest; a weak card may be set to high or ultra by hand and then runs lighter numbers. high reaches 150 m, ultra 1,000 m. Rides on the ray traced car self-reflections (mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl with mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt: the row is grey until that one is on RAY TRACED), needs ray queries and needs the city pack and the city hit data, which the launcher's setup builds from your game files (the game builds them in the background if they are not there, and the row says BUILDING DATA until they are done); without them the paint keeps the game's reflection. The pause menu's RT CITY REFLECTIONS row (GRAPHICS > REFLECTIONS). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_screen.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, a reflected point that is in the picture takes the picture's own colour (the game's lighting, foliage and lamps as drawn). false: every reflected point is shaded from the city's own materials, for comparing. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_coat.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, a reflection of the city is a mirror's, as a reflection of another car is: sharp, with the paint's clear coat layer over it, so that what is in it can be told at a glance. false: the paint's soft cone alone. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_reach.help: "Debug: how far a reflection ray looks for the city, in metres, 5 to 3000; 0 (the default) is the level's (high 150 m, ultra 1,000 m, a weak card 60 and 150). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_view.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, replaces the colour a city hit shows in the car paint's ray traced image (look at it through mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_view 2): 1 where the colour comes from (green the picture's own, red shaded, yellow both), 2 the kind of surface it hit (a ramp over the G-buffer's classes); 0 (the default) the colour. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_chrome.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, the player's chrome (the tailpipes, the badges, the trim) reflects the city and the cars beside it from the ray traced image, as the paint does, instead of only being darkened where the car's own parts cover it. false: the chrome as before. Live (the chrome's shader changes at the next draw)."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_glass.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, the player's car windows reflect the city and the cars beside it: a ray traced pass adds the mirror reflection over the glass by its Fresnel (more at a grazing view), on top of the game's own. false: the glass as before. Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_lamps.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, a point of the city that a reflection ray hit (in the car paint, the chrome, the other cars' paint and the glass) is lit by the street lamps and the fill lights around it, and lamp lenses, signs and lit windows glow by the world's lamp schedule (the ray tracing world frame's lamp grid, 96 lamps and a cap on their light), so a night street reflects lit lamps, signs and windows. false: the reflections as before (no lamp light on a hit, the glow by the sun's height). Live."

mcla_gpu_city_refl_world_light.help: "Debug: with mcla_gpu_rt_reflections on, a point of the city that a reflection ray hit (in the car paint, the chrome, the other cars' paint and the glass) is lit by the world's light: the sun's direction and colour, the ambient, the sky and the environment map of the street the picture shows (the ray tracing world frame's), not by the constants of the car's own draws, whose sun is a rig of its own. false: the car's draws' light, as before. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_masks.help:
"Debug: how the car's parts are told apart in the top level: 0 the tyres by their shader and glass by being drawn after the world's "
    "first draw (only in a frame where some of the car's draws are and some are not: where all are, nothing is glass), 1 every part "
    "that is no tyre is a body. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl.help:
"Car self-reflections: your car's paint reflects its own body, which the game's paint does not: the wing shows in the "
    "trunk lid and the mirror in the door, and the reflection is darker where the body shades it, under a spoiler or "
    "in a wheel arch, and it also shows the car's own colour in the reflection. on is the one level; off leaves the game's "
    "paint as it is. auto (the default) is on for a discrete graphics card and off for an integrated one (a handheld, or the "
    "iGPU of a desktop CPU). Costs the graphics card a little while it is on (about 0.1 ms a frame at 4K on an RTX 5080). "
    "It works in the game, behind the pause menu and in the garage, not on the map. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_test.help:
"Diagnostic: forces the car self-reflections (mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl) to a level whatever the setting says, for a test "
    "or a comparison. 0: follow the setting (the default). 1: the specular occlusion alone, the reflection is darkened where "
    "a short ray along it passes just behind a part of the car (the setting has no such level: it costs the same as 2). "
    "2: the full effect, the same, and the car's own colour of the previous frame is reflected there (what the setting on does). "
    "Needs the shader pack's "
    "car_selfrefl variant and the motion blur draw's camera. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_view.help:
"Diagnostic: shows a stage of the car self-reflection instead of the paint (only while the car self-reflections are on): "
    "1 the weight of the hit, 2 the colour the ray found, 3 the paint's baked vertex occlusion, 4 the state of the trace "
    "(red: the point is not found in the previous frame, blue: the ray left the picture, green: no hit, yellow: a hit, "
    "orange where the march's hit is probably the hidden face of a part, the brighter the more of the reflection it takes), 5 the "
    "ray traced image at the paint's pixel (purple: no image this frame, cyan: no data there, so the march ran, green: no hit, "
    "yellow: a hit on the player's own part, orange: on another car), 6 the clear coat's layer's amount (its fresnel by the share of the hit on another car, white is 1), "
    "7 what that layer adds (the other car's colour by the amount). 2 is the ray traced reflection alone at full intensity. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_length.help: "Diagnostic: how far the car self-reflection's ray goes, in the game's world units (about metres). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_thickness.help:
"Diagnostic: how far behind a part of the car's surface (as the previous frame saw it) a ray point still hits it, "
    "in the game's world units; the weight of a point is full up to half of it and falls to nothing at it. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_strength.help: "Diagnostic: the most of the reflection the car self-reflection takes over, 0 to 1. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_source.help:
"Diagnostic (car self-reflections, shared screen products): where the history pass takes the scene colour from. 0: the shared colour_post where the "
    "frame has it at the picture's size (another effect wanted it), else the main colour target's own planes. 1: always the main colour target's planes "
    "(the old path). 2: as 0, and the car self-reflection asks for the shared colour_post itself, so that the same pictures can be compared with 1 without "
    "a reflections effect (the bytes of the history image are the same). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_steps.help:
"Diagnostic: the points on the car self-reflection's ray, 4 to 24 (the cost is one texture read each, and three more for "
    "each segment between two points that holds the outline of a part; they are closer together near the car's surface, and "
    "the step the weight makes at a part's outline is a point's share of the whole hit). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_full.help:
"Diagnostic: the share of the car self-reflection ray's points that, all inside a part of the car, take the whole hit "
    "(0.25: 3 of the 12). A smaller one makes every hit heavier and the outline of a part a steeper step, a larger one lighter and "
    "softer. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_gain.help:
"Diagnostic: a multiplier on the brightness of the car's own colour in its reflection (1: the target's exponent bias "
    "taken out, which is the paint's own units; unverified: raise it if the reflection of the car looks too dark). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_history.help:
"Diagnostic: the size of the car self-reflection's history image: 0 the rule (half of the render size for the occlusion-only "
    "test level and from 2560 pixels across, the full size otherwise), 1 the full render size, 2 half of it in each direction (a quarter "
    "of the memory and of the pass's work). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_shadow_map.help:
"Car shadow map: your car casts a shadow of its real shape on itself and on the road beside it. The game's own sun shadows "
    "draw the car in a rough low-detail form into maps whose texels are 1 to 25 cm, so the wing, the mirrors, the sills and the "
    "wheels cast no shadow of their own; this draws the car again from the sun, at full detail, into a small map fitted to it "
    "(2048 by 2048 on ultra, 1024 by 1024 on high), and the contact shadows read it. It only runs while the contact shadows "
    "(mcla_gpu_contact_shadows) are on, in the game view, in daylight. off, high, ultra or auto (the default): ultra on a discrete "
    "graphics card, high on an integrated one. Costs a little graphics card time (the car's triangles drawn once more, depth only) "
    "and 8 or 32 MiB of video memory. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_shadow_map_owns.help:
"Diagnostic: while the car shadow map is drawn and the contact shadows are at full strength "
    "(the sun 12 degrees up or more, a dry road), the game's sun shadow maps no longer draw the player's car, so its shadow on "
    "the world is the car shadow map's alone and has no second edge of the game's low-detail one. Off: the game draws the "
    "car into them as it always does. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_shadow_map_view.help:
"Diagnostic: 1 draws the car shadow map in a square in the lower left corner of the picture (grey by depth, near the sun "
    "bright; dark blue where nothing of the car is), while the map is drawn. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_light_shadows.help:
"Light shadows: shadows from headlights (and later street lamps). The game draws no shadow from a light that is not the sun; "
    "this draws the scene's opaque objects again from the lights, depth only, into small maps (768 by 768 texels on medium, 1024 by 1024 on high, 1280 by 1280 on ultra: a texel is 1 to 2 cm wide 10 m from the car), and the lights' light reads them. medium shadows your car's headlights and the nearest other car's, with one map for each car; high gives your car a map for each headlamp, "
    "so a pole in front of it casts a shadow from each of its two lamps, and the nearest other car still has one; ultra also shadows the next nearest car, gives all three cars a map for each lamp, "
    "and is sharper. off, medium, high, ultra or auto (the default): ultra on a fast graphics card, medium on a medium one, off on an integrated one. "
    "It only runs while a headlight is lit, in the game view. Costs graphics card time and render thread time (the frame's opaque draws once more for each map) and 9 MiB (medium), "
    "24 MiB (high) or 75 MiB (ultra) of video memory. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_test.help:
"Diagnostic: 1 makes a headlight shadow map from a light of its own at the camera (shining where the camera looks, 35 degrees wide, 40 m), "
    "whenever no car's headlight is lit, so that the maps can be looked at by day with mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_view 1: the map from the camera's own "
    "point of view shows the same scene as the main view, which tells the replay's matrices are right. Nothing reads such a map: no light is shadowed "
    "by it. The setting itself must not be off. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_view.help:
"Diagnostic: 1 draws the headlight shadow atlas in a rectangle in the lower right corner of the picture (grey by distance from the "
    "lamps, near bright; dark blue where nothing was drawn; the tiles are framed), while the maps are drawn. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_skip.help:
"Diagnostic: draws left out of the headlight shadow maps, a sum of 1 plain opaque draws, 2 alpha tested ones (foliage, fences), 4 skinned ones "
    "(people), 8 vehicles' parts. 0: none left out. For finding which kind a wrong shadow comes from. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_cull.help:
"Diagnostic: which faces the headlight shadow maps draw. 0: the faces turned from the light (front faces culled where the game culls back "
    "faces; the default), 1: both faces, 2: the game's own. A pipeline is made for each, so a change takes a moment to build. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_views.help:
"Diagnostic: how many views each shadowed car gets in the headlight shadow maps. 1: one for the car (made from the middle of its two lamps: "
    "the first version's); 2: one for each headlamp (a pole in front of the car casts two shadows). 0: the level's own (medium: one for each car; high: one for each lamp of your car and one for the other car; ultra: one for each lamp of every shadowed car). "
    "A change remakes the atlas. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_bias.help:
"Diagnostic: a factor on the depth bias the headlight shadows' lookup subtracts from a surface's distance from the lamps before it "
    "compares (the map's own slope bias is fixed). Larger: fewer speckles on surfaces that face the lamps and shadows that detach from what casts them. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_cone.help:
"Diagnostic: 1 (the default) leaves out of each headlight shadow map the draws whose place is outside the lamps' view (the view's cone and "
    "reach, with a margin for how far a thing reaches from its place: 7 m for a car, 40 m for anything else), before their constants are copied. 0 draws "
    "every collected draw into every map. For measuring what the cull saves and for finding a shadow the cull took away. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_skirt.help:
"Diagnostic: 1 (the default) draws each vehicle part a second time into the headlight shadow maps, 0.22 m lower and 0.6 m farther "
    "along the light, which puts the underbody on the road and closes the gap under a car that a low lamp shines through (without it the road behind a car is "
    "lit through the ground clearance except where the tyres block: a few thin stripes instead of the car's shadow). 0 draws the car once. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_lamp_cm.help:
"Diagnostic: the radius, in centimetres, of the headlamp the headlight shadows' penumbra is worked out for (the first version: 7, a lens about 14 cm across). "
    "A shadow gets softer with its distance from what casts it by 2 R L / w (L metres behind a blocker that is w metres from the lamp): 1.3 cm at 1 m and 8.8 cm at 7 m behind a pole 9 m away for 7. "
    "Larger is softer, and the kernel it asks for is cut by the footprint (mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_kernel), so at 2 a larger lamp changes little: try 12 with 3 or 4, or 20 with 4. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_kernel.help:
"Diagnostic: how many texel fetches a side the headlight shadows' lookup makes: 2 (the default) reads 4 x 4 texels with 4 fetches and lets a penumbra grow to 1.5 texels each side (the first version's), "
    "3 reads 6 x 6 with 9 fetches (2.5 texels), 4 reads 8 x 8 with 16 fetches (3.5 texels). A larger footprint costs graphics card time (every pixel a headlight lights reads it) and shows a larger lamp "
    "(mcla_gpu_headlight_shadow_lamp_cm) as softer shadows. Live."

mcla_gpu_a2c_dither_all.help:
"Alpha to coverage: every draw takes the same offsets, so a depth pre-pass the game draws "
    "with the solid ones (2, 2, 2, 2) covers the samples its colour pass (dithered 3, 1, 0, 2) "
    "covers: the dithered with MSAA, the solid at 1 sample (a dither there is a fixed screen "
    "door on grass and fences). Off: each draw keeps the game's offsets, as the "
    "console and Xenia -- samples the pre-pass gave depth and the colour pass dropped keep the "
    "clear (white dots on fences and foliage, a white checkerboard on LOD cross-fades; with "
    "MSAA off, whole pixels). Hot reload."
comments: // One alpha-to-mask pattern for every draw. MCLA draws its alpha-tested
// surfaces twice over the same depth: the depth pre-pass (the ShadowBlend
// shaders, whose colour becomes the shadow collector) with the solid offsets
// 2, 2, 2, 2, then, after a colour clear, the colour pass under GREATER_EQUAL
// with the dithered 3, 1, 0, 2. In two pixels of each quad the dithered
// threshold is above the solid one (by 1/(2N) and 1/(4N) at N samples), so a
// sample whose alpha lies between them keeps the pre-pass's depth -- what is
// behind it fails the depth test -- and gets no colour: it keeps the clear,
// 2.38 in the HDR target, a white dot. That is what the hardware rule the
// shaders follow gives (Xenia's; Xenia shows the same dots): half a pixel at
// the console's 2x, the whole pixel at 1x (mcla_gpu_msaa off); dots on fences
// and foliage, a checkerboard on LOD cross-fades. Every draw on one pattern
// makes a surface's depth and colour cover the same samples at any sample
// count. With MSAA it is the dithered one the game gives its colour passes.
// At 1 sample (mcla_gpu_msaa off, every upscaler) a dither has one sample per
// pixel to spread over: a fixed 2x2 screen door on grass and fences that no
// upscaler takes out (it does not move with the jitter). There every draw
// takes the solid 2, 2, 2, 2 of the game's pre-passes, a plain threshold.

mcla_gpu_object_names.help:
"Give the GPU's textures, buffers, shaders and pipelines their debug names, which "
    "RenderDoc, PIX, Nsight Graphics and the D3D12 debug layer show. A name costs a few "
    "microseconds, and a world loads hundreds of textures in one frame, so they are set only "
    "when something can read them: on their own when RenderDoc, PIX or Nsight Graphics started "
    "the game, with mcla_gpu_debug_layer, and with mcla_gpu_perf_markers. This turns them on for "
    "a tool that does not load a DLL (Radeon GPU Profiler) or that attaches later. Read when the "
    "device opens."

mcla_gpu_frame_generation_multiplier.help:
"How many frames DLSS frame generation shows for each one the game renders (mcla_gpu_frame_"
    "generation = dlss): 2 makes one in between, 3 two, 4 three. 3 and 4 need an RTX 50 series card "
    "(the plugin says how many the card takes; a higher number than it takes is lowered). The frame "
    "cap counts rendered frames (mcla_gpu_frame_generation_fps_limit). Live."

mcla_gpu_census_ps.help:
"Diagnostic: up to 4 pixel shader identities, hex, comma separated. Per "
    "guest frame, the draws and vertices recorded with each; per report window, their "
    "distribution. Empty: off."

mcla_gpu_census_targets.help:
"Diagnostic: per report window, every pass the frames drew into (its EDRAM "
    "targets) with its draws per frame and the pixel shaders that drew there."

mcla_gpu_edram_aliasing.help:
"EDRAM inheritance detector (M5.2d): per EDRAM "
    "tile and aspect, the identity that wrote it last, reporting a draw or a resolve that would "
    "see another identity's bytes on the console -- which the host does not carry over. Off: "
    "none of its work is done."

mcla_gpu_coverage_queries.help:
"With mcla_gpu_edram_aliasing: an occlusion query around each opaque draw the detector "
    "takes to cover its scissor, checking that it did. Costs GPU time, for "
    "checking a report. Off: no query pool is made, read or reset, and such takes go "
    "unchecked (listed once per pair)."

mcla_gpu_edram_capture.help:
"With mcla_gpu_edram_aliasing: a RenderDoc capture of the frame after the first report of "
    "each kind picked by these bits, 4 at most: 1 a pair met by a write that keeps "
    "or blends another identity's bytes, 2 a pair met by a read, 4 the first reader of "
    "inherited bytes of each kind. 0: none. Needs the game started under RenderDoc."

mcla_gpu_gbuffer.help:
"Diagnostic (G-buffer, perf/GBUFFER-SURVEY.md): which planes of the G-buffer the main view's lit shaders write beside the "
    "game's colour. off: none, and the game's own shaders draw, bit for bit. normals: the world normal of the surfaces whose shader has the G-buffer variant, "
    "into a second render target the main view's draws carry, cleared with the game's own clear of the main colour. full: the same, the other planes are not "
    "written yet. auto: what the effects that are on ask for (the ambient occlusion, the contact shadows and the bounce light ask for the normal while mcla_gpu_ao_gbuffer_normals is on; none on: no image is made and no shader changes). The colour of the picture "
    "is the same with it on. Not in the 4x views behind the pause menu and the map, nor in a cutscene. Live (the first frame with it on builds the extra shaders "
    "and pipelines: a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_gbuffer_attach.help:
"Diagnostic (G-buffer): which draws of the main view bind the G-buffer's render targets. writers: only the draws whose shader "
    "writes it (the planes keep what an earlier draw wrote under a draw of a shader that has no variant yet). all: every draw of the main view's window, the ones that "
