    "write no plane with a blend state that clears (an opaque draw: the pixels become no data) or masks (a blended draw: they stay); no render pass switch, no stale "
    "pixels. It needs a blend state per render target: Vulkan has it, Direct3D 12 only with the Plume fix that enables independent blending, and forcing all without "
    "it puts undefined values in the planes. auto: all where the back end has it, writers where not. Live."

mcla_gpu_gbuffer_view.help:
"Diagnostic (G-buffer): draws one plane of the G-buffer over the main view at the mid-scene depth copy, where the ambient "
    "occlusion runs (only while mcla_gpu_gbuffer makes the plane): 1 the normal as a colour (0.5 + 0.5 n), 2 the albedo, 3 the smoothness, 4 the class "
    "of each pixel as a colour, 5 which pixels hold data (white) and which do not (black), 6 the lit weight, 7 the missing pixels (green: data; red: the depth "
    "holds geometry and the planes hold no data; black: the sky). The planes no shader writes yet show as no data. The rest of the frame (particles, tone map, "
    "glow) is drawn over it as usual, so the colours are the game's after the tone map. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_screen_extract.help:
"Diagnostic (shared screen products): where the depth chain, the normal image and the bounce light's colour chain are recorded. true (the default): by the shared screen "
    "products, once a frame, into images they own (the ambient occlusion, the bounce light, the contact shadows and the reflections read them). false: by the ambient "
    "occlusion's own passes into the same images (the old path, kept for one release to compare pictures). Both give the same bits. Live."

mcla_gpu_screen_hiz_fused.help:
"Diagnostic (shared screen products): how the Hi-Z's first levels are made while the reflections want it. true (the default): the depth chain's own passes write them beside their "
    "images in the same draw (the depth pass the Hi-Z's level 0, the two coarser depth levels its levels 1 and 2), so that the Hi-Z's own passes for them are not recorded. false: "
    "the Hi-Z's own pass for every level (the old path, kept for one release to compare pictures). Both give the same bits. Needs mcla_gpu_screen_extract. Live."

mcla_gpu_screen_view.help:
"Diagnostic (shared screen products): draws one product of the shared screen frame over the main view at the mid-scene depth copy, where the ambient "
    "occlusion runs (it runs a frame of its own for this when it and the contact shadows are off): 1 the linear depth, 2 the Hi-Z level mcla_gpu_screen_view_level (the min of "
    "the linear depth, each texel stretched over the pixels it covers), 3 the Hi-Z level against the pixels it covers (red where it is deeper than one of them, which cannot "
    "be; green, brighter where the min is nearer than the pixel), 4 the normal image (only in a frame whose passes make it), 5 the vehicle mark of the depth, 6 colour_post (the level mcla_gpu_screen_view_level; only while a consumer or this view makes it), 7 the history's colour (the last frame's colour_post). The rest of the "
    "frame (particles, tone map, glow) is drawn over it as usual. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_screen_view_level.help:
"Diagnostic (shared screen products): the level the views 2 and 3 (the Hi-Z) and 6 (colour_post) of mcla_gpu_screen_view show: 0 is the traced size (colour_post's own size for the view 6), "
    "each level above is half the one below (the Hi-Z has 7 levels at 1080 lines, down to 1/64, colour_post up to 5 and only while the reflections want them); a level the chain does not have shows its last. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr.help:
"Reflections on surfaces: sharp reflections of the scene on wet roads, wet sidewalks, glass, metal and water, traced through the picture itself (screen space) and added to "
    "the game's own reflections. A car's paint and chrome keep their own (CAR REFLECTIONS, CAR SELF-REFLECTIONS). Only what is on the screen can be reflected: where a ray "
    "finds nothing, or a surface is near the picture's edge, the game's own reflection stays alone. off, high, ultra or auto (the default: for now off on every graphics card). "
    "high: one ray a pixel at half the picture's size, up to 40 steps, about 10 frames of history; ultra: two rays a pixel, up to 64 steps, about 12 frames, which is smoother "
    "and finds more. Costs graphics card time, the G-buffer's planes (made only while this is on) and about 12 MiB (1080p) to 48 MiB (4K) of video memory for the effect's own "
    "images. A wet road reflects, a dry one does not (the weather's wetness takes about a second to rise or fall). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_view.help:
"Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): draws one picture over the main view in place of the effect's add, where the ambient occlusion runs: 1 the term the effect adds (alone on black), 2 the class gate "
    "(green a pixel that reflects, brighter with its share; blue the stub's; orange a vehicle or the paint and chrome, which keep their own reflections; dark red anything else; black no data), 3 the raw trace at "
    "half size before the accumulation (premultiplied radiance), 4 the trace's distance (blue to white by a log scale, orange where the hit is a vehicle's, red a ray that found nothing, black not traced), 5 the game's road reflection view as the effect reads it, over the whole picture (black: none in this frame), 6 the term's sign (green what is added, red what is taken out of the game's own reflection). 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_gi.help:
"Ray traced bounce light: light bounces around the city the way it does in the real world. The sunlit street and walls light the shaded sides of buildings, the ground under bridges "
    "and the insides of alleys with a soft glow in place of a flat ambient, large coloured walls tint what stands near them, and at night each street lamp and neon sign lights the facades, "
    "the sidewalk and the cars around it a little more. What is behind or beside the camera counts too (the screen-space bounce light, mcla_gpu_ssgi, can only use what is in the picture). "
    "It is worked out in a field of probes laid round the camera from the city's own triangles (the city pack) and added to the picture where the G-buffer knows the surface; it never darkens. "
    "Where it stands it takes the place of the screen-space bounce light, which stays for graphics cards that cannot ray trace and for the places the field does not cover, and it is as strong as "
    "BOUNCE LIGHT STRENGTH says (mcla_gpu_ssgi_intensity). off, high, ultra or auto (the default): high on a graphics card that traces rays quickly (the ray tracing tier strong: about an RTX 3070 "
    "and up, an RX 7800 XT and up), off on the rest; a weaker ray tracing card can switch it on by hand, with fewer probes. high is three cascades of probes, 2, 4 and 8 m apart, "
    "or two, 3 and 6 m apart on a weaker card. ultra adds a fourth cascade, 16 m apart, and refreshes the probes twice as often. Needs a graphics card with ray queries (Direct3D 12 with DirectX Raytracing 1.1, or Vulkan with ray queries) "
    "and the city pack; without them the screen-space bounce light stands. The pause menu's RT BOUNCE LIGHT row (GRAPHICS > LIGHTING AND SHADOWS). Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_gi_view.help: "Diagnostic (ray traced bounce light, the probe field's apply): draws one picture over the main view in place of the bounce light's add, at the trigger where the field runs: 1 the irradiance the field holds at the pixel, 2 the confidence (red the field has nothing there, green it stands), 3 the sky visibility (dark blue closed, white open), 5 the ground baseline the field's irradiance is reduced by, 6 the leak test (green no probe is hidden from the point by geometry, red all of them are), 9 the light the pass adds (alone on black, four times as bright), 10 the net irradiance after the baseline, the dead band and the cap, 11 the occlusion's term the bounce is multiplied by. 4, 7 and 8 are the field's own pictures (the probes as spheres). 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_gi_bounces.help:
"Diagnostic (ray traced bounce light): how much of the field's own light the probes take back in when they are updated, which is the second bounce and the ones after it for free: "
    "0 is strictly one bounce, 0.5 (the default) is about two, with brighter canyons; 0.95 at most, so that the loop cannot grow. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_gi_dry_run.help:
"Diagnostic (ray traced bounce light): lets the probe field run while the probe update (package G2 of the design) is not built into this renderer, to prove the field's owner and the order of the frame. "
    "With RT BOUNCE LIGHT on, the field's textures are made, its reset and weights passes run and the apply is told of it, but nothing traces into the probes, so the field never becomes ready, shows nothing, "
    "and the screen-space bounce light stays the source. The RT BOUNCE LIGHT row is grey with (NOT READY) while the update is missing; this makes it live for a test. Has no effect once the update is built. Live."

mcla_gpu_gi_cabin.help:
"Diagnostic (ray traced bounce light, the player's cabin, INTERIOR-CAM-FIX, the A/B): on (the default) the probe field's bounce light on the cabin's own surfaces (the driver, the dash, the wheel, the seats: a vehicle's part that is not paint, chrome or glass, inside the car's box) "
    "is cut to 30% while the camera is inside a roofed car, because the probes trace the city only and cannot see the car's roof (the glass's share is left); off is the field's light as it was (the street's irradiance at the cabin, as if the car had no roof). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_strength.help: "Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the effect's strength, 0 to 4: the added reflection is multiplied by it (the class's own gain, the Fresnel term and the picture's edge fades come on top). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_min_smooth.help:
"Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): a pixel rougher than this (0 rough to 1 mirror; the G-buffer's smoothness after the road's wetness raised it) is not reflected. -1: the default, 0.40 (a dry road at 0.30 is not, "
    "a wet one at 0.92 is). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_stub.help:
"Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): 0 uses the G-buffer's material plane (RT3) where the frame has it and the stub where it does not (every pixel whose world normal points up and is no vehicle is a road of "
    "smoothness 0.85); 1 always the stub. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_wet.help:
"Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the road's wetness, 0 dry to 1 pouring rain: it raises a road's and a sidewalk's smoothness. -1: what the game says (the vertex constant c43.x of the main view's draws, "
    "0.095 dry and 1.17 in rain, smoothed over about a second). A value forces it, to look at the wet road without rain. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_history.help:
"Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the share of the last frames the accumulation keeps, 0 to 0.98 (0.9 is a mean of about ten frames; 0 draws the raw ray, noise and all). -1: the level's (high 0.90, ultra 0.92). "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_fallback.help: "Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the share of the game's own road reflection (its 256 x 256 planar view of the whole screen) the effect takes out of a road where its rays find a reflection of their own, 0 to 1 (times the strength the game shows that view with, VS c43.y): 1 replaces the soft reflection with the sharp one, 0 adds the effect on top of it (the reflection is then doubled, as before the fallback). Where no ray finds anything the game's reflection stays alone. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_vehicle_rows.help: "Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): 1 moves the reflection of a moving vehicle with the vehicle's own motion (the ambient occlusion's vehicle table), 0 treats it as the world's, which smears it (the comparison). Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_rt.help:
"Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the ray traced fallback, for the pixels the picture could not speak for (a reflected thing that is off the picture, behind something in front of it, or a ray that points back at "
    "the camera): the same ray is traced into the city's buildings and what it hits is shaded with the city's own materials and lights, so a wet street shows the street instead of the game's blurred reflection. "
    "auto (the default): follows REFLECTIONS ON SURFACES on a graphics card that traces rays quickly (high: glass, metal and water, up to 0.25 million rays a frame; ultra: also roads and sidewalks, up to 1 million, "
    "two rays a pixel), off on a weak one and on a card that does not trace rays at all. off: the screen-space reflections alone (the comparison); high or ultra: that level on any card that traces rays (a weak card "
    "takes a lighter version). Needs ray queries, the city pack and the city hit data, and REFLECTIONS ON SURFACES on; a governor lowers the cap by half, up to three times, while the passes take more than "
    "their share of the frame. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_denoise.help: "Diagnostic (screen-space reflections, the ray traced fallback): RtDenoise, the filter that cleans the fallback's noise where DLSS Ray Reconstruction does not (a bilateral a-trous on the pixels the fallback made: the kernel follows the reflection, wide for a rough surface and a far hit, narrow for a near mirror, and stops at edges of depth, normal, roughness, brightness and hit distance). -1 (the default): the level of REFLECTIONS ON SURFACES gives the number of iterations (high 2, ultra 3); 0: off (the comparison); 1 to 3: that many iterations (steps of 1, 2 and 4 pixels of the half size image). Skipped by itself in a frame Ray Reconstruction takes. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_blue_noise.help: "Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the reflection rays' random numbers (which way inside the surface's lobe each pixel looks) come from a blue noise tile that has no lattice in it, stepped along the R2 sequence every frame, so what the accumulation leaves of the noise is a fine grain that stays where it is. False: the first version's interleaved gradient noise, a lattice that slid across the picture 5.6 pixels a frame and read as stripes crawling over a puddle, for comparing. Live."

mcla_gpu_ssr_resolve.help: "Diagnostic (screen-space reflections): the accumulation averages the trace's 3x3 over the pixels of one surface before it takes the history (nine rays of one lobe are nearer its mean than one), looks the history of a pixel whose ray found nothing up with the nearest hit of its neighbours, and does not let one frame whose rays all missed wipe a bright reflection (the clip takes at most a quarter of it a frame). A lamp's or a tail light's reflection flickered with the sparse hits. False: the first version's resolve (the centre pixel alone, the clip whole), for comparing. Live."

mcla_gpu_ghost_log_interval.help:
"Diagnostic: log one live frame in every N with the 1280x720 scene clears "
    "and three-stripe resolves, plus all EDRAM target creations and growths. 0: off; 1: every "
    "frame. Hot reload for reproducing the frame ghost."

mcla_gpu_msaa.help:
"MSAA of the images of the screen the game multisamples (M6d.2): off (1 sample), 2 (the "
    "console's), 4 or 8 samples on the host. The game itself always draws its own 2 sample "
    "layout; the host gives its images of the screen the samples chosen here, so its pause menu "
    "and map world view, which the game draws with 4 samples, get the same as the game view. "
    "Targets the game does not multisample, or that are not images of the screen, keep the "
    "game's samples. Live: a change is made between two frames, after the pipelines for the new "
    "sample count are made. While an upscaler (mcla_gpu_upscaler) runs, MSAA is 1 sample "
    "whatever this says (the upscaler smooths the picture, and MSAA under it only costs time); "
    "the choice is kept and comes back when the upscaler is off."

mcla_gpu_flicker_probe.help:
"Diagnostic: read every guest frame back, as the window shows it, and log "
    "the blocks of 16x16 pixels that change for 1-5 frames and come back to exactly their "
    "old bytes (a flicker). Meant for a static scene such as the pause menu. Costs a copy of "
    "the image per frame on the GPU and about a millisecond of render-thread CPU. Off: "
    "nothing is made."

mcla_gpu_flicker_probe_dumps.help:
"With mcla_gpu_flicker_probe: how many flicker events also write the frame before, the "
    "first frame of the blip and the frame after as mcla_flicker_<event>_<frame>_<what>.tga "
    "next to the executable (3.7 MB each at 1280x720)."

mcla_gpu_flicker_probe_shots.help:
"With mcla_gpu_flicker_probe: a comma-separated list of guest frame numbers, each written "
    "as mcla_flicker_000_<frame>_shot.tga next to the executable whether or not it flickered. "
    "For comparing what two platforms or builds put in the window at the same frame."

mcla_gpu_frame_generation.help:
"Frame generation: off, fsr31 (AMD FSR 3.1 frame generation, on any graphics card, with or "
    "without an upscaler) or dlss (NVIDIA DLSS frame generation through Streamline, on an RTX 40 or "
    "50 series card: 2x, and 3x or 4x on an RTX 50 with mcla_gpu_frame_generation_multiplier; "
    "Streamline presents the frames, and on Vulkan it applies from the next start). An interpolated "
    "frame is made between every two the game renders and "
    "shown half a frame before the real one, so a game that renders 60 frames a second shows 120. "
    "It does not make the game react faster: the real frames are shown one frame later and the "
    "latency reducer (NVIDIA Reflex, AMD Anti-Lag 2) is switched on while it runs, where the card "
    "has one. Only the 3D scene is generated; the menus, the pause menu, the map and the loading "
    "screens are shown as the game draws them, and the interface is drawn over each generated "
    "frame. The frame rate limit counts rendered frames while it runs "
    "(mcla_gpu_frame_generation_fps_limit). Wants a display of 100 Hz or more or a variable refresh "
    "display. Live: it is taken at a frame boundary and the picture may flicker once while the "
    "window's swap chain is made again. Only offered where the graphics card and the AMD files next "
    "to the game can run it."

mcla_gpu_frame_generation_fps_limit.help:
"The frame rate cap while frame generation runs, in frames the game RENDERS a second (twice as "
    "many are shown): -1 is HALF DISPLAY, the default, the floor of 97% of half of the display's "
    "refresh rate (116 at 240 Hz, 58 at 120 Hz), which fills the display; it is only offered on a "
    "display of 100 Hz or more, and where it is not the cap you chose (fps_limit) applies. 0 is no "
    "cap, and a number from 1 to 360 caps the rendered frames at it (60 shows 120). A cap above half "
    "the display's rate adds latency: the frames queue in front of the display. Live."

mcla_gpu_frame_generation_tearing.help:
"Frame generation presents with vertical sync (FIFO), so a frame is never torn and a variable "
    "refresh display follows the frames. On presents immediately instead, which tears. Live: read at "
    "every present while frame generation runs."

mcla_gpu_trace_frame.help:
"Write a raw trace of the guest frame that begins after this many guest "
                      "frames (0 = off) to mcla_gpu_trace_<frame>.txt next to the executable. "
                      "Decoded by tools/gpu/trace_analyze.py. A 6000-draw frame is tens of MB."

mcla_gpu_trace_count.help: "How many consecutive frames mcla_gpu_trace_frame writes, one file each."

mcla_gpu_class.help:
"Diagnostic: forces the GPU class the graphics upgrades' auto values are chosen from (low: "
    "integrated GPUs and handhelds, mid: discrete with under about 6 GiB of video memory or a "
    "slower GPU family such as the GTX 10 and 16 series and the RX 400/500 series, high: the "
    "rest). "
    "auto: the class the renderer found for this GPU, logged at start as '[gpu] class: ...' with "
    "the rule that chose it (by adapter type, by memory or by name). Only "
    "the value auto of the upgrades follows it (shadow filter and detail, car and road reflection "
    "detail, ambient occlusion, contact shadows, sun shafts, bounce light); "
    "a choice of the player's own is never changed. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_tier.help:
"Diagnostic: forces the ray tracing tier the ray traced upgrades' auto values are chosen from (none: "
    "the card cannot trace rays or has no ray tracing units, weak: it traces at a moderate speed, such as an RTX 3060 or an RX 6600, "
    "strong: it traces quickly, such as an RTX 5080 or an RX 7900 XT). "
    "auto: the tier found for this card (its table row and, when it ran, the benchmark of mcla_gpu_rt_bench), logged at start as "
    "'[gpu] ray tracing tier: ...' with the rule that chose it; while mcla_gpu_class forces a class, the tier follows it (high: strong, "
    "mid: weak, low: none) so that a test that says a class runs that class's cells. Only the value auto of the ray traced upgrades "
    "(the car's reflection, occlusion and sun ray; later the city's shadows, reflections and bounce light) follows it, and the "
    "number of cars they trace and how far; a choice of the player's own is never changed. Live."

mcla_gpu_rt_bench.help:
"Diagnostic: the ray tracing benchmark that can move a card between the weak and the strong tier. "
    "auto: on the first start with a card that can trace (and again after its driver or the graphics API changes) a short compute pass "
    "traces a few million rays through a small synthetic city and logs the speed ('[gpu] rt bench: ...'), which is kept in "
    "rt_bench.txt next to larecomp.toml; off: no benchmark, and a kept result is not read; force: run it at every start. "
    "Takes effect at the next start."

mcla_gpu_readable_cache.help:
"Ask the guest heap whether a guest range is readable once a guest frame per 4 KiB page "
    "instead of once a draw: the capture checks about ten ranges a draw, and each check takes "
    "the heap's lock (about 0.2 ms a frame at 2,600 draws). The pages found readable are "
    "forgotten at every present. A page the guest unmaps within the frame and that a later draw "
    "still points at would be read as before the unmapping (the memory stays mapped, so it "
    "cannot fault); off asks the heap at every check, as before."

mcla_gpu_readable_cache_check.help:
"Diagnostic, with mcla_gpu_readable_cache: also ask the heap at every check the cache answers, "
    "and count and log (the first 16) the answers that differ. The count is in the "
    "'[gpu] readable cache:' line at shutdown; it must be 0. The heap is asked as often as without "
    "the cache."

mcla_gpu_shader_memo_check.help:
"Diagnostic: no draw takes its shaders from the frame's identity memo; every draw reads the "
    "guest's shader objects and looks the identity up in full, and the memo's answer, address, "
    "size and variant are compared with it. The differences are counted and logged (the first 16); "
    "the count is in the '[gpu] shader memo:' line at shutdown and must be 0. The lookups cost as "
    "much as without the memo."

mcla_gpu_hdr.help:
"HDR output for an HDR10 display. off: the usual picture. auto: HDR while Windows has HDR "
    "turned on for the display the game is on, following Windows' HDR switch and the display the "
    "window is moved to. on: HDR even if Windows does not say its HDR is on; where the display or "
    "the driver cannot show it the usual picture is used and the log says why. The HUD and the "
    "menus are shown at your paper white setting; the game's lights, the sun, the sky at dusk and "
    "the headlights go above it (how far: mcla_gpu_hdr_highlights). Takes effect within a moment, "
    "at the end of a frame; the picture may flicker once while the window's swap chain is made "
    "again."

mcla_gpu_hdr_paper_white_nits.help:
"How bright the game's white is in HDR, in nits (Windows' own slider covers 80 to 480). 0: "
    "the Windows SDR content brightness setting, or 200 when Windows does not report it. "
    "Changes at once."

mcla_gpu_hdr_peak_nits.help:
"The brightest level HDR output may reach, in nits (200 to 4000 covers most displays). 0: "
    "what the display reports, or 1000 when it reports nothing. Changes at once."

mcla_gpu_hdr_test_pattern.help:
"In HDR, shows brightness bars instead of the game. The top row starts at 100 nits and "
    "doubles every 4 bars, to see where the display stops showing steps; the bottom left is "
    "paper white and the bottom right the same bars rolled off to the peak setting. It covers the "
    "whole picture, the menus too. The pause menu's TEST PATTERN row shows it only while that row "
    "is highlighted and never saves it; set on the command line it stays on for the run. Changes at "
    "once."

mcla_gpu_hdr_layers_view.help:
"Diagnostic (HDR output): what a frame whose UI was kept as a layer shows. 0 the frame, 1 the "
    "UI layer alone, 2 the scene alone, 3 the UI's coverage as grey, 4 magenta where the scene "
    "is above the game's white, 5 the float scene's difference from the 8-bit scene times 16. "
    "Frames without layers show the front buffer whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_hdr_compose_in_present.help:
"Diagnostic (HDR output): the present's passes that read the frame 1:1 add the UI layer to the "
    "scene themselves, instead of reading a float image the compose pass made of the two. On by "
    "default: one full-screen float16 pass and its image less (about 0.15 ms and 63 MiB at 4K). Off: "
    "the compose pass and its image as before, for comparing the two. A scaled present and the "
    "debug views of mcla_gpu_hdr_layers_view use the image whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_hdr_highlights.help:
"HDR output: how far the game's lights, the sun, the sky at dusk and the headlights go above "
    "the game's white: 1 normal, 1.5 bright, 2 brighter, 3 brightest. It is the steepness of the "
    "HDR curve above where it leaves the game's, so the brightest light stays under the display's "
    "peak whatever it is. Changes at once, also in the world behind the pause menu and the map; "
    "nothing happens while HDR output is off."

mcla_gpu_headlights.help:
"Headlights: the cars' headlights light the road, the world and the other cars at night (the game's own only glow). "
    "Your car, the nearest opponents and the nearest traffic cars each get a spot light in front of them, up to four at a "
    "time, from dusk to dawn. on is the one level; off leaves the night as the game has it. auto (the default) is on for "
    "a discrete graphics card and off for an integrated one (a handheld, or the iGPU of a desktop CPU). Costs the "
    "graphics card a little at night, only on the pixels the beams reach. Live; the first time the headlights show, the "
    "graphics card builds the lit shaders' variants (a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_neon_light.help:
"Neon light: the neon underglow of a car lights the ground, the kerbs, the walls and the other cars near it, in the neon's own colour and pulse. "
    "on is the one level; off leaves the neon as the game has it (its own glow under the car). auto (the default) is on for a discrete graphics card and off for an integrated one (a handheld, "
    "or the iGPU of a desktop CPU). It costs the graphics card a little, only while a car with its neon lit is in view, and only on the pixels the neon reaches (a few metres round the car). "
    "Live; the first time it shows, the graphics card builds its pipeline (a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_headlight_strength.help:
"Diagnostic: how strong the headlights are, a number their light is multiplied by (1: the built-in look; 0: none). "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_range.help: "Diagnostic: how far a headlight reaches, in metres (the light falls to nothing there). Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_cone.help: "Diagnostic: the headlight cone's outer half angle in degrees (the full light is inside a third of it). Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_night.help:
"Diagnostic: when the headlights are on. -1: from the game's own lights (each car's headlight points say whether "
    "they are on: 2.0 at night, 0 by day), and from the sun's height for a car whose points were not seen (night below "
    "3 degrees, none above 12; the default). 0: never. 1: always, by the sun's rule alone, to see them by day. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_edge.help:
"Diagnostic: how the headlights pick the cars at the edge of the frame. On (the default): a car is worth what its beam "
    "adds to the picture, not where its lamp is, and a car the game stops drawing because it left the frame keeps its light while its beam is still in the view "
    "(up to 1.5 seconds), fading with the beam and with its distance. Off: the first version, a light dropped within 8 frames of the game's last draw of its car, and "
    "a car whose lamp is off the screen counted at 0.35. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_log.help:
"Diagnostic: logs a census line of the headlights every 300 frames, with '[headlights]' in front: the sun and the "
    "night factor, the lens draws seen, the cars with a front lens, the lights picked with their place and axis, and the "
    "draws that took the variant. Live."

mcla_gpu_low_latency.help:
"The GPU vendor's latency reducer: NVIDIA Reflex on an NVIDIA GPU, AMD Anti-Lag 2 on an AMD "
    "one. It holds the game back at the start of a frame just long enough that the frame meets a "
    "free GPU: less input lag when the GPU is the limit, at the price of some frame rate when "
    "it is. auto (Reflex on; Anti-Lag 2 off until it has been tried on a Radeon), off, on, or "
    "boost (Reflex's On + Boost: the GPU clocks stay high; Anti-Lag 2 has no boost and takes it "
    "as on). Where the GPU, the driver or the graphics API has no reducer the pause menu has no "
    "row for it and it stays off whatever this says (the log says why at start). While frame "
    "generation runs (mcla_gpu_frame_generation) it is on whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_memory_census.help:
"Watch every vertex and index range the executed draws read, the way the buffer cache will, "
    "and log every 600 frames what that cache would upload ("
    "24.21). Diagnostic: it write-protects guest pages."

mcla_gpu_msaa_with_upscaler.help:
"While FSR or DLSS draws the scene, keep the MSAA level of mcla_gpu_msaa (2, 4 or 8 samples) "
    "instead of 1 sample. The upscaler then gets a scene whose edges and alpha tested foliage are "
    "already smoothed by the sample coverage, and has less aliasing to average over its jitter; it "
    "costs the multisampled scene at the render size. The upscaler's masks (mcla_gpu_upscaler_masks) "
    "are not affected: they are drawn into coverage images with the same samples and averaged, so "
    "the two switches are independent. For A/B. Live (read at start too)."

mcla_gpu_perf_markers.help:
"Name the frame's phases in the command lists for GPU profilers: PIX events on D3D12, "
    "debug utils labels on Vulkan; how deep, mcla_gpu_perf_markers_level. Nsight GPU "
    "Trace's multi-pass metrics need them. Off: no label is recorded. Read when a frame "
    "starts."

mcla_gpu_perf_markers_level.help:
"How deep mcla_gpu_perf_markers names the frame. 0: Frame alone. 1: Frame and its phases "
    "(Scene, EndOfFrame, Present, Overlay) -- the same in every frame, what Nsight's multi-pass "
    "metrics need. 2: also a label per guest clear, resolve, composite and Lock write-back "
    "inside Scene; their count changes from frame to frame, so multi-pass metrics drop them. "
    "Read when a frame starts."

mcla_gpu_skip_shaders.help:
"Workaround for a driver that dies compiling one particular shader combination: a "
    "comma-separated list of shader identities (the 16 hex digits of the pack's keys). A "
    "guest pipeline that uses any of them is not built, and its draws are treated like those "
    "of a pipeline that failed. Measured on Mesa's dzn (Vulkan over D3D12 in WSL2), which "
    "overflows its stack in vkCreateGraphicsPipelines for the pair b000e9d48f010bd8 + "
    "68387d4a0b431769 (each alone is fine)."

mcla_gpu_pipeline_cache.help:
"Keep the pipelines the game asked for across sessions ("
    "24.35, M5.3): their keys go to cache/mcla_gpu_pipelines_<backend>.bin beside the "
    "executable on exit, and are read back at start -- the other backend's file too, so what one "
    "API saw is ready in the other (24.40 V2). Off: nothing is read, recorded or written."

mcla_gpu_bloom_scale.help:
"Fix: the glow of lights (the bloom) keeps the size the game gives it at render scales above 1x "
    "(a higher render resolution, or an upscaler to a 1080p or 4K output). The game blurs the bloom "
    "with taps a fixed number of pixels apart; at 2x or 3x the same taps reach half or a third as far "
    "on the screen, so a window's glow shrinks and the glow of a lamp or a tail light disappears. This "
    "makes each tap cover the pixels it stands for, so the glow looks as it does at 1x. At a render "
    "scale of 1x the picture is the same either way. Off: the game's own taps. Live."

mcla_gpu_glow_visibility.help:
"How the glow of street lamps (their halo and star) and the other glow sprites decide whether they are "
    "hidden by the scene: game (the game's own: one depth test at the glow's centre, so a lamp beside a palm "
    "trunk or a pole pops fully on and off as the wind or the camera moves it by a fraction of a pixel) or "
    "soft (the share of 24 tests on a small disc round the centre scales the glow: a glow in the open is the "
    "game's, one at an edge fades over about two pixels instead of popping; the disc is the same size at every "
    "render scale). game leaves the game's own shaders, and the picture, as they are. Needs the shader pack's "
    "variant file. Live; the first time soft shows, the graphics card builds its shaders (a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_luminance_scale_fix.help:
"Fix: the game's auto-exposure (how bright the picture is made, which adapts over time) measures the "
    "same part of the screen at render scales above 1x as at 1x. The game averages the brightness of the "
    "frame from a small set of taps a fixed number of pixels apart; at 2x or 3x the same taps cover a "
    "half or a third of the area they covered at 1x (28% of the picture at 3x), so a small bright light "
    "(a lamp, a lit window, a tail light) moving in and out of one of them can make the brightness pump "
    "or flicker, most at night. This makes each tap average the pixels it stands for. At a render scale "
    "of 1x the picture is the same either way. Off: the game's own taps. Live."

mcla_gpu_aa.help:
"Anti-aliasing of the composed scene, before the UI (M6c): off, fxaa (FXAA "
    "3.11, Xenia's preset) or smaa (SMAA 1x, preset HIGH). The image the game resolves into the "
    "front buffer includes it (photos too). Live."

mcla_gpu_fsr.help:
"FSR1 on the present (M6c.1): when the window's letterbox is larger than the "
    "front buffer on both axes, EASU passes (at most 2x per axis each) up to it, then RCAS. "
    "Otherwise the bilinear present. Live."

mcla_gpu_fsr_sharpness.help:
"FSR1 RCAS sharpness reduction in stops: 0 sharpest, 2 softest (the SDK presenter's "
    "present_fsr_sharpness_reduction and its default). Live."

mcla_gpu_fsr_max_passes.help:
"Most FSR1 EASU passes (each at most 2x per axis); a bilinear stretch finishes what they "
    "leave. The SDK presenter's present_fsr_max_upsampling_passes. Live."

mcla_gpu_present_dither.help:
"Adds a faint noise, at most half of one colour step of the screen, to the finished picture "
    "just before it is shown, so that smooth gradients (the sky at dusk) show fewer bands. Live."

mcla_gpu_process_memory_log.help:
"Diagnostic: every this many frames, log what the process's memory is made of (the commit "
    "charge and working set, the committed address space by kind, the private regions by size, "
    "the process heaps, the biggest regions). It walks the whole address space, which takes "
    "some milliseconds on the render thread each time. 0: off."

mcla_gpu_vsync.help: "Present on vertical blank. Read every frame."

mcla_gpu_pass_timing.help:
"Measure GPU time per pass: a timestamp at every pass boundary (target change, resolve, "
    "clear, present, overlay), summed per pass and logged by cost with the frame statistics. "
    "A measurement for the performance work, off by "
    "default."

mcla_gpu_present_wait.help:
"Pace presents with the swap chain's latency wait (DXGI waitable object / "
    "VK_KHR_present_wait) when the device has it. On D3D12 Plume then presents with sync "
    "interval 0 and the wait alone paces the frame, so measure before turning it on."

mcla_gpu_adapter.help:
"Adapter name to create the device on. Empty: on D3D12 the adapter Windows' "
                      "graphics setting for this app names, else the high-performance GPU; on "
                      "Vulkan Plume picks, or the GPU graphics_backend auto chose Vulkan for. The "
                      "emulated GPU (RENDERER: XENIA) runs on the same one unless d3d12_adapter or "
                      "vulkan_device is set."

mcla_gpu_verify_constants.help:
"Compare every 64-byte block of both constant banks on every draw, not only the blocks the "
    "guest's dirty masks name, and send (and count) any that changed without its dirty bit. "
    "Costs guest CPU per draw. Off by default since M3 measured no block outside the masks; the "
    "guest's XXH3 of both banks every 32 draws still checks the rebuilt banks "
    "."

mcla_gpu_validate.help:
"Run the milestone M3 validator on every record besides the replay: per-record counters and "
    "the mcla_gpu_validation_*.csv files next to the executable. Decodes every draw a second "
    "time on the render thread (3.5-7 ms/frame measured in M3)."

mcla_gpu_batch_draws.help:
"Submit the guest frame's command list to the GPU every this many prepared draws, unfenced, "
    "and continue in a new list (0: one submission per guest frame, the default). For measuring "
    "submission batching."

mcla_gpu_present_release.help:
"Release the guest's Swap as soon as the render thread has read the last guest memory a "
    "present needs (after the scene's end-of-frame work and the front buffer's texture), and "
    "before it submits the frame and presents. Without it the guest waits for the whole present, "
    "about 0.2 ms a frame at 240 FPS. Not used with mcla_gpu_vsync, nor when the previous present "
    "took longer than 1 ms after that point (the GPU is behind): the guest then waits as before, "
    "so it never runs more than that ahead."

mcla_gpu_present_release_check.help:
"Diagnostic, with mcla_gpu_present_release: checks what that rests on. It releases the guest at "
    "every guest present (also when the GPU is behind), and from the release to the end of the "
    "present it counts, and logs the first 16, each read or write of guest memory by the render "
    "thread. The count is in the '[gpu] present release:' line at shutdown; it must be 0."

mcla_gpu_debug_layer.help:
"Enable the D3D12 debug layer before the device exists and log its warnings "
                    "and errors. Needs D3D12SDKLayers.dll from the same Agility SDK release as "
                    "D3D12\\D3D12Core.dll, placed next to it (the system's copy belongs to the OS "
                    "runtime). Vulkan validation is a property of a Debug build of Plume and "
                    "cannot be switched on here."

mcla_gpu_resolution_scale.help:
"Render scale: every render target that is an image of the screen (the scene, the UI, the "
    "post-processing sized from the screen) is this many times the guest's in each direction, from "
    "0.5 to 3 in steps of 0.05 (0.75 = 960x540, 1.5 = 1920x1080, 2 = 2560x1440, 3 = 3840x2160 from "
    "720p; other values go to the nearest step, and outside 0.5 to 3 to the nearer end). 0, the "
    "default: the screen's -- the window's 16:9 area over the game's 1280x720, followed while the "
    "game runs (fullscreen, a resized window): the picture is drawn at the size of the window "
    "(\"Render Scale 100%\" in the pause menu); above it is supersampling. Not used while a "
    "temporal upscaler (mcla_gpu_upscaler) runs: its output is always the screen's, and the scene "
    "is drawn at its mode's share of that. Not used either while mcla_gpu_fsr is on with a preset "
    "(mcla_gpu_fsr_preset). Live: the images are made again at the new scale at a frame boundary, "
    "once the value has stood for a moment (and, while an upscaler runs, once its context for the "
    "new sizes is ready); a scale whose images the card cannot make (video memory is short) is not "
    "made: the old one is kept, the pause menu's RENDER SCALE row says LIMITED and the log says so. "
    "The guest keeps seeing its own sizes."

mcla_gpu_fsr_preset.help:
"With mcla_gpu_fsr on: the internal resolution scale is the screen's (the window's 16:9 "
    "area over the game's 1280x720, followed while the game runs) divided by an FSR1 quality "
    "ratio -- ultra_quality 1.3, quality 1.5, balanced 1.7, performance 2, ultra_performance 3 -- "
    "on the 0.05 grid and at least 0.5, and FSR1 upscales it to the window. custom: "
    "mcla_gpu_resolution_scale (by default the screen's, which leaves FSR1 nothing to upscale: pick "
    "a preset). With mcla_gpu_fsr off it is not used, nor while a temporal upscaler "
    "(mcla_gpu_upscaler) runs. Live, like mcla_gpu_resolution_scale."

mcla_gpu_lock_dump.help:
"Diagnostic: after a Lock write-back, every 8888 level the locked range "
                    "covers is decoded from guest memory and written as "
                    "mcla_gpu_lock_<serial>_<base>_<w>x<h>_L<level>.tga next to the executable "
                    "(the vinyl's mip chain)."

mcla_gpu_resolve_fill_half_pixel.help:
"With mcla_gpu_resolution_scale above 1, a resolve of a scaled target reads "
                    "its first host columns and rows -- the half-pixel gap no full-screen draw "
                    "covers -- from the first one surely covered, as Xenia's "
                    "resolve_resolution_scale_fill_half_pixel_offset does. Off: "
                    "the gap keeps whatever was there, a 1-pixel line on the top and left "
                    "edges. A/B switch."

mcla_gpu_resolve_7e3_ceiling.help:
"A resolve of a 7e3 colour target (k_2_10_10_10_FLOAT, the 3D scene) clamps "
                    "each sample's red, green and blue to what the console's target holds, as "
                    "Xenia does: 0 to 31.875 as stored, which with the game's exponent bias of 4 "
                    "is a colour of 1.99 at most. The host's float16 target holds far more, "
                    "and the tone map and the bloom then see lights the console never had: a "
                    "red underglow pool is white in the middle instead of pink. Off: no clamp. "
                    "Not applied to a frame that can carry the HDR float scene (HDR output with "
                    "the HDR pack loaded and no FXAA or SMAA running): its tone map wants the "
                    "range. "
                    "A/B switch."

mcla_gpu_lock_ahead_verify.help:
"Diagnostic: a lock whose pages an earlier lock read ahead still reads them from the pool (it "
    "waits for the GPU as before), and the bytes are compared with the ones kept. Reported in the "
    "log with the prefix 'lock read-ahead check:' (an error line for every page that differs, the "
    "first 8). The vinyl editor is where it counts. Off: nothing is done."

mcla_gpu_resolve_memory_encode_delay.help:
"Frames a colour resolve's encode into the resolve memory (and that of a depth resolve into "
    "k_8_8_8_8) may wait. 0: every "
    "encode of a frame is recorded at its end. N: recorded once a reader or writer "
    "of its pages needs it, or after N frames; a resolve that rewrites the same rectangle "
    "replaces it before it runs, so most are never recorded (75% on a drive). 2 by default: on a "
    "Radeon iGPU 57 FPS against 52 at 0. At most 120. Hot reload."

mcla_gpu_resolve_memory_check.help:
"Diagnostic, slow: every encode also runs at once into a second, reference pool (what "
    "mcla_gpu_resolve_memory_encode_delay 0 gives), and at each reader of the real pool (decode, "
    "vertex copy, lock write-back) and for the whole pool every 600 frames the bytes are compared "
    "with it. Reported in the log with the prefix 'resolve memory check:' every 600 frames and "
    "at shutdown (RESULT PASS or FAIL). For wrong or flickering textures that the delayed encode "
    "may cause: the answer is in the log. Off: nothing is done."

mcla_gpu_anisotropy.help:
"Anisotropic texture filtering: game (the game's own fetch constants), off, 2, 4, 8 or 16. "
    "Applies to mipmapped textures whose min, mag and mip filters are all linear. Live."

mcla_gpu_scene_profile.help:
"Diagnostic (M6a): the render thread's time per stage of a draw (constant banks, "
    "state decode, shaders and layout, geometry, pipeline, constants, textures, upload, targets, "
    "draw), one line per window of 600 frames. Off: nothing is timed."

mcla_gpu_target_sig.help: "Debug A/B: memoize draw target scale, samples and depth layer using the target signature. Live."

mcla_gpu_layout_two_way.help: "Debug A/B: keep two recent input layouts, pipeline keys and ready pipelines. Live."

mcla_gpu_work_17oct.help:
"On/off for all of the renderer work of 17/10/2026: the half-pixel fill of "
    "scaled resolves (mcla_gpu_resolve_fill_half_pixel), the depth bias times the scale "
    "(mcla_gpu_scale_depth_bias), the delayed colour encodes "
    "(mcla_gpu_resolve_memory_encode_delay) and the encode batch counters. Off: as before "
    "that day. Hot reload."
comments: // The switch over the renderer work of 17/10/2026, asked for by
// the user, live: on, every part of it runs as its own cvar says; off, the
// renderer does what it did before that day.

mcla_gpu_scale_depth_bias.help:
"With a resolution scale above 1 (M6b.3c): the slope-scaled depth bias times the "
    "scale of the draw's targets, as Xenia does -- a host pixel is 1/scale of the guest's. Off: "
    "the guest's factor unchanged (for A/B). Hot reload."

mcla_gpu_census_scale.help:
"Diagnostic (M6e.0): logs once per case each resolve product a draw at another resolution "
    "scale reads (with the fetch's filters) and each copy of an image of the screen that lands "
    "away from its source. Off: nothing is checked."

mcla_gpu_scene_extra_bias.help:
"While an upscaler draws the scene smaller than it is shown, its textures are sampled by "
    "log2(render size / output size) levels of detail lower, as the output's size would pick, plus "
    "this many levels more. -1 is what AMD's FSR guide asks for (a sharper picture the upscaler "
    "fills in over its jitter); 0 or -0.5 sample blurrier levels, which shimmer less on fine "
    "texture detail (grass, road grain, fences) and soften it. For A/B. Live."
comments: // The scene's extra texture detail bias under an upscaler (Scene::SceneBias): live, for A/B.

mcla_gpu_upscaler_masks.help:
"Whether the upscalers get the reactive mask (the cars' shadow decals, particles, light "
    "volumes) and the transparency and composition mask (car glass): on, they are drawn "
    "(upscaler_masks.h). Off: no mask is made and the upscaler trusts its history everywhere, "
    "for A/B (a mask that is wrong shows as shimmer where it covers). Live."

mcla_cam_cut_blur_fix.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT (for A/B pictures): on a frame where the scene's camera cuts, the game's motion blur "
    "gets this frame's own matrices as the previous frame's, so it does not smear the frame (E5: the first frame "
    "after a cut). Off: the game's constants as they are."

shader_pack_dir.help:
"The folder the shader packs (mcla_shaders.v8.pack and mcla_shaders_variants.v3.pack) are read from "
    "and built into. Empty: the cache/shaders folder next to the program or, where that folder "
    "cannot be written to, larecomp/cache/shaders in the local application data folder; a pack "
    "left in the program's assets folder by an older install is still used when there is none "
    "in that folder. When this is set, only this folder is used."

mcla_gpu_shadow_filter.help:
"How the sun's shadows are filtered: game (the game's own: four taps at an angle that changes from "
    "pixel to pixel, a grainy edge), soft (more taps on a disk, a "
    "smooth edge without grain, of the same width as the game's, or narrower on a finer shadow map: SHADOW DETAIL), pcss (soft, with "
    "contact hardening: a shadow is sharp where it touches what casts it and softer with the distance "
    "from it, as the sun's own shadows are; an integrated graphics card gets soft). auto (the default) "
    "picks by the graphics card: game on an integrated one, pcss on the rest. Your car's own shadow "
    "(CAR SHADOW MAP) is filtered the same way. The sun's shadows show from "
    "8 to 17 hours in clear weather. Costs graphics card time in the screen's shadowed pixels (pcss "
    "about the same as soft: away from the edges it takes fewer taps). Live; the first time soft or pcss "
    "shows, the graphics card builds its shaders (a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_shadow_filter_taps.help:
"Diagnostic: how many taps the soft shadow filter takes, 4 to 32. 0: by the graphics card (8 on an "
    "integrated one, 16 on the rest). Live."

mcla_gpu_shadow_filter_radius.help:
"Diagnostic: how wide the soft shadow filter is, as a multiple of the game's own filter measured in "
    "texels of the shadow map (1: the edge of a shadow takes the same number of shadow map texels, so "
    "the same width as the game's on its own 1280x1280 map, half as wide on high and a third on ultra: "
    "mcla_gpu_shadow_resolution). Live."

mcla_gpu_shadow_filter_sun.help:
"Diagnostic: how big the sun is for the contact hardening of pcss, as a multiple of its real angular "
    "radius (0.27 degrees). 1 is the real sun, whose penumbra is narrower than one texel of the shadow map "
    "for anything lower than about 3 metres, so a shadow is sharp everywhere; a larger sun makes the "
    "edge of the shadow of a car or a pole visibly softer with the distance from what casts it (the "
    "width is capped at twice the soft filter's). Live."

mcla_gpu_shadow_filter_pcf.help:
"Diagnostic: how a tap of the soft shadow filter reads the shadow map. On: "
    "it compares the four texels one by one at the receiver's own slope and blends the answers (a true "
    "percentage-closer tap): the shadow edge is smooth, without the grain of one compare of a blended depth. "
    "Off: with the game's own sampler, which compares a depth blended from four texels (what the game's four "
    "taps do): a grainy edge, as the game's. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts.help:
"Sun shafts: a low sun behind trees and buildings streams light across the scene, as light "
    "through a haze. They show at dawn and dusk (strongest between 2.5 and 27 degrees of sun "
    "height, none by day above 45 degrees, none at night or in rain) and only while the sun is on "
    "the screen or not far beyond its edge. The value is how strong they are: off is the game's own "
    "picture, then light, default, strong, stronger and strongest (1x to 5x the built-in strength; default is 2x). "
    "auto (the default) is default on a discrete graphics card and off on an integrated one (a "
    "handheld, or the iGPU of a desktop CPU). The ray quality follows the card by itself. low and high "
    "are values of an older version and mean default. Costs graphics card time only while they show. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_intensity.help:
"Diagnostic: a fine multiplier on the strength mcla_gpu_sun_shafts gives the sun shafts (1 is "
    "the level as it is). Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_steps.help:
"Diagnostic: how many steps each ray of the sun shafts marches (8 to 128). 0: by the graphics "
    "card (32 on a mid-range one, 64 on a fast one). More steps make smoother rays and cost more; "
    "the light the rays gather stays the same. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_density.help:
"Diagnostic: how much of the way to the sun each ray of the sun shafts covers, 0.3 to 1 "
    "(1: all of it). Longer rays are longer streaks; shorter ones stay near the sun. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_threshold.help:
"Diagnostic: the brightness (the scene's linear light, 1 is white) the sky must pass to light "
    "the sun shafts; what is under it does not shine. Lower lets more of the sky shine. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_sky_depth.help:
"Diagnostic: the stored depth (1 near, 0 far) at or under which a pixel is sky for the sun "
    "shafts. The sky is drawn at the far end, 0; raise it if the shafts find no sky. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_view.help:
"Diagnostic: shows a stage of the sun shafts instead of adding them (only while they are on "
    "and the sun gives shafts): 1 the sky image the rays march over, 2 the blurred image, 3 the "
    "added light alone. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_early.help:
"Diagnostic: adds the sun shafts at the game's mid-scene depth copy, before the fog and the "
    "particles, instead of at the game's copy of the main colour after them (the fog then covers "
    "them), to compare the two. Without it the shafts go in at that copy and fall back to the "
    "mid-scene point by themselves when no such copy comes. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_cap.help:
"Diagnostic: caps the sun shafts' two working images at 960x540 (the size they are at 1080p, a quarter "
    "of their old size at 4K, the same shape as the picture; a picture whose half size is under that is "
    "untouched). The shafts are a smooth, blurred light, so the picture is the same to within the ray "
    "noise being coarser; it saves a good part of the passes' time at 1440p and 4K while the shafts "
    "show. False: the images are half the picture's size, as they were. Live."

mcla_gpu_sun_shafts_census.help:
"Diagnostic: every Nth guest frame (and the first three frames with the main view), one log "
    "line of what the sun shafts did: the sun's height and where it is in the picture, the "
    "fades, what became of the frame's two points. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_env_resolution.help:
"How sharp the reflections in the paint, windows and bonnet of the cars are: the game draws the "
    "world around the car as a 512x256 picture for them to reflect, which is why the reflections look "
    "soft up close. game (the game's own 512x256), high (1024x512), ultra (1536x768), or auto (game on "
    "an integrated graphics chip or a card with less than about 6 GB of memory, high on any other card). "
    "Costs a little graphics card time and video memory (about 4 MiB for high, 16 MiB for ultra). Live."

mcla_gpu_reflection_resolution.help:
"How sharp the road reflection is: the wet roads, the shop and building windows and the water "
    "show a mirror image of the city that the game draws at 256x256 and stretches over the whole "
    "screen, which is why it looks soft. game (the game's own 256x256), high (512x512), ultra "
    "(768x768), or auto (game on an integrated graphics chip, high on any other card). Costs a "
    "little graphics card time and video memory (about 4 MiB for high, 13 MiB for ultra). Live."

mcla_gpu_reflection_scale.help:
"Diagnostic: the road reflection's size as a multiple of the game's 256x256 (any step of 0.05), "
    "instead of what mcla_gpu_reflection_resolution says. 0: the setting's. Live."

mcla_gpu_shadow_resolution.help:
"How fine the sun's shadows can be: the game draws them into four 640x640 maps in one 1280x1280 "
    "picture, which limits how sharp an edge can get. game (the game's own 1280x1280), high "
    "(2560x2560), ultra (3840x3840), or auto (game on an integrated graphics chip, high on any other "
    "card). With SHADOW FILTER on soft the edge of a shadow is half as wide on high and a third as "
    "wide on ultra; with the game's own filter it keeps its width and gets smoother. Costs a little "
    "graphics card time and video memory (about 25 MiB for high, 56 MiB for ultra, and as much again "
    "for the maps being drawn). The sun's shadows show from 8 to 17 hours in clear weather. Live; "
    "the first time it changes the graphics card builds its shaders (a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_side_mirrors.help: "The car's two side mirrors without ray tracing: the game's own rear view mirror camera is drawn once into a small picture of its own, and the glass of both side mirrors (and the HUD's rear view mirror, when it is on) show that picture, so a mirror shows the street and the cars behind you instead of the game's blurred sky, mostly in the first person cameras (cockpit, bumper), where the glass is big enough to read. auto picks by graphics card: off on integrated graphics (the game's own mirrors), high on a mid range card and ultra on a fast one. high draws the picture 512 pixels wide every second frame, ultra 768 pixels wide every frame (sharper, costs more); off keeps the game's own mirrors. Where RT SIDE MIRRORS is on (a graphics card that can ray trace) it takes the place of this setting. The pause menu's row is GRAPHICS, REFLECTIONS, SIDE MIRRORS. Live."

mcla_gpu_split.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: a before/after split in one frame. A position from 0 to 1 across the picture's width: the effects "
    "named by mcla_gpu_split_effects (ambient occlusion, the present's dither) are applied only left of it, and right of "
    "it the picture is drawn without them. -1 is off (the default; nothing changes and nothing costs), 1 is the effect "
    "everywhere. A scene's `split <a>..<b> over <s>` keys write it; a compositor draws the divider line. Live."

mcla_gpu_split_effects.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: which effects mcla_gpu_split cuts: ao (ambient occlusion only), dither (the present's dither only) "
    "or all. An effect that is off in its own setting stays off. Used only while mcla_gpu_split is on. Live."

mcla_gpu_volumetrics.help:
"Volumetric light: beams of light under the street lamps and the cars' headlights, a haze that light shows in, "
    "and the sun's shafts between trees and buildings (through the game's own shadow cascades). It is a camera "
    "aligned volume lit by compute passes and added to the scene once, so it costs the same whatever is on screen: "
    "medium, high or ultra grow the volume and the number of lamps and headlights it lights. off is the game's own "
    "picture (its fog, and in rain its cone meshes under the lamps). auto (the default) is medium on a mid-range "
    "graphics card, high on a fast one and off on an integrated one. Nothing is added by day in clear weather with "
    "no light on. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_census.help:
"Diagnostic: every Nth guest frame (and the first three frames with the main view), one log line of what the "
    "volumetric light did: what became of the frame, the collector's atlas, the fog quad's colour. 0: off. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_keep_cones.help:
"Diagnostic: draws the game's own cone meshes under the lamps (xrage_spotlightfog, in rain) as well as the "
    "volumetric light, to compare the two. Without it the cones are not drawn in a frame the volume was made. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_density.help:
"Diagnostic: a multiplier on the haze's thickness the volumetric light uses (the look's own: 0.0012 per metre in a clear night, "
    "0.008 in rain, 0.010 in fog; 1: as the look has it). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_ground_height.help:
"Diagnostic: a multiplier on the scale height of the thicker haze above the ground in the volumetric light (40: as the look has it, 0: no "
    "ground layer). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_ground_strength.help:
"Diagnostic: a multiplier on how much thicker the look makes the haze at the ground than high above it (1: as the look has it, 0: "
    "none). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_noise.help:
"Diagnostic: how much the haze's thickness varies from place to place in the volumetric light (0: even, 1: "
    "patches of clear air). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_wind.help: "Diagnostic: how fast, in metres a second, the haze's patches drift in the volumetric light. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_g_sun.help:
"Diagnostic: a multiplier on how strongly the look makes the haze scatter the sun forward (0.6: as the look has it; the look's value is 0.6 to 0.72, 0: evenly, toward 0.95: only toward the camera when "
    "looking at the sun). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_g_lamp.help: "Diagnostic: a multiplier on how strongly the look makes the haze scatter a street lamp's light forward (0.25: as the look has it). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_g_head.help: "Diagnostic: a multiplier on how strongly the look makes the haze scatter a car's headlight forward (0.6: as the look has it; oncoming lights glare in fog). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_lamp_strength.help: "Diagnostic: a multiplier on the street lamps' light in the volumetric light. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_head_strength.help: "Diagnostic: a multiplier on the cars' headlights' light in the volumetric light. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_sun_strength.help: "Diagnostic: a multiplier on the sun's light in the volumetric light. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_extinction.help:
"Diagnostic: a multiplier on how much of the haze's own dimming the volumetric light applies to the picture (0.25: as the look has it; 0: it only adds "
    "light, 1: the full physical amount; the game's own fog dims the distance already). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_far.help:
"Diagnostic: how far in metres the volumetric light reaches (30 to the level's own, 120 on medium and 160 on "
    "high and ultra). 0: the level's. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_temporal.help:
"Diagnostic: blends each frame's volume with the last frame's, moved to where the camera is now (high and "
    "ultra; medium has none). Off: the volume shows its noise. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_early.help:
"Diagnostic: adds the volumetric light at the game's mid-scene depth copy, before the fog and the particles, "
    "instead of at the game's copy of the main colour after them, to compare the two. Without it the light goes in "
    "at that copy and falls back to the mid-scene point by itself when no such copy comes. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_test.help:
"Diagnostic: adds a test light to the volumetric light, where the camera looks, to see its beams without the game's own "
    "lights: 1 a street lamp 8 m ahead and 4.5 m up (the game's street lamps are then not read), 2 a headlight (the rig's "
    "headlights are then not read), 3 both. A test light also keeps the haze at least 0.004 thick. 0: none. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_inputs.help:
"Diagnostic: which of the game's lights the volumetric light reads: 1 the street lamps (the game's per-frame lamp list), "
    "2 the cars' headlights (the headlight rig's lights and, where the shadow maps run, their shadows), 3 both (the default), "
    "0 neither. A bit that mcla_gpu_vol_test uses for a test light is left to the test light. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_lamp_limit.help:
"Diagnostic: at most this many of the game's street lamps are put in the volumetric light (the brightest in view are "
    "kept, with hysteresis); 0: as many as the level reads (12 on medium, 32 on high, 48 on ultra). Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_stable.help:
"Diagnostic: keeps the volumetric light steady in motion: a street lamp's glow is averaged over each slice of the "
    "light's grid instead of sampled once at a random place in it (so it no longer pulses as the camera moves and the history no longer has "
    "noise to average), a pixel at an edge of depth looks the light up at every sample of the picture's anti-aliasing instead of the first, "
    "the history's weight follows time, not the frame count, the lamps fade in a real 0.35 s whatever the frame rate, a shadowed headlight takes three taps of its "
    "shadow map along each cell of the grid, the history's beam follows a car's headlights where they moved, and a frame whose camera is not known takes the previous one moved on by its "
    "last step. False: the first version. Live."

mcla_gpu_vol_view.help:
"Diagnostic: 1 shows only the light the volumetric light adds, in place of the picture (to see or measure how steady "
    "it is), 2 the same eight times brighter, 3 thirty-two times brighter (for the faint headlights), 0 the picture. The bloom and the tone map still follow it. Live."

mcla_gpu_lights_census.help:
"Diagnostic (the one light description, LIGHT-UNIFY U2): every guest frame the light manager collects the headlight rig's lights, the "
    "headlight shadow maps and the volumetric light's street lamps into one frame of lights, checks it against what the lit shaders' headlight block and the volumetric "
    "light's inputs hold, and uploads it; nothing reads it, so the picture does not change. Every Nth guest frame one log line says what was collected and how many "
    "checks found a difference. 0: off (the manager is not called). Live."

mcla_gpu_local_lights.help:
"Diagnostic (the deferred local light pass, LIGHT-UNIFY GB-H1; off until the lamp A/B is judged): at the game's mid-scene depth copy, after the ambient occlusion, one draw per light adds "
    "the light to the main colour from the G-buffer's normal, albedo and lit weight and the depth, in the city's units (a lamp here is a lamp of the game's own light grid: "
    "mcla_gpu_local_lights_ab holds one lamp through both to compare them). While it is on the main view's draws also write the G-buffer's normal and albedo (a small cost, paid only then). "
    "Which lights it adds is mcla_gpu_local_lights_sources and mcla_gpu_local_lights_ab; with both at 0 it adds none. Not in the 4x views behind the pause menu and the map, nor in a cutscene. Live."

mcla_gpu_local_lights_sources.help:
"Diagnostic (the deferred local light pass, GB-H1 and GB-H3): which lights it adds besides the lamps mcla_gpu_local_lights_ab hands it. A sum: 1 the lights of the frame that add surface light and "
    "that the game's own shaders do not already light with (today the cars' headlights, which the forward headlight stage lights as well: the two add, so use it with HEADLIGHTS off), "
    "2 a test lamp 8 m ahead of the camera and 4.5 m up, 4 the police light bars (the game's own flash), 8 the headlights of the cars the forward headlight stage does not light, "
    "16 the cars' brake, tail, turn and reverse lamps, 32 the lamps of a mod's lights.bin that the game's grid is not lighting (the camera is outside the mod's rectangle). The cars' and mods' classes "
    "have a budget each that grows with the LIGHT SHADOWS level, 32 lights in all. 0: only the A/B's lamps. Live."

mcla_gpu_local_lights_ab.help:
"Diagnostic (the lamp A/B of the deferred local light pass, GB-H1): what happens to the lamps of a mod's lights.bin (mod_lights.cpp; while the camera is over the mod's rectangle the game lights the scene "
    "with that lamp set alone). 0: the game's own light grid lights them (A). 2: the grid is built with them off and the local light pass adds the same lamps (B; needs mcla_gpu_local_lights). "
    "1: neither (the control: A and B each minus the control are the lamp's own light in each path). Read when the city's lights are loaded: it applies at the next start."

mcla_gpu_local_lights_gain.help:
"Diagnostic (the deferred local light pass, GB-H1): a multiplier on the light the pass adds (1: the game's units as read: the lamp's colour times the night light intensity and the height factor of the lit "
    "shaders). The lamp A/B says whether 1 is right. Live."

mcla_gpu_local_lights_car_gain.help:
"Diagnostic (the deferred local light pass, GB-H3): a multiplier on the look of the cars' lights it adds (the police light bars, the head lamps of the cars the forward headlight stage does not light, "
    "the brake, tail, turn and reverse lamps). Their colours and strengths are looks set by eye, not the game's units: this turns them up or down without a build. Live."

mcla_gpu_lamp_shadows.help:
"Diagnostic (the street lamps' shadows, LAMP-SHADOWS-4): the nearest street lamps get a shadow from the shadow atlas (cars, poles and people on the road under them), drawn by the deferred local light pass "
    "at the mid-scene depth copy with the same lookup as the headlights'. -1 (the default): they follow the LIGHT SHADOWS row - while the deferred local light pass runs for anything else (mcla_gpu_local_lights on, or "
    "mcla_gpu_headlight_pass pass or both) and LIGHT SHADOWS is not off, the lamps have a shadow, how many by its level (medium 2, high 4, ultra 8; Auto: Low off, Mid medium, High ultra). 0: none. 1: on whatever "
    "the pass's own settings say (the pass runs for the lamps). The shadow replay records into the shared atlas while it is on. Live. See mcla_gpu_lamp_shadows_mode for how the pass uses the shadow."

mcla_gpu_lamp_shadows_mode.help:
"Diagnostic (the street lamps' shadows): how the deferred local light pass uses a lamp's shadow. 0 (the default): subtract - the game's own light grid still lights the lamp and the pass takes the "
    "shadowed share of that light away (the lamp's light as the grid has it, times one minus the visibility), for every surface the G-buffer holds, cars and people included. 1: own - the lamp is not in "
    "the grid (the lamp A/B's mod lamps) and the pass adds its light times the visibility. Live."

mcla_gpu_lamp_shadows_view.help:
"Diagnostic (the street lamps' shadows): what the deferred local light pass draws for a shadowed street lamp instead of its light. 0 (the default): the light. 1: the shadow itself as a picture, red "
    "where the lamp's shadow takes light and green where it is lit. 2: a colour for each lamp's row of the shadow table (brighter in the shadow), which shows the pick and its hysteresis. 3: the lamp's whole light is taken away whatever the shadow (the units check: the pool must go to the ambient and no pixel may go negative). Live."

mcla_gpu_lamp_shadows_lamps.help:
"Diagnostic (the street lamps' shadows): how many lamps have a shadow at once. 0 (the default): the LIGHT SHADOWS level's number. A number from 1 to 10: that many (with a spare tile for a lamp whose "
    "shadow fades out). -1: no lamp (the headlights keep their views). Live."

mcla_gpu_lamp_shadows_cache.help:
"Diagnostic (the street lamps' shadows): 1 (the default) gives each lamp two tiles, a static one for the world that does not move (drawn when the lamp takes its tile and added to, kept) and a live one "
    "for the cars and people (drawn every frame), which costs one more tile of video memory a lamp and saves the world's draws. 0: one tile a lamp, everything drawn every frame. Live."

mcla_gpu_neon_light_gain.help:
"Diagnostic (a car's neon underglow in the deferred local light pass, GB-NEON-TUNE): a multiplier on the neon's light. 1 is the tuned underglow: the game's neon colour as a hue, its pulse and "
    "fade as a strength, a radiant intensity of about 2.3 street lamps at 1 m facing the tube, fading to nothing at the reach; 0 puts the light out, 2 is twice as strong. Live."

mcla_gpu_neon_light_reach.help:
"Diagnostic (a car's neon underglow in the deferred local light pass, GB-NEON-TUNE): a scale on how far the neon's light reaches (1: 5 / 5.5 / 6 m by the LIGHT SHADOWS level; the light fades "
    "smoothly to nothing there, and the pass's reach test, its draw rectangle and its culling use the same distance). The pictures' softer and stronger arms use 0.8 and 1.3. Live."

mcla_gpu_neon_light_tuned.help: "Diagnostic (a car's neon underglow in the deferred local light pass, GB-NEON-TUNE, the A/B): on (the default) the light is the retuned one (the game's colour as a hue and a strength, a "

mcla_gpu_local_lights_cost_off.help:
"Diagnostic (the cost of the deferred local light pass, GB-NEON-COST, the A/B): a sum of the savings to switch OFF so that the pass runs as it did before them. "
    "1 the reach test before the planes are read (the pixel shader asks the depth whether any light of the draw reaches the pixel, and leaves the pixels none reaches without reading the G-buffer's three planes), "
    "2 one draw for a car's neon tube (its two to four lights are summed in the shader: one pass over the picture where there were one for each light), "
    "4 the cap of the neon contact term's reads (a pixel of a tube of three or four lights marches the depth for the two strongest lights only, the others take the nearest one's answer: up to 10 depth reads a vehicle pixel where each light marching for itself made up to 20). "
    "0, the default: all on. The picture is the same either way up to the rounding of the half float colour target for the first two (they leave out only what adds nothing). The third moves a few percent of the light of a vehicle pixel the contact term shuts partly. Only the graphics card time differs otherwise. Live."

mcla_gpu_neon_contact.help:
"Diagnostic (a car's neon underglow in the deferred local light pass, GB-NEON-BLEED, the A/B): on (the default) a neon light is shut out of the car's own panels on a vehicle pixel: the light's way to the pixel is looked up in the picture's own depth for 0.8 m and a point behind a visible surface by a shell's thickness is inside something, so the vents, the lip, the cabin and the wheels' dish that face the light through a body get none of it. "
    "Off: the law's N.L alone (the neon shows through the other car's panels). Live."

mcla_gpu_gi_bounce_headlights.help: "Diagnostic (the ray traced bounce light's emitters, GI-BOUNCE-RT, perf/GI-BOUNCE.md, the A/B of one source group): on (the default) the light of the frame's surface lights (the headlight rig's lights of the cars it lights) and the head lamps of the cars it does not also bounces: what a ray of the RT bounce light hits (the probe field's rays for the lights that stand still, the per-pixel pass's for all of them, the reflections' city hits) is lit by it, by the same laws and units as the deferred light pass lights the picture with. Off: this group is not gathered and does not bounce through ray tracing. Live."

mcla_gpu_gi_bounce_neon.help: "Diagnostic (the ray traced bounce light's emitters, GI-BOUNCE-RT, perf/GI-BOUNCE.md, the A/B of one source group): on (the default) the light of the cars' neon underglow tubes (it also needs NEON LIGHT on, which is what makes the game's neon table fill) also bounces: what a ray of the RT bounce light hits (the probe field's rays for the lights that stand still, the per-pixel pass's for all of them, the reflections' city hits) is lit by it, by the same laws and units as the deferred light pass lights the picture with. Off: this group is not gathered and does not bounce through ray tracing. Live."

mcla_gpu_gi_bounce_rear.help: "Diagnostic (the ray traced bounce light's emitters, GI-BOUNCE-RT, perf/GI-BOUNCE.md, the A/B of one source group): on (the default) the light of the cars' brake, tail, turn signal and reverse lamps also bounces: what a ray of the RT bounce light hits (the probe field's rays for the lights that stand still, the per-pixel pass's for all of them, the reflections' city hits) is lit by it, by the same laws and units as the deferred light pass lights the picture with. Off: this group is not gathered and does not bounce through ray tracing. Live."

mcla_gpu_gi_bounce_other.help: "Diagnostic (the ray traced bounce light's emitters, GI-BOUNCE-RT, perf/GI-BOUNCE.md, the A/B of one source group): on (the default) the light of the police light bars and the mods' lamps outside their grid also bounces: what a ray of the RT bounce light hits (the probe field's rays for the lights that stand still, the per-pixel pass's for all of them, the reflections' city hits) is lit by it, by the same laws and units as the deferred light pass lights the picture with. Off: this group is not gathered and does not bounce through ray tracing. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_pass.help:
"Diagnostic (the forward headlight stage against the deferred local light pass, GB-H2, the A/B): which of the two lights the cars' headlights. forward (the default): the lit shaders' headlight variant lights, as the game has always had it. "
    "pass: the deferred local light pass lights the headlights of the same cars with their shadows from the atlas (it also reaches the lit shaders the variant leaves out, the cars' paint and the pedestrians; needs the G-buffer's planes, which it asks for while HEADLIGHTS is on, and runs whatever mcla_gpu_local_lights says), and the variant stays only on the draws the pass does not light (mcla_gpu_headlight_pass_keep_forward). "
    "both: the variant lights and the pass adds the same lights again (the sum of the two: for the difference pictures). HEADLIGHTS (mcla_gpu_headlights) stays the master of both. Live."

mcla_gpu_headlight_pass_keep_forward.help:
"Diagnostic (the forward headlight stage against the deferred local light pass, GB-H2, the A/B of the headlight route pass): in the route pass the lit shaders' headlight variant stays on the draws the deferred pass does not light "
    "(the neon, the store sign and the lamp glass, which the pass skips as emissive; a draw the G-buffer does not carry, such as a pipeline still being made or a view that is not the main one; a draw that clears the planes), so what is "
    "in the beam is not left dark; the draws the pass does light drop it, so a pixel is lit once. Off: the route pass takes the variant away from every draw, as the first version did (what the pass does not light gets no headlight). No "
    "effect in the routes forward and both. Live."

mcla_gpu_light_pick.help:
"Diagnostic (the one picker of the lights, LIGHT-UNIFY U3): how the lights are picked. unified (the default): the headlight rig's four lights and the "
    "cars that get shadow views are picked by one rule (how much of a beam is in the view, the distance, a place kept by the one that holds it), with every "
    "fade, linger and coast counted in seconds of the scene clock, so that a light fades in the same time at 30, 60 and 144 frames a second. legacy: the "
    "first code of the two pickers (frames counted at the game's pace), to compare with: at 60 frames a second the two pick the same lights with the same "
    "weights. Live."

mcla_gpu_light_pick_record.help:
"Diagnostic (the one picker of the lights, LIGHT-UNIFY U3): a file path. With it, the headlight rig writes every guest frame's inputs of its tracker "
    "(the cars its lens draws showed, the camera's view) to <path>.rig.txt and the headlight shadow replay writes the inputs of its pick of cars (the rig's "
    "lights, the cap, the context) to <path>.views.txt, in the text format of light_pick_record.h, for the unit test light_pick_test to replay through both "
    "pickers. Empty: nothing is written. Live; changing the path starts new files."

mcla_gpu_light_frame.help:
"Diagnostic (the one light description, LIGHT-UNIFY U4, the A/B of the flips): which consumers read the light manager's frame of lights instead of their own producer. "
    "A bit mask: 1 the lit shaders' headlight block, 2 the volumetric light's street lamps, headlights and shadow views, 4 the lights the headlight shadow maps pick cars "
    "and make views from; 7 all three; 8 (LIGHT-UNIFY U5) the headlight shadow maps are recorded into the one shared shadow atlas (its layout, clear, the one barrier for the pixel and compute readers, memory fitted to the video memory budget) and the frame's shadow views are read from its published form by light id; 15 all four. 0 (the default until the runs have shown the bytes equal): every consumer reads its own producer, as before. The data a flipped "
