    "consumer gets is byte for byte what its own producer made (mcla_gpu_lights_census checks it every frame while it is on, and says so in its line), so the picture "
    "does not change. Live."

mcla_gpu_sync_builds.help:
"Trailer toolkit (M2d): while on, nothing is left out for a pipeline that is still being made. "
    "A draw whose pipeline a builder thread has not finished (\"skipped [pipeline pending ...]\" in "
    "the scene lines), and the second draws of the HDR scene and the upscaler masks, wait for it "
    "on the render thread instead, so no frame of a recording misses an object. The frames that "
    "make a new pipeline are slow while it is on. The log counts the waits and their time "
    "(\"[gpu] capture sync\"). Capture mode turns the same switch on by itself while it records. "
    "Off: as before. Live."

mcla_gpu_pause_vehicle_vectors.help:
"Diagnostic: in the pause menu's world, the garage and the map, take the game's own per-vehicle motion for a "
    "vehicle's pixels in the temporal upscalers' motion vectors, as in the game view. Off (the default): a vehicle "
    "there takes the camera's motion like the world (a car in the garage is still while the camera orbits it, and "
    "the game's slots for the vehicles are not trusted in those frames). Live."

mcla_gpu_temporal_jitter_hold.help:
"Diagnostic: hold the temporal upscalers' sub-pixel jitter at zero while the history restarts in every frame (a "
    "camera the cut rule or the game's previous-matrix test cannot follow): a frame resolved from one frame is "
    "steadier unjittered. Off: the jitter goes on as before. Live."

mcla_gpu_upscaler_zero_jitter.help:
"While FSR or DLSS draws the scene: no sub-pixel jitter at all. The projection is not moved and "
    "the upscaler is told a jitter of 0 (one value, so the draws, the motion vectors and the upscaler "
    "agree). The upscaler then has no sub-pixel samples to rebuild detail from and the picture is "
    "no sharper than the render size; a flicker that follows the jitter phase is gone with it, one "
    "that stays is not the jitter's. For A/B. Live."
comments: // Test levers for the static-scene flicker analysis (debug only, live, never saved; defaults = the
// behaviour without them).

mcla_gpu_upscaler_post_reads_output.help:
"While FSR or DLSS draws the scene at the output's size (FSR's Native AA, DLAA): the game's post "
    "chain before the upscale (the half-size downsample that the bloom's bright pass, the exposure "
    "and the motion blur's half-size layer are made from) reads the previous frame's upscaled "
    "picture, as it does at every other mode (on, the default since 2026-11-14: measured on a still "
    "pause view with FSR Native AA, flat areas 8x and the distant tower 3x steadier). Off: the old "
    "path, the raw jittered scene at that size, kept for A/B. Live."

mcla_gpu_upscaler_lazy_load.help:
"Debug (A/B): load the upscalers' libraries only when they are needed. On (the default): "
    "AMD's FidelityFX runtime (amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_*.dll, 35 to 55 MiB) is opened when an FSR "
    "is first used, not at every start (an AMD graphics card still asks it at the start, because "
    "only the runtime can say whether FSR 4 is offered), and NVIDIA's Streamline and DLSS (D3D12 on "
    "an RTX card) start their background warm-up only once the pause menu's UPSCALING row has been "
    "shown or DLSS frame generation is chosen, not five seconds after every start; DLSS and FSR "
    "chosen at the start load at the start as always. Off: the old behaviour, FidelityFX opened by "
    "every start and the DLSS warm-up five seconds after the game first draws. Read at the start."

mcla_gpu_upscaler.help:
"Upscaling of the 3D scene: off, fsr31 (AMD FSR 3.1), fsr4 (AMD FSR 4, only where the "
    "graphics card and driver run it) or dlss (NVIDIA DLSS, only on an NVIDIA RTX card, with "
    "NVIDIA's files next to the game). The scene is moved by a different sub-pixel amount every "
    "frame and the upscaler rebuilds a sharper, steadier picture from the frames; the menus, the "
    "HUD and the bloom, glow and tone map stay at full size. The picture it makes is the size of "
    "the window (its 16:9 area), whatever mcla_gpu_resolution_scale says, and the scene is drawn "
    "at the mode's share of that. While one is on, FXAA and SMAA are "
    "held off and MSAA is 1 sample (your MSAA choice, mcla_gpu_msaa, is kept and comes back when "
    "the upscaler is off). A choice this PC cannot run is treated as off. Live: turning an "
    "upscaler on, off or to another one is made at a frame boundary once the new one is ready, "
    "while the old one keeps working (FSR in about half a "
    "second, DLSS in several seconds). The exception is DLSS on Vulkan: that graphics device is "
    "made through NVIDIA's Streamline only when dlss is the saved choice at the start (it adds "
    "several seconds to every start), so choosing dlss in a Vulkan game started with something "
    "else is saved and applies at the next start, and the menu offers a restart. Until then the "
    "game keeps what it runs (the upscaler and its mode as they were, or none), it is not turned "
    "off."

mcla_gpu_fsr31_mode.help:
"FSR 3.1's mode, AMD's names and the share of the output the scene is drawn at: native_aa "
    "(100%, only smoothed), quality (67%), balanced (59%), performance (50%) or ultra_performance "
    "(33%), per direction, of the output (the window's 16:9 area, whatever "
    "mcla_gpu_resolution_scale says). Live: the scene is drawn at the new size from a frame "
    "boundary once the upscaler is ready for it, and the old mode works until then."

mcla_gpu_fsr4_mode.help:
"FSR 4's mode, AMD's names and the share of the output the scene is drawn at: native_aa "
    "(100%, only smoothed), quality (67%), balanced (59%), performance (50%) or ultra_performance "
    "(33%), per direction, of the output (the window's 16:9 area, whatever "
    "mcla_gpu_resolution_scale says). Live: the scene is drawn at the new size from a frame "
    "boundary once the upscaler is ready for it, and the old mode works until then."

mcla_gpu_vendor_denoiser.help:
"The pause menu's DLSS RAY RECONSTRUCTION row (a GeForce RTX card) or AMD FSR RAY REGENERATION row (a Radeon RX 9000 series card on Windows 11): "
    "the graphics card maker's denoiser, who cleans the grain out of the noisy effects (the reflections on surfaces, the ray traced reflections, the ray traced bounce light). Other cards have no such row and use our own denoisers. "
    "Off (the default): our own denoisers. On: NVIDIA's DLSS Ray Reconstruction (it does the upscaling too, in place of DLSS Super Resolution, for the frames it takes, so it needs DLSS as the upscaler) or "
    "AMD's FSR Ray Regeneration (Direct3D 12; it cleans before the upscaler runs, whatever the upscaler is), wherever an effect that it can clean is on and this PC can run it. "
    "A switch is live and the frames in between are the upscaler's own; only DLSS Ray Reconstruction's plugin is loaded when the game starts, so turning it on in a game that started with it off asks for a restart. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_denoiser.help:
"Debug (A/B): overrides the pause menu's DLSS RAY RECONSTRUCTION / AMD FSR RAY REGENERATION row (mcla_gpu_vendor_denoiser): who cleans the grain out of the noisy effects (the reflections on surfaces, the ray traced reflections, the ray traced bounce light): NVIDIA's DLSS Ray Reconstruction (RTX cards), AMD FSR Ray Regeneration (Radeon RX 9000 series cards, Direct3D 12), or our own denoisers. "
    "row (the default): the row decides (ON is the vendor's denoiser, OFF is ours). "
    "auto: the vendor's denoiser where an effect that is on looks better with it and this PC can run it (nothing is trusted to auto yet, so auto is our own denoisers today). "
    "rr (DLSS RR / FSR RAY REGEN in the old menu): the vendor's denoiser wherever it can run and an effect that it can clean is on. ours: our own denoisers only; Streamline is then started without the Ray Reconstruction plugin, "
    "so leaving ours needs a restart. DLSS Ray Reconstruction does the upscaling too, in place of DLSS Super Resolution, for the frames it takes (not the pause menu's world, the garage, the map or a cutscene); its context is made in the background "
    "beside Super Resolution's, so a switch of this setting is live and the frames in between are Super Resolution's. AMD FSR Ray Regeneration cleans the reflections on surfaces before the upscaler runs, whatever the upscaler is, "
    "and needs no restart (AMD's runtime is opened when the setting asks for it). Live; only the plugin is chosen when Streamline starts (the debug setting mcla_gpu_dlss_rr overrides it)."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr.help:
"Debug (A/B): overrides the DLSS RAY RECONSTRUCTION row (mcla_gpu_vendor_denoiser, and the debug chooser mcla_gpu_denoiser) for NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction (RR), a denoiser and upscaler in one that replaces DLSS "
    "Super Resolution where our effects leave noise it can clean (perf/DLSS-RR.md). auto (the default): the row decides. off: nothing of it exists whatever the row says: the plugin is not asked for and nothing changes. probe: Streamline is started with the RR plugin (an RTX "
    "card, sl.dlss_d.dll and nvngx_dlssd.dll next to the exe) and the log says whether this card and driver support it and which sizes it takes, but no frame uses it. on: RR is chosen as the row turned on would choose it, "
    "and without the row's rule that an effect it can clean is on (RR over a frame with nothing to denoise, for the A/B and cost runs), which the log says each time the choice changes and why not. While it is chosen, Ray Reconstruction's context is made in the background beside Super Resolution's, which keeps upscaling the frames meanwhile and every frame "
    "Ray Reconstruction cannot take (the pause, garage and map worlds, cutscenes, frames without guides); the switch between them is live and never restarts. Read at the start (Streamline's plugins are chosen when "
    "it starts; on Vulkan only when DLSS is the saved upscaler)."

mcla_gpu_ray_regen.help: "Debug (AMD FSR Ray Regeneration, perf/RAY-REGEN.md, RG-1): whether AMD's denoiser runtime is opened and asked at the start. auto (the default): only when an effect that can hand it a signal exists (the screen-space reflections do, and the AMD FSR RAY REGENERATION row is on: nothing is opened while it is off, and a row that is turned on opens it live). off: never. probe: on a Radeon RX 9000 series card on Direct3D 12 (never on any other PC) amd_fidelityfx_loader_dx12.dll and amd_fidelityfx_denoiser_dx12.dll are opened on a worker thread, the runtime's providers are listed and a small trial context is made: the log's '[gpu] ray regen:' lines say whether this card and driver take it and what a context costs, and no frame uses it. on: the AMD FSR RAY REGENERATION row on, with the rule that an effect it can clean is on lifted (the A/B and cost runs). Read at the start."

mcla_gpu_ray_regen_ssr.help: "Debug (A/B, AMD FSR Ray Regeneration, perf/RAY-REGEN.md, RG-3): what the screen-space reflections do while AMD FSR Ray Regeneration takes the frame. 1 (the default): the trace is the signal it denoises (radiance at the trace's half size with the ray's hit distance, next to guides in AMD's formats) and the reflections' resolve reads its output, with no accumulation over frames of their own. 0: they keep their own accumulation even then (the picture to compare with). With AMD FSR Ray Regeneration not the choice (every PC but a Radeon RX 9000 series card on Direct3D 12 with the AMD FSR RAY REGENERATION row on) nothing changes, whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_view.help:
"Debug (Ray Reconstruction guides): draws one of the images the DLSS Ray Reconstruction guide pass makes from the G-buffer over the upscaler's output "
    "(perf/DLSS-RR.md, RR-2): 1 the diffuse albedo, 2 the normal (0.5 + 0.5 n), 3 the roughness, 4 the specular albedo, 5 the hit distance (black on a "
    "surface, blue in the sky), 6 the responsivity. The guide pass runs while mcla_gpu_dlss_rr is on (DLSS, an RTX card that supports Ray Reconstruction) "
    "or, for a view, whenever an upscaler runs; the G-buffer planes it reads are made from the frame after it is asked for. The game's tone map and UI are "
    "drawn over the view as usual. A frame with no G-buffer (the pause menu, the garage, the map, a cutscene) shows the upscaler's own picture. 0: off. "
    "Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_test.help:
"Debug (Ray Reconstruction fallbacks, perf/DLSS-RR.md, RR-3): makes the frames Ray Reconstruction cannot take happen on purpose, to see that Super Resolution takes them and the switch back needs no rebuild of the context. "
    "0: off. 1: the guide images are withheld from the upscaler for 30 frames in every 60 (the frames are Super Resolution's, the plan says the guides are missing, the context stays). "
    "2: in the same frames the dispatch carries no diffuse albedo, so the rules refuse the guides and Super Resolution takes the frame in the same call (the census counts them). "
    "3: Ray Reconstruction's evaluation fails three frames in a row, once: it is dropped for the session and Super Resolution goes on (the log says so; DLSS stays on). "
    "Only while Ray Reconstruction is the plan (mcla_gpu_dlss_rr on). Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_ssr.help:
"Debug (A/B, Ray Reconstruction, perf/DLSS-RR.md, RR-4a): what the screen-space reflections do while Ray Reconstruction takes the frame. "
    "1 (the default): they hand it their raw one-ray-a-pixel result straight into the colour (no accumulation over frames of their own: Ray Reconstruction is the denoiser) and write how far each ray went into "
    "its hit distance guide. 0: they keep their own accumulation even then (the picture to compare with). With Ray Reconstruction not the plan (Super Resolution, FSR, no upscaler) nothing changes, "
    "whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_car_refl.help:
"Debug (A/B, Ray Reconstruction, perf/DLSS-RR.md, RR-4b): what the ray traced reflections of the cars do while Ray Reconstruction takes the frame. "
    "1 (the default): the paint reads the trace's raw image (the filter that takes the cone's grain out, mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt_denoise, is skipped: Ray Reconstruction is the denoiser) and the distance of "
    "each reflection's hits is written into its hit distance guide. 0: the filter runs even then (the picture to compare with). With Ray Reconstruction not the plan nothing changes, whatever "
    "this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_rt_gi.help:
"Debug (A/B, Ray Reconstruction, perf/DLSS-RR.md, CITY-RT G6): what the ray traced bounce light's per-pixel pass (ULTRA on a strong ray tracing card) does while Ray Reconstruction takes the frame. "
    "1 (the default): it hands Ray Reconstruction its raw one-ray-a-pixel diffuse light (no filter of its own: Ray Reconstruction is the denoiser) and the length of each ray as the hit distance guide where no reflection gave one. "
    "2: the same, but without the hit distance (NVIDIA's guide asks for it of the specular only). 0: it keeps its own filter even then (the picture to compare with). With Ray Reconstruction not the plan "
    "(Super Resolution, FSR, no upscaler) nothing changes, whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_rt_lights.help: "Debug (A/B, Ray Reconstruction, perf/DLSS-RR.md, RT-LIGHTS-D1 part 2): what the ray traced light visibility (mcla_gpu_rt_lights) does while Ray Reconstruction takes the frame. 1 (the default): the filter "\n    "does not run (Ray Reconstruction is the denoiser: it cleans the picture the light pass draws with the one-ray-a-pixel visibility in it), and the light pass reads the unfiltered visibility. 0: the effect keeps its own filter even then (the picture to compare with). "\n    "With Ray Reconstruction not the plan (Super Resolution, FSR, no upscaler) nothing changes, whatever this says. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_rr_rt_ao.help: "Debug: use raw ray traced ambient occlusion while DLSS Ray Reconstruction takes the frame. 0 keeps the built-in denoiser. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_mode.help:
"DLSS's mode, NVIDIA's names and the share of the output the scene is drawn at: dlaa (100%, "
    "only smoothed), quality (67%), balanced (58%), performance (50%) or ultra_performance (33%), "
    "per direction, of the output (the window's 16:9 area, whatever mcla_gpu_resolution_scale "
    "says). Live: the scene is drawn at the new size from a frame boundary once the upscaler is "
    "ready for it (several seconds for DLSS), and the old mode works until then."

mcla_gpu_upscaler_sharpness.help:
"How much the FSR upscalers sharpen their picture (AMD's RCAS pass), 0 to 1: 0 adds no "
    "sharpening, 1 the most. DLSS has no sharpening. Live."

mcla_gpu_fsr_debug_view.help:
"Test lever (FSR 3.1 and FSR 4 only): the upscaler's context is made with AMD's debug "
    "visualization (it holds more video memory) and every dispatch asks it to draw its own views "
    "into the picture it makes: the motion vectors it received and how much it trusts its history "
    "(its reactive, disocclusion and blend factor views, as its version has them; in FSR 4 the "
    "bright purple is a pixel whose history it does not trust). Everything the game does "
    "afterwards (bloom, tone map) reads that picture, overlay included. A change makes a new "
    "context: about half a second of plain frames. For A/B. Live."

mcla_gpu_dlss_mask_tags.help:
"Diagnostic: which of Streamline's hint inputs carry the masks DLSS is given (what is drawn "
    "again for the upscaler: shadows of cars, particles, light volumes, car glass). Add up: 1 the "
    "reactive mask goes in as the bias-current-colour hint, 2 as the reactive mask hint, 4 the glass "
    "mask goes in as the transparency and composition hint. 7: all three. Used with "
    "mcla_gpu_upscaler_mask_test (an all-ones mask) to see which hint the DLSS plugin reads: with "
    "the test on, 1 alone, then 2 alone, then 4 alone; the one that makes the picture lose its "
    "smoothness over time is read. Live."

mcla_gpu_fsr_velocity_factor.help:
"FSR's fVelocityFactor, 0 to 1 (FSR's own default is 1). 0, the default here, trusts the history "
    "less where something moved, which steadies bright pixels (on a still scene the strongest "
    "flickers drop by about two thirds, with no visible ghosting while driving). -1: not set, FSR's "
    "own default is restored. Passed to the context once it exists and again when it changes. Debug "
    "only. Live."
comments: // FSR's own tuning constants, passed through ffxConfigure on the context (FfxApiConfigureUpscaleKey;
// debug only, live, never saved). -1 is "not set": FSR's own default. A value of 0 or more is passed to
// the context before its first dispatch and again whenever it changes; the runtime clamps it to its
// range. FSR 3.1 reads them; FSR 4's provider may refuse the keys (the log says what it answered).
// The first two are 0 by default (the play build's values: measured on a still scene, the strongest
// flickers drop by about two thirds, and no ghosting shows while driving); the third is a test lever
// with FSR's own default.

mcla_gpu_fsr_shading_change_scale.help:
"FSR 3.1's fShadingChangeScale, 0 and up (FSR's own default is 1). More makes its computed "
    "shading change count for more, so a pixel whose lighting changed lets go of its history "
    "faster; 0, the default here, turns that off (together with the velocity factor of 0, the "
    "strongest flickers of a still scene drop by about two thirds). -1: not set, FSR's own default "
    "is restored. Passed to the context once it exists and again when it changes. Debug only. Live."

mcla_gpu_fsr_min_disocclusion_accumulati.help:
"Test lever (FSR 3.1): FSR's fMinDisocclusionAccumulation (its default is -0.333; only 0 to 1 "
    "can be set here). AMD: raising it may reduce the white flicker of thin objects that "
    "disocclude one another often; too high, ghosting. -1: not set, FSR's own default. Passed to the "
    "context once it exists and again when it changes. For A/B. Live."

mcla_gpu_texture_dump.help:
"Write every texture the NATIVE renderer uploads to <mods>/textures_dump/<dictionary>/"
    "<name>__<hash>.dds, once per texture per session (F2 does it for one frame). Texture mods "
    "replace a texture by the hash at the end of the file name, from "
    "<mods>/<Mod>/textures_replace/; <mods> is modloader/, mods/ or models/."

texture_mods.help:
"Use the texture mods (<mods>/<Mod>/textures_replace/). False shows the game's own textures; "
    "changing it re-indexes the mods at the start of the next frame."

texture_reload.help:
"Set to true to reload the texture mods (<mods>/<Mod>/textures_replace/) at the start of the "
    "next frame, the same as RELOAD TEXTURE MODS in the pause menu. It clears itself afterwards."

mcla_gpu_texture_decode_threads.help:
"Threads that decode the textures of the draws queued behind the one the renderer is on "
    "(untile, byte swap), so a burst of new textures as the game streams in the next stretch of "
    "road does not stall the render thread. -1: one thread per 4 logical processors, up to 3, none "
    "below 4 processors. 0: the render thread decodes every texture itself, when its draw needs "
    "it. The threads run below the game's."

mcla_gpu_texture_decode_selftest.help:
"Test only: at start-up, decodes a few thousand random texture levels (every block size, "
    "endian, tiled and linear, packed-tail offsets, DXT decompression) with the fast decoder and "
    "with the plain per-block one, and logs whether every byte matched."

mcla_gpu_texture_decode_verify.help:
"Test only: every texture level the game uploads is decoded a second time with the plain "
    "per-block decoder and compared byte for byte with the fast one's; a difference is logged "
    "once per texture. Slow: it brings the old cost back."

mcla_gpu_upscaler_mask_test.help:
"Diagnostic: tests whether the upscalers read their mask inputs. 1 gives the reactive mask (what "
    "FSR calls reactive; DLSS's bias-current-colour and reactive hints) every pixel at 1, 2 gives the "
    "transparency and composition mask every pixel at 1, 3 both. An upscaler that reads a mask then "
    "stops trusting its history: the picture loses its smoothness over time (edges crawl, thin lines "
    "flicker); one that does not read it looks as before. Only while FSR or DLSS runs. 0: the real "
    "masks. Live."

mcla_gpu_vram_log.help:
"Diagnostic: every this many frames (at the next check of the video memory, every 30 frames), "
    "log how much video memory the process uses against the budget the system gives it, and what "
    "the texture, resolve product, EDRAM target and resolve memory caches hold, whether or not "
    "memory is short. For a report of stutter or crashes on a card with little video memory. "
    "0: off."

mcla_gpu_watch_base.help:
"Diagnostic: a guest physical address in hex. Every resolve into, product "
    "activated or deactivated over, texture fetched from and resolve-memory decode of "
    "[base, base + mcla_gpu_watch_size) is logged in order with the guest frame and draw: the "
    "last 1500 events are kept until the first decode of the range, then written out with "
    "every later one (at most 20000 lines). Empty: off."

mcla_gpu_watch_size.help: "Diagnostic: the length, in hex, of mcla_gpu_watch_base's range."

mcla_gpu_watch_capture.help:
"Diagnostic, with mcla_gpu_watch_base: a RenderDoc capture of the frame after 1 = the first "
    "decode of the range from the resolve memory, 2 = the first product over it deactivated by "
    "another resolve. 0: none. Needs the game started under RenderDoc."

trigger_resistance.help:
"DualSense trigger resistance: a throttle spring on R2 and brake resistance on L2 while a car "
    "is driven, slack everywhere else. Other controllers are not touched."

trigger_vibration.help:
"DualSense trigger vibration: R2 vibrates while the driven wheels spin under power and L2 while "
    "the brakes lock the wheels, harder the more they slip. Other controllers are not touched."

adaptive_triggers.help:
"Old setting, replaced by trigger_resistance and trigger_vibration. False in an older settings "
    "file turns both off."
comments: // The one setting both effects used to share. Only read for old settings files: false there turns
// trigger_resistance and trigger_vibration off at the first tick, and this goes back to true.

trigger_throttle.help: "R2 resistance at the end of its travel, 1 (light) to 8 (firm). Used by trigger_resistance."

trigger_brake.help: "L2 resistance at the end of its travel, 1 (light) to 8 (firm). Used by trigger_resistance."

mcla_audio_output.help: "auto: the default device, or silence when none opens. null: always silent."

cam_freelook.help:
"Mouse look on the gameplay camera. The shipped lookaround is four digital pan actions "
    "easing towards clamped limits, which is why the camera settles on a handful of angles "
    "instead of following you. With this on, the mouse steers the view directly while you drive "
    "with the keyboard and mouse: the pointer is hidden and locked (the window's relative mouse "
    "mode, raw counts from the mouse) and the view eases back behind the car when the mouse "
    "has been still for a moment. It is active only while the keyboard and mouse are the last "
    "thing you used, with the car on the road: no menu, map, phone or overlay up, and the window "
    "in front. A controller's right stick looks around as it always did."

cam_freelook_sens.help:
"Mouse look sensitivity: radians of view movement per count the mouse reports. 0.0035 "
    "turns the view a full circle for about 6 cm of movement on an 800 DPI mouse and about 3 cm "
    "on a 1600 DPI one; a mouse with a higher DPI turns further for the same movement, so "
    "lower this for it."
comments: // The sensitivity rule (mouse_look_core.h): radians of view per RAW mouse count. At Windows' default pointer speed one count was one cursor pixel, which is what this
// used to be measured in, so 0.0035 keeps the same feel at default sensitivity whatever the mouse's DPI is (360 degrees = 1795 counts: 5.7 cm at 800 DPI, 2.8 cm at 1600).

cam_freelook_yaw_limit.help:
"How far the view may turn left or right, in radians. Pi is all the way "
    "round. This is the cap on our own angle, not the game's -- the game's own "
    "limits are what this feature overwrites."

cam_freelook_pitch_limit.help:
"How much tilt the mouse may accumulate, in radians. This caps the input, "
    "not the result -- where the camera ends up is decided by the two "
    "elevation limits below, which are what keep it out of the ground."

cam_freelook_inplace_rigs.help:
"Comma-separated camera rig indices that turn in place instead of "
    "orbiting: the views mounted on the car. Switch to a view, read the rig "
    "number out of the cam_freelook_diag line, add it here. Empty orbits "
    "everything.\n"
    "\n"
    "The camera button cycles 3, 2, 1, 0 and wraps; 4 belongs to some other "
    "context and turns up on its own. 1 is the cockpit, and 0 is the bumper "
    "sitting next to it in the cycle -- which is a reading of the cycle order, "
    "not something measured, so if a view mounted on the car still swings out "
    "of the bodywork, its number belongs in this list."
comments: // A camera bolted to the car -- cockpit, bumper, bonnet -- has nothing to
// orbit: it turns where it sits, like a head. Swinging it round a centre seven
// metres away, which is right for a chase camera, walks it straight out
// through the bodywork.
// Which rigs those are cannot be worked out from here. The honest signal would
// be the camera's real distance to the car, and that distance is exactly what
// this feature never manages to find out -- it is why the orbit radius is a
// cvar in the first place. So it is a list, and the diagnostic prints the rig
// number every time it applies, which makes filling the list a matter of
// reading one line per view.
// r24 in sub_822C0320 is the rig the camera system settled on this frame, and
// Hook_CameraSystem has been recording it since the first probe. Per the note
// on Patch_DebugCam it is 1 for the cockpit view and 2 for a static one.

cam_freelook_min_elev.help:
"Lowest the camera may go, as an angle in radians above the horizontal "
    "through the point it orbits. 0 is dead level with the car; below that it "
    "goes under it and into the ground. Negative values are allowed for "
    "deliberately low shots, on the understanding that the ground is not "
    "consulted."
comments: // Rotating the finished matrix means the game's camera collision never sees
// the result, so the floor has to be put back by hand. It states cleanly in
// geometry: pos = centre - forward * d with d negative, so the camera sits
// forward.y * |d| above the point it orbits and its elevation is
// asin(forward.y). Clamping that angle is exactly clamping how far under the
// car the view can get. Orbiting rigs only -- in place the position never
// moves, so there is nothing to keep out of the ground.

cam_freelook_max_elev.help:
"Highest the camera may go, same units. Short of pi/2 on purpose: at dead "
    "overhead the forward vector is parallel to world up and the yaw stops "
    "meaning anything."

cam_freelook_approach.help:
"LookaroundApproachRate while free look is on. 0 leaves the shipped value. "
    "The shipped one eases the view towards its target over a good fraction of "
    "a second, which reads as lag under a mouse."
comments: // Both default to 0 = leave the shipped value alone. Their units are not known
// -- "rate" reads as per-second and "factor" as a 0..1 blend, but neither is
// confirmed -- and a wrong value here is indistinguishable from the whole
// approach not working. Changing one thing at a time is the point.

cam_freelook_lerp.help: "LookaroundLerpFactor while free look is on. 0 leaves the shipped value."

cam_freelook_return_delay.help:
"Seconds the mouse has to sit still before the view starts easing back "
    "behind the car. The game's own equivalent is LookaroundDelayTime. Set it "
    "very high to keep the view wherever it was left."
comments: // The shipped camera recentres itself: LookaroundDelayTime then
// LookaroundDecayRate. Not reproducing that was the difference between a free
// look and a view that silently accumulates every stray twitch of the mouse
// until the car is sitting crooked and there is no way to put it back.

cam_freelook_return_rate.help:
"How quickly the view eases back once the delay is up, as a fraction of "
    "the remaining angle per second. The game's own equivalent is "
    "LookaroundDecayRate."

cam_freelook_invert_x.help:
"Mirror the horizontal axis. Needed if the tune's left/right limits turn "
    "out to be signed the other way round from what this assumes."

cam_look_obj.help:
"Byte offset into the camera system holding the pointer to the object the "
    "look lives in. 860 is what the field probe found."
comments: // ── Driving the camera object the probe found ──────────────────────────
// The measurement landed on one object -- camsys+860, which came out as
// 0xBD910980 -- and on fourteen floats inside it, at +96 through +156. Three
// rows of unit-length vectors at +96/+112/+128 and a world position at +144:
// the camera's own matrix, rotating about Y and orbiting as the view swings.
// The two floats that are not part of it are the interesting ones. +140 and
// +156 are the w lanes of the third and fourth rows, which is where RAGE
// habitually parks a scalar it did not want to give a field of its own, and
// they went from about zero to -0.947685 and -7.34199 -- an angle in radians
// and, to within the accuracy of reading a matrix, the radius the position
// orbited on.
// Whether +140 is what the camera READS to build that matrix or what it WROTE
// afterwards is the only thing left to settle, and no amount of staring
// settles it. So the offsets are cvars, the write happens inside the camera
// tick before the update runs, and the value is read back on the next frame
// and compared against what was written. That answers it in one run and lets
// other candidates be tried without a rebuild.

cam_freelook_orbit.help:
"Distance from the camera to the point it turns around, used whenever the "
    "object's own +156 is not usable.\n"
    "\n"
    "It usually is not. +156 was measured at -7.34 during a held look and that "
    "is where this default comes from, but it is the w lane of the position "
    "row and the game computes it the same way it computes the angle at +140 "
    "-- both read zero whenever the game's own look is idle, which is exactly "
    "when this feature is doing the looking instead. The field still wins when "
    "it holds something sane, so a camera that keeps a real distance there is "
    "followed rather than overridden."

cam_look_phase.help:
"Which matrix the look turns. 2 is the real one: the camera matrix "
    "sub_8220AA68 is handed at 0x8220AA88, before it has read a byte of "
    "it, from which the game publishes to dword_8286D804+4208 and +4272 "
    "and mirrors into the cine director. 0 and 1 turn that mirror "
    "instead, at 0x822C0790 and at the camera tick epilogue, and are "
    "kept only because they were tried first -- sub_823CC2E8 is a plain "
    "setter that copies the real matrix into it, so writing there is "
    "writing to a copy and nothing on screen ever changed. The camera "
    "collision lives on its own switch, cam_freelook_collide, and not on "
    "this one -- see there."

cam_freelook_cs_invert.help:
"Flip the sign used when feeding the camera state's own two angle channels "
    "(cs+776 yaw, cs+772 pitch). The offset and direction were derived from "
    "sub_82202E38 and sub_82227DE0 -- both store `pi/2 - angle`, so a turn is a "
    "subtraction -- but which way that reads on screen is a handedness question "
    "the maths does not settle. If the view turns opposite to the mouse with "
    "cam_freelook_collide on, this is the switch. Only affects the collide "
    "path."

cam_freelook_collide.help:
"Turn the camera one stage earlier, at the camera state (0x8231CEB0), so "
    "the game's own camera collision resolves the rotated position and the "
    "view stops passing through walls and buildings. OFF by default because it "
    "is unproven: it hands the look to sub_8231CE30, and any rig whose camera "
    "state does not route through there gets no free look at all while this is "
    "on. Turn cam_freelook_diag on with it -- the log says whether the hook "
    "ran, which camera state it got, and what CollideType that state carries. "
    "With this off, cam_look_phase decides everything, exactly as before."

cam_freelook_tune.help:
"Also pin the LookaroundLimit* tune fields, the first approach. It did not "
    "hold on its own and is kept only so the two can be tried together."

cam_freelook_diag.help:
"Log the lookaround tune fields as they are found and the angles being "
    "written, once a second."

cam_probe_mark.help:
"Button: snapshot the gameplay camera object. Flips back off. Do it with "
    "the car still and the view centred, then look around, then use "
    "cam_probe_dump."

cam_probe_dump.help:
"Button: snapshot the camera again, diff it against cam_probe_mark and "
    "write every float that moved to <exe>/cam_fields.txt. Flips back off."

cam_probe_run.help:
"Button: run the whole camera measurement on a timer. Close the overlay "
    "when it is armed; the baseline is taken after cam_probe_arm_delay with "
    "the camera left alone, and the diff cam_probe_hold_delay after that with "
    "the look held. Both samples happen with nothing on screen. Flips back "
    "off."
comments: // The two buttons above cannot be used for the measurement they were written
// for: reaching them means opening the settings overlay, and opening it takes
// the game out of whatever camera state was being held. This runs the whole
// sequence on a timer instead, so the overlay is only ever open while the
// camera is idle and both samples are taken with it shut.

cam_probe_arm_delay.help:
"Seconds between arming cam_probe_run and the baseline sample. Long "
    "enough to close the overlay and let the camera settle."

cam_probe_hold_delay.help:
"Seconds between the baseline sample and the diff. Hold the look for all "
    "of it."

cam_trace.help:
"Write cam_trace.csv: every game update's camera (position, direction, shake), the player "
    "car's position and the clock's time step, every guest swap, and when each frame was "
    "presented and reached the screen. For measuring camera judder."

carbon_all_parts.help: "Carbon fiber can be applied to any body part, not just the hood."

carbon_menu_diag.help:
"Log the garage menu state tree, per-state field dumps and the "
    "activate/command stream while the paint screen is open."
comments: // Menu instrumentation. Off by default because it is chatty, but it is what
// mapped the garage UI in the first place: the state tree, the field dump that
// found state+12, the activate/command stream. Keep it — turning it on again
// beats rediscovering any of it.

hide_mouse_pointer.help:
"Hide the mouse pointer during play. It goes at once when a controller is "
    "used and after about 3 seconds without mouse movement, only over the game "
    "window while it has focus. Mouse movement, a click, the wheel or losing "
    "focus brings it back, and it stays while the mouse is over an overlay."

cutscene_replay.help:
"Which cutscene the pause menu's CUTSCENES tab replays. Names match the "
    "scene's animation pack under $/resources/animation/cineanimpacks. The "
    "default is a hangout exit because those need no cars: an offline scan of "
    "the generated scripts shows the cut_hangout_* scenes make zero Cars_* and "
    "zero AssignNameToSlot calls, while the story scenes want four racers that "
    "free roam does not have."

cutscene_play_now.help:
"Set to a cutscene name to play it immediately, without going through the "
    "menu. Clears itself once the scene starts."

cutscene_force_events.help:
"Diagnostic only, and it does NOT help a replay: mgr+305 turned out to be "
    "the SKIP request, not a 'scene is playing' flag. sub_823BEEB0 reads it, "
    "asks sub_823BBB98 for the time of the next cut event, and jumps the scene "
    "clock there -- measured: the garage scene picked 2.833s and ended in four "
    "frames, and district champs picked 74.233s and its clock went 0.036 -> "
    "74.254 in one frame. Leave it off; it is kept only to reproduce that."

cutscene_force_camera.help:
"Run the camera event's own start handler (sub_823D7280) on the event that "
    "Camera_LaunchEvent queued, if the cutscene camera is still idle a frame "
    "later. That handler is the only thing in the game that writes the camera's "
    "clock (cineCam+120), and mcCineDirector::IsCameraActive (sub_823CDC90) "
    "refuses to hand the screen to the cutscene camera while that clock is "
    "negative -- so if the event is queued but never dispatched, this is exactly "
    "the work the game skipped, done with the game's own function and the game's "
    "own event object. It is a no-op when the camera is already running."

cutscene_menu_autoclose.help:
"Let a scene picked from the pause menu start by itself: unpause the game "
    "with the pause manager's own ResumeOnly request, play, then hand the menu "
    "by calling the same function the Continue item calls (sub_8265F428), so the "
    "menu closes through the game's own transition -- the one that unpauses and "
    "emits resume/ENTERNORMAL/HUDMOVIE. Turn it off to arm the scene and close "
    "the menu by hand instead."

cutscene_skip_uses_teardown.help:
"Make the skip button end a REPLAY through our own teardown instead of the "
    "game's skip path. Off, because the native path is the one that restores "
    "anything: it does not kill the scene, it pushes the scene clock to the next "
    "cut event, and SetTime then runs every event in between -- including the "
    "tail (fade_to_black, bookmark_cut_to_game, fade_to_scene) that hands the "
    "camera back, brings the HUD in and stops the speech. Our teardown skips all "
    "of that, which is why it left the audio playing and nothing restored. Kept "
    "only as an escape hatch if a scene wedges with no cut event to jump to."

cutscene_keep_movies.help:
"Clear mgr+316 before the scene tears down, so FinishScene does not run its "
    "movie teardown. That branch is `if (mgr+316) { sub_821F6238(movies); "
    "sub_821F15C8(...); }`, and sub_821F6238 walks four movie slots calling "
    "sub_821F4C18, which does `v4 = slot[2]; if (v4) { *v4 = 0; slot[2] = 0; }` "
    "-- it writes zero over the first dword of whatever that slot points at, and "
    "the first dword of an object is its vtable. The pause menu is a Flash movie "
    "(PAUSEMOVIE), and reopening it after a replay died on exactly that: a vfunc "
    "call through an object whose vtable had been zeroed. mgr+316 is set by "
    "SetSceneName, so every replay took that branch. A mission survives it "
    "because the flow rebuilds the movies on the way back to gameplay; a replay "
    "has no flow. The cost of skipping it is the scene's subtitle movie not "
    "being released -- a leak, not a crash."

cutscene_probe_log.help:
"Print the per-frame trace of a replay: which characters stream in, every "
    "actor launch with its clip and entity, the camera hand-over, and each cine "
    "event as it fires with its name from the game's own table. Off by default "
    "because a 74 second scene is a few hundred lines. The things that mean "
    "something went wrong -- a bailed script, a wedged scene, a stuck release "
    "counter -- are always printed regardless."

cutscene_run_script.help:
"Start any script object by name, relative to $/script_obj, on the next "
    "frame. Meant for the game's own cutscene harness -- "
    "'tools/CutsceneTests/SETUP_GENERIC_CUTSCENE' slots the racers and "
    "characters a scene needs. Clears itself once the script is mounted."

cutscene_setup.help:
"Run $/script_obj/tools/CutsceneTests/SETUP_GENERIC_CUTSCENE before the "
    "scene. It is the game's own standalone-cutscene harness: it slots four "
    "racers and nine character sets, which is what a generated cutscene script "
    "assumes and bails out without."

cutscene_bind_coordsys.help:
"Anchor the scene to the player's car before it plays, through the game's "
    "own CineScript_SetGameCoordSysBindingCopyRacer. A cutscene is authored "
    "around its own origin, not in world space; the gameplay script that "
    "normally plays one WARPS the player to the scene and leaves the binding "
    "at zero, which is why an all-zero binding looked correct when this was "
    "measured on a real garage entry. A replay does not warp, so with no "
    "anchor the scene plays at the world origin -- measured: the player's car "
    "went from (819.6, 17.5, -808.4) to (-0.1, -2.8, -5.6) across one replay, "
    "which is both the car that will not drive afterwards and the actors that "
    "walk on nothing. Anchoring brings the scene to the car instead, which is "
    "what the reward and cop-pullover scenes do natively. Off by default: it "
    "made things worse in play, so the anchor stays behind this flag until "
    "there is a measurement that says what it broke."

cutscene_pad_racers.help:
"Repeat the player into the cutscene's remaining car slots when the world "
    "has fewer racers than the scene wants. Wrong on screen -- several cars end "
    "up being the same one -- but it is what gets a scene past its "
    "'insufficient number of racers slotted' guard in free roam."

cutscene_debug.help:
"Dump the whole script-thread tree and the scrThread array with each "
    "cutscene gate report. Off by default: it is ~200 lines a shot."

cutscene_stop.help:
"Abort the running cutscene and dump which of mcCineScript's gates never "
    "opened. 'kill' raises the script's own kill flag; 'finish' runs the "
    "teardown directly, which is what gets the HUD back from a wedged scene."

fullscreen_exclusive.help:
"With fullscreen on: exclusive fullscreen. The display is switched to the size of "
    "`fullscreen_resolution` (the nearest mode it lists; the display's own size when it is empty) "
    "while the game has the focus, and put back when the game loses it or closes. Off is borderless "
    "fullscreen: a window without a frame the size of the display, the display left as it is. "
    "Windows only."

mcla_compare_effect.help:
"Developer tool (builds with LARECOMP_DEV_TOOLS only): which graphics effect the compare key flips off and on, to see "
    "what it does: bounce (the bounce light, the default), contact (contact shadows), shafts (sun shafts), occlusion "
    "(ambient occlusion), filter (the sun shadow filter), selfrefl (the car's reflection of its own body) or bloom (the glow "
    "size fix: the select key does not walk to it, set it here or on the command line). The select key is F12 and the "
    "compare key F1 until they are rebound in the key bindings of F4 (bind_mcla_compare_next, bind_mcla_compare). F12 "
    "selects the next effect and shows which one in a label at the top of the screen; F1 shows the selected effect the other "
    "way than your setting has it, the label says how, and the next press puts your setting back. The flip is never "
    "saved, and it is dropped when the setting it flips is changed or this one is. Live."

mcla_compare_label_seconds.help:
"Diagnostic: how long the compare key's label stays up before it fades out (about 0.35 s more), 0.5 to 30. "
    "A test run takes its pictures a second after the press and sets it higher. Live."

fma_float_fast.help:
"On a CPU without FMA3 (Intel before Haswell, AMD before Piledriver), fused multiply-adds "
    "whose operands are single-precision values are computed with a double multiply and add, "
    "which gives the same bits, instead of the C runtime's software fma (157 to 165 cycles a "
    "call). Nothing changes on a CPU with FMA3. Off passes every call to the runtime. Takes "
    "effect at the next start."

guest_profile.help:
"Sample the busiest threads, and photograph every thread when the game stops. "
    "The same thing MCLA_PROFILE=1 turns on, reachable from the config file so a "
    "session need not be launched from a shell to get it. The periodic report says "
    "where frame time goes; the stall dump is the one that matters when a load "
    "never finishes, because the thread the sampler follows is parked in a wait by "
    "then and the stuck one is somebody else. Reports land in logs/profile_*.log."

impulse_triggers.help:
"Xbox One and Xbox Series trigger rumble: the right trigger shakes while the driven wheels "
    "spin under power, the left while the brakes lock the wheels, harder the more they slip. "
    "Controllers without trigger motors, and a DualSense (which has its own settings), are not "
    "touched."

impulse_trigger_strength.help:
"How strong the Xbox trigger rumble is, in percent of what the trigger motors can do "
    "(10 to 100)."

input_log.help:
"Log every key, mouse and controller event that the active-device rules looked at and what they "
    "decided (counted, or why it was ignored), at most 4000 lines. The switches themselves are always "
    "logged."

input_test_pad_loss.help:
"Test only: set to true to act as if the controller in the player's hands had just been unplugged: the "
    "same rule as a real removal (only while a pad is the active device and the game is driven; the pad "
    "need not be real). The next pad poll takes it; set it to false and true again for another."

keyboard_native.help:
"Native keyboard, always on. Feeds the keyboard and the mouse buttons straight into the game's own "
    "input layer (rage ioMapper) from the window's key events: menus and driving get separate key sets, "
    "so Enter can be 'accept' in a menu and Pause on the road without ever being both. A debug switch "
    "to tell whether a bug comes from it (off = the keyboard does nothing)."

comments: // ── Menus (the FlashNavigator mapper). Comma separated key names, the same names
// as keybind_* ("Return", "Escape", "Space", "PageUp", "F5", "Semicolon" ...).
// A combination such as Shift+Up counts as its last key.

kb_ui_start.help:
"Start: opens the pause menu on the road and answers \"PRESS START\" on the title screen. "
    "It is Start only while NO menu is open: with a menu up these keys are accept/back and "
    "nothing else, which is what keeps Enter from being accept and Start at once. A key held "
    "when a menu closes stays off until released, so the Enter that picks CONTINUE cannot "
    "reopen the pause menu."

kb_ui_select.help: "Menus: the Back/Select button (GPS, map). Start has no key here on purpose."

kb_drive_steer_left.help: "Driving: steer left (pairs with the right key at the same position)"
comments: // ── Driving (the player's control-map mapper).

kb_drive_weight.help: "Driving: weight transfer, the 'turn in' of the pad's B (either Ctrl key)"
comments: // The defaults of the road (KBM-DESIGN.md 2.7, phase P5): WASD and the arrows steer, accelerate and brake; Space is the handbrake; Ctrl is the weight transfer (Caps Lock was a
// lock key that toggles the host's state); Shift, X or the left mouse button is nitro; the right mouse button looks back (the mouse itself looks around: mouse_look.h). None of
// these is also a menu key that matters on the road: the menu's keys (kb_ui_*) live in the UI mapper, which the road's mapper never sees, and Start (Enter, Esc) is live only while
// no menu is open. Q and E are the gears here and the tabs (LB, RB) in a menu; Tab is the map's and the GPS's Back button, never a driving key.

kb_drive_nitro.help: "Driving: nitro (the pad's X). On the road the X prompt shows the first of these keys that has a cap. LMB is the left mouse button."
comments: // "Shift,X,LMB": X stays on nitro as well as Shift (a pad habit). It used to be needed so that the prompt for the pad's X, painted with the menu's X key, did what the pad's X
// does on the road (KBM-DESIGN 1.3 item 8); the prompts now show the driving key on the road (prompt_glyphs.h, Context), so the first key with a cap, Shift, is what shows there.

kb_drive_camera.help: "Driving: change camera, one step along the game's cycle (the pad's RB)"

kb_drive_camera_keys.help:
"Driving: keys that jump straight to a camera, slot 1..5 (empty = off). The game only "
    "has a button that steps through its cameras; the jump presses it for you, as many "
    "times as the cycle needs, and stops on the one asked for."

kb_drive_camera_views.help:
"Driving: which camera each slot above selects, as the game numbers them: 0 bumper, "
    "1 cockpit, 2/3/4 the chase views. Default: slot 1 action(4), 2 bumper(0), 3 classic(3), "
    "4 static(2), 5 cockpit(1). Swap numbers here if 3 and 4 turn out the other way round."

kb_drive_lookback.help: "Driving: look back. RMB is the right mouse button."

kb_drive_pause.help:
"Driving: the PAUSE action of the control map. Empty by default: the pause menu is opened "
    "by Start in the UI mapper (kb_ui_start), which is where the pad's Start goes as well."

kb_drive_popup_select.help: "Driving: answer a pop-up with A (empty = pad only; Enter would also be Pause)"

kb_drive_popup_back.help: "Driving: answer a pop-up with B (empty = pad only)"

kb_steer_rise.help: "Keyboard steering: seconds from centre to full lock while a steering key is held (a tap is a small correction). Shorter = twitchier, 0.05 is nearly the old on / off steering."
comments: // Keyboard steering is not a 0 / 100 % switch: full lock builds up while a key is held and returns to centre when it is let go (mouse_look_core.h StepSteer). The ramp
// rides the left stick's X axis of the state the game reads (KeySteerScope, XamInputGetState wrapper), so the game steers exactly as it does for a stick pushed that far.

kb_steer_return.help:
"Keyboard steering: seconds from full lock back to centre when the steering key is let go, and the time the wheel takes to come through the centre when you steer the other "
    "way. Shorter = the car straightens up quicker."

kb_steer_ramp.help: "Debug: the steering ramp above. Off = the old key pair, full lock at once and centre at once (it rebuilds the driving mapper)."

kb_steer_log.help: "Log the steering ramp: one line per input poll while a steering key is held or the wheel is coming back (at most 3000 lines)."

keycaps_dir.help:
"Folder of the 64x64 key cap PNGs the keyboard glyphs are painted from, named by "
    "lower-case key (return.png, escape.png, a.png, capslock.png ...). Empty = the "
    "set embedded in the executable (src/keycaps/). Built by tools/keycaps/pack_keycaps.py."

extra_button_l4.help:
"Host key(s) that the pad's L4 button sends (e.g. \"Numpad4\"; several: \"Numpad4,F13\"). "
    "The key stops acting as a keyboard key and becomes the game button L4. Empty = unused."
comments: // The extra buttons of a pad (back paddles: L4, L5, R4, R5). A pad that has them sends nothing
// of its own for them -- the maker's software makes each one press some other button or key --
// so the host key the pad is set to send is named here and the game gets a button of its own.
// Bind it in Options > Controller > Customize like any other button. Empty = not used.

extra_button_l5.help: "Host key(s) that the pad's L5 button sends. See extra_button_l4."

extra_button_r4.help: "Host key(s) that the pad's R4 button sends. See extra_button_l4."

extra_button_r5.help: "Host key(s) that the pad's R5 button sends. See extra_button_l4."

prompts_ps_map.help:
"Debug: which dictionary bitmaps hold the game's own PlayStation shoulder, Start and Back buttons, as SLOT=shared_N.dds pairs separated by commas "
    "(slots A B X Y LB RB LT RT Start Back Phone), e.g. \"LB=shared_8.dds,RB=shared_32.dds\". A slot with no entry here or in the built-in table (prompt_glyphs.h) "
    "gets the shipped picture (src/keycaps/ps_*.png). Used to try candidates without a build."

prompts_glyph_dump.help:
"Debug: a folder; when the UI's texture dictionary is first found, every small DXT5 bitmap in it is written there as raw RGBA (<name>_<w>x<h>.rgba, plus index.txt), "
    "to see which bitmap is which glyph. Empty = off. Read once at start."

map_mouse.help:
"Drive the full map's cursor with the mouse. The pointer position is "
    "unprojected onto the map plane, so the cursor lands where you point "
    "instead of drifting like a stick would."

map_mouse_fov.help:
"Vertical field of view, in degrees, of the camera the full map is drawn "
    "with. The only number the unprojection cannot read out of the game. Too "
    "small and the cursor lags behind the pointer towards the screen edges; "
    "too large and it runs ahead. The centre of the screen is correct at any "
    "value, so calibrate by pointing at a corner."

map_mouse_flip_x.help:
"Mirror the horizontal axis of the map cursor. Needed only if the camera "
    "basis rows turn out to be left-handed -- the cursor then moves the wrong "
    "way along one axis while the other tracks correctly."

map_mouse_flip_y.help: "Mirror the vertical axis of the map cursor. See map_mouse_flip_x."

map_mouse_zoom.help:
"Zoom the full map with the scroll wheel. The camera height is the zoom, "
    "so this walks it through the game's own min/max at +1124/+1128."

map_mouse_zoom_step.help: "Multiplier applied to the map camera's height per wheel detent."

map_mouse_zoom_smooth.help:
"How much of the remaining distance to the wheel's target height the "
    "camera covers each frame. A detent is a step, and stepping the camera "
    "straight to it is what made the zoom read as jerky; this eases into it "
    "instead. 1.0 restores the instant jump."

map_mouse_zoom_to_cursor.help:
"Zoom around the point under the pointer instead of around the middle of "
    "the view. With this off the camera only changes height, which slides the "
    "world under a pointer that has not moved and drags the cursor towards "
    "the centre on every detent."

map_mouse_magnet.help:
"Leave the map's cursor magnet alone. The map snaps the cursor onto the "
    "selected icon, both on selecting it and again on every frame it stays "
    "selected, which is how a thumbstick is made to feel sticky over "
    "waypoints and what welds a pointer to the first one it brushes. Off "
    "suppresses both snaps for whichever device currently owns the cursor "
    "being the mouse -- a stick moved out of its deadzone takes ownership "
    "back and gets its magnet with it. The selection and its highlight are "
    "never touched either way, so hovering works regardless."

map_mouse_max_steps.help:
"Ceiling on how many stick-sized steps one frame may walk the cursor "
    "towards the pointer. The map's boundary sweep is written for the small "
    "deltas a stick produces and reads a null neighbour pointer when handed a "
    "long chord, so the move is subdivided rather than teleported. Anything "
    "left over is covered by the next frame, so a ceiling too low shows up as "
    "a cursor that crawls after a fast flick rather than as anything worse. "
    "The walk stops as soon as it arrives or stops making progress, so a high "
    "ceiling costs nothing on the small movements that make up most frames."

map_mouse_hide_cursor.help:
"Hide the OS pointer while the full map is up. The in-game cursor tracks "
    "it one to one, so the visible cursor is the game's own."

map_mouse_diag.help:
"Log the map screen pointer, camera basis and the world point the mouse "
    "unprojects to, once a second."

warp_spot.help:
"Where F9 drops the car: \"x y z heading\" (heading in degrees, 0 = facing +Z). "
    "Empty = the first point a mod names in models/<mod>/warps.txt. The car is "
    "dropped onto whatever collision is below the point."

start_garage_last.help:
"The garage nearest the car the last time it was driven (hollywood, beaches or sc); "
    "start_garage = last starts the session there. The game keeps it up to date."

start_garage.help:
"Which district garage the car starts the session at: hollywood (what the game "
    "always does), beaches, sc, or last (the garage nearest the car when the game was "
    "closed). The car is moved there once, when it first appears at Hollywood's door, so a "
    "change is seen at the next start of the game."

menu_cam_lock.help:
"Always show the same shot instead of letting the game rotate. Off = the "
    "game picks (setMenuCam plus its own visibility probes) and menu_cam_slot is "
    "ignored; on = menu_cam_slot every time. This is the on/off switch — the "
    "slot number by itself never locks anything."

mcla_exposure_log.help:
"TEMP DIAG: log the guest auto-exposure value this many times, one sample every "
    "120 front-end camera updates. Runs on a GUEST hook, so it works with the native "
    "runtime on OR off -- which is the point: the native path renders menu camera 53 "
    "a uniform 1.8x brighter than the emulated one, and the emulated exposure has "
    "never been read."

mcla_exposure_log_addr.help:
"TEMP DIAG: physical guest address mcla_exposure_log reads (the 1x1 luminance "
    "target)."

menu_cam_slot.help:
"Which shot menu_cam_lock pins (0-63). Ignored while menu_cam_lock is off, "
    "so parking a number here is harmless."

menu_cam_custom.help:
"Place the menu camera at the shot from <exe dir>/menu_cameras.txt matching "
    "the current slot. Slots with no line keep the stock camera. The file is "
    "re-read when it changes, so you can tune it with the menu on screen."

menu_cam_only_custom.help:
"Show only your own shots. Whatever slot the game picks is remapped onto the "
    "lines present in menu_cameras.txt, so the stock cameras never appear. The "
    "game's rotation still decides which of your shots comes up; turn on "
    "menu_cam_lock to pin one. Needs menu_cam_custom."

menu_cam_cycle.help:
"Seconds between shots, rotating through every line in menu_cameras.txt. "
    "0 = no rotation. The game does not rotate the front-end camera itself — it "
    "only calls setMenuCam for the network and garage menus, so without this the "
    "boot screen sits on one shot forever. Ignored while menu_cam_lock is on."

menu_cam_record.help:
"Capture the game's own menu shots into menu_cameras.txt as 'cam' lines. "
    "There is no table of stock camera spots in the XEX — they only exist as "
    "runtime state — so this samples the real camera whenever it moves somewhere "
    "new (25+ units) and appends it with the next free slot number. Leave it on "
    "while the menus cycle, then turn it off: every shot, stock and custom, is "
    "now a line you own. Works with menu_cam_custom on; it always records what "
    "the game produced, never what this placed."

menu_cam_diag.help:
"Log the camera the game hands to the renderer (mode id, position, matrix "
    "rows) once per mode change, and every shot this places. Turn on if a shot "
    "does not show up or points the wrong way."

mouse_look_log.help:
"Log what the mouse look does: the raw mouse counts and the view angles about every tenth of a second while it moves "
    "(at most 4000 lines). The changes of relative mouse mode are always logged."

show_test_movie.help: "Show the TestMovie debug button in the pause menu"

garage_tire_offset.help:
"Add a TIRE OFFSET row to the garage wheels > dimensions screen, editing "
    "the per-car TireOffset0/1 bytes retail parses but never uses."

squash_stretch.help:
"Squash & stretch the player's car like the \"Why's This Dealer?\" meme. "
    "Visual only — physics and collision are untouched."

squash_amplitude.help:
"Squash depth, 0..0.9. 0.25 = the body loses a quarter of its height at the "
    "bottom of the cycle and gains half of that in width."

squash_pivot.help:
"Pivot height in metres along the up axis, in car space. 0 = scale about the "
    "car origin (the body sinks and rises). Negative values push the pivot down "
    "toward the tyre contact patch so the car keeps its ground contact."

squash_up_axis.help:
"Which car-space axis is up: 0 = X, 1 = Y, 2 = Z (RAGE default). The other "
    "two axes take the anti-phase widening."

squash_traffic.help: "Apply the squash to every car in the world instead of just the player's."

string_dump_enabled.help: "Capture encountered strings to TOML for translation/modding"

string_replace_enabled.help: "Inject replacement strings from disk when available"

string_language.help: "Language code for string replacements (e.g. pt_BR, es_ES)"

larecomp_texture_folder.help:
"Folder the texture dumps are written to. Empty: textures_dump/ in the "
                      "mod folder (modloader/, mods/ or models/ beside the executable)"

time_of_day_hold.help:
"Freeze the world at time_of_day instead of letting the day cycle run. This "
    "is the on/off switch — the hour by itself changes nothing while this is "
    "off, so you can park a value and arm it later."

time_of_day.help:
"Hour to hold the world at (0-24, fractional), applied while "
    "time_of_day_hold is on. Takes effect every frame, so dragging the bar walks "
    "the sun across the sky live. Menu presets: 6.0 sunrise, 16.75 afternoon, "
    "17.4 sunset, 23.5 night."

time_of_day_realtime.help:
"Follow your computer's clock: the world sits at the real local hour and "
    "keeps up with it. Outranks time_of_day_hold."

weather.help:
"Force the weather. 'game' leaves it alone, including its own random "
    "changes; a named sky pins that one and stops the automatic changes. 'real' "
    "follows the actual weather where you are, refreshed once an hour — it "
    "resolves your location from your IP through ipapi.co and reads the forecast "
    "from open-meteo.com, so those two services see your IP while it is on. "
    "Applies live."

time_of_day_speed.help:
"Multiplier on the day cycle speed. Only applies while time_of_day_hold is "
    "off — a held hour does not advance at all. 1 = stock, 0 = frozen where it "
    "is, 10 = ten times faster. The stock rate varies with the hour (about 2 "
    "minutes per hour at midday, 3 at night)."

tire_offset_step.help:
"Metres of lateral wheel movement per TIRE OFFSET notch (17 notches, "
    "-8..+8, so the default spans about +/-10 cm). 0 disables the effect while "
    "leaving the garage row usable."

tire_offset_targets.help:
"Bitmask (decimal) of the per-wheel matrix blocks TIRE OFFSET moves: 1 = "
    "model+1088 (the tyre), 2 = +1344, 4 = +1600, 8 = +1856, 16 = +1920. "
    "31 moves all five; drop bits to find which block owns which part."

ui_color_buttons.help:
"Show the pause menu's color buttons (UI OPTIONS) as the garage's own "
    "PickColor: garage.xsf's color button, placed in the pause movie and "
    "driven the way the garage's Fillmenu drives it."

trigger_slip_log.help:
"Development: once a second while a car is driven, write each wheel's ground speed, slip speed "
    "and the wheelspin and lock-up amounts the trigger effects use to the log."

mcla_cam_log.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: while a scene's camera is running, log it every this many frames: scene time, position, direction, field of "
    "view. 0: only the cuts."

mcla_capture_audio.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: during a take the game's audio output is replaced by one that mixes exactly one video frame of sound "
    "per frame and writes it to audio.wav in the take's folder; the real device is given back when the take ends. The capture driver is put in "
    "front of the audio output when such a take starts, not before (a game with no take has the stock output). Off: nothing is installed, the "
    "real output plays during the take, in real time, and no WAV is made. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_audio_surround.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: the take's WAV has the six channels of the game's 5.1 mix (fl fr fc lfe bl br) instead of the stereo "
    "fold the real output plays. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_audio_timeout_ms.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: how long the game waits at its frame gate for the mixer's frames of one video frame before it goes on "
    "with a frame of silence for each that has not come (counted in the audio summary; three in a row stop the waiting for the take)."

mcla_capture_fps.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: a take at this many frames a second, from the next update: the game steps by exactly 1 / this "
    "whatever a frame takes to render, every frame is read back and the game waits for it before the next update. 0 ends the take. "
    "10 to 1000. A scene's capture key does the same."

mcla_fixed_step_fps.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: the game steps by exactly 1 / this many frames a second, whatever the frame takes (the engine timer is given "
    "the game's own tick count for it); the FPS limit, the step cap and frame pacing stand aside. No take, no frame gate. 0: off. "
    "10 to 1000."

mcla_capture_dir.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: the folder the take folders go in (a relative path is relative to the game's folder). Read when a "
    "take starts."

mcla_capture_name.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: the take's folder name when the scene gives none (a name that is taken gets -2, -3 ...). Empty: "
    "the scene's own name, else take. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_out.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: the take folder itself, exactly (it has to be new or empty); the take then ignores the dir and "
    "the name. Empty: <dir>/<name>. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_sink.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: what happens to a frame once it is read back: none (counted and dropped), ffmpeg (a pipe to the "
    "program in mcla_capture_ffmpeg: FFV1 in video.mkv), png (ffmpeg writes one PNG for every frame) or raw (video.bgra, B8G8R8A8 "
    "frames). A scene's sink wins. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_statelog.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: write state.csv in the take (the game's state for every frame: the scene's statelog on does the "
    "same). Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_ffmpeg.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode (sink ffmpeg): the ffmpeg program, a full path or a name on PATH."

mcla_capture_ffmpeg_args.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode (sink ffmpeg): ffmpeg's output options, between the raw input and video.mkv."

mcla_capture_ring.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: host buffers between the readback and the writer (2 to 8): the most frames that wait for the writer. "
    "Fewer are used when mcla_capture_memory_mb or the free memory says so. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_memory_mb.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: the hard cap, in MiB, on the memory a take holds (its GPU readback buffers and its ring, one frame "
    "each). The ring is cut first, then the GPU buffers; a take that does not fit with 2 + 2 frames does not run, and the log says what "
    "to change (a lower render scale). Nothing grows with the take's length or the writer's speed. Read when a take starts."

mcla_capture_ram_floor_mb.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: free physical memory, in MiB, that has to stay free. A take whose buffers would take it lower is cut "
    "down or refused at its start, and a take that sees it fall below stops with an error (an 8K take used up the PC's RAM). 0: no floor."

mcla_capture_lag.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: how many frames the game may run ahead of the readback. 0: it waits for frame k to be read back "
    "before it starts update k + 1."

mcla_capture_gate_timeout_ms.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: how long the game waits at the frame gate before it goes on (counted in the summary; three in a "
    "row switch the waiting off for the take)."

mcla_capture_virtual_clock.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: during a take the upscaler's history rule and the UI movies' pacing read frames x step instead of "
    "the wall clock. Off, a slow capture makes the upscaler start its history again on every frame."

mcla_capture_delay_ms.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: the readback of each frame sleeps this long (a slow writer, in milliseconds)."

mcla_capture_log_every.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT capture mode: a [cap] line with the costs of a frame every this many frames (0: the summary only)."

mcla_freecam.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: the free camera. The pad flies the camera (left stick moves, right stick looks, triggers up and down, LB and RB tilt, "
    "D-pad zooms and sets the speed, a stick click is fast or slow) and the game gets no pad input but Start, so the car does not drive. "
    "Back + A records the flight, Back + X is home. Off: the game's own camera."

mcla_freecam_record.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: record the free camera's flight into a raw track file (one sample a game update; ports\\scripts\\scene_cam.py turns it "
    "into a scene's camera track). On starts a file, off ends it. Back + A on the pad flips it. Only records while the free camera flies."

mcla_freecam_out.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: the file the next free camera recording is written to (replaced when it exists). Empty: freecam\\flight-<date>-<time>.cam.csv "
    "next to the game."

mcla_freecam_speed.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: how fast the free camera flies at a full stick, in metres a second (L3 four times as fast, R3 a quarter, D-pad left and right "
    "step it)."

mcla_freecam_look.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT: how fast the free camera turns at a full right stick, in degrees a second."

mcla_freecam_inertia.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT: how long the free camera takes to settle after the sticks move, in seconds (the turn and the tilt take half). 0: none."

mcla_freecam_log.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT: while the free camera flies, log its pose every this many frames ([fly] lines). 0: only the events."

mcla_cin_hud_alpha.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: how much of the game's own UI (HUD, map, phone, prompts, gamertags, world icons) the picture shows, "
    "from 0 to 1. 1 is the game's frame and costs nothing; 0 is the 3D picture with no UI; in between is a fade. The pause "
    "menu, the DEBUG menu, the race pause, the map and the F3 card are never faded. Frames whose UI the renderer cannot "
    "keep apart from the picture (loading, movies) show it whole. Plume renderer only. Live; a scene's hud keys write it."

mcla_director.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT DIRECTOR (debug): the game listens on 127.0.0.1 (loopback only, a token in the info file) for an agent's commands and runs the same commands as the Director panel (documentation/DIRECTOR-PROTOCOL.md). Live: on starts the listener, off stops it. A scene cannot set it."

mcla_director_info.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT DIRECTOR: a file name; while the listener is up the game writes director.json there (port, token, pid, slot, scene). Empty: no file."

mcla_director_root.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT DIRECTOR: the folder the Director's commands may write to, as relative paths without '..'. Empty: the game's working folder."

mcla_director_panel.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT DIRECTOR PANEL (debug): the Director's panel over the picture: a timeline with the scene's keys to drag, the free camera's keys by framing, rigs with sliders, cars to spawn and place, routes to record or drop and edit, the take's render button, and the routes and the camera's path drawn in the world. Every action is a command of the Director and a line of the scene file. Live; the key Ctrl+F12 (ui.bind.mcla_director) flips it. Needs mcla_director (the panel offers to switch it on)."

mcla_scene.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: run the scene file at this path: a full path, or a name looked up next to the game and in its scenes "
    "folder (.scene may be left off). Hour, weather, traffic, time scale and settings follow the scene's timeline; the file is "
    "read again when it changes. Empty: off."

mcla_scene_restart.help: "TRAILER TOOLKIT: a change of this number runs the armed scene again from its start."

mcla_scene_t.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: 0 or more holds the scene's clock at this many seconds on every update (stills, scrubbing); -1 lets "
    "it run."

mcla_state_log.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT: write one CSV row per game update (the player's and the scene's cars, the camera, the hour and weather, the "
    "clocks, the scene clock, the random number state) to this .csv file, or to state.csv in this folder, for take_diff.py. Rows "
    "are written while the player has a car. A scene's `statelog on` asks for the same. Empty: off."

audio_mixer_priority.help:
"Host priority of the game's two audio threads: the guest thread that mixes each 5.33 ms "
    "frame (the game's request for a higher priority is ignored) and the SDK's audio worker "
    "that calls the game for each frame: 0 = normal, 1 = above normal, 2 = highest, 3 = highest "
    "and registered with the Windows multimedia scheduler (\"Pro Audio\"), -1 = automatic: 3 on "
    "a PC with 6 or fewer logical processors, 0 otherwise. On Linux 1 to 3 raise the threads' "
    "nice value if the system allows it (it usually does not for an ordinary user). Takes "
    "effect at the next start."

fov_3p_scale.help: "FOV scale — 3rd person / chase cam (0.5 = narrower, 2.0 = wider)"

smooth_chase_cam.help: "Fix: Smooth chase camera boom interpolation at 60 FPS using continuous-time exponential decay."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Continuous exponential camera boom smoothing at 60 FPS

smooth_camera_transitions.help: "Fix: Eliminate camera transition jitter and 180-degree wrap flipping when transitioning between orbit, menu, and gameplay cameras."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Smooth camera transition interpolation & wrap fix

scale_camera_shake.help: "Fix: Scale camera shake intensity across framerates (60+ FPS) to prevent violent noise jitter during drifts, burnouts, and crashes."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Continuous-time camera shake scaling

camera_shake_scale.help: "Camera shake intensity multiplier (0.0 = disabled, 0.6 = balanced PC rumble, 1.0 = full console shake)."

debug_cam.help:
"Free-fly camera during live gameplay: left stick moves, right stick looks, triggers change "
    "speed. Gameplay keeps running underneath (drive, traffic, physics)."

debug_cam_sens.help: "Free-fly camera look sensitivity (radians/second at full stick)."

debug_cam_mouse.help: "Free-fly camera: use the mouse to look (the pointer is hidden and locked while it is active)."

debug_cam_mouse_sens.help: "Free-fly mouse look sensitivity (radians per raw mouse count)."

tune_field_probe.help: "Log every tune field name as it registers."
comments: // Diagnostic: dumps every tune field as it registers. Off by default -- it fires for
// every tune in the game (about 1100 unique names across ~28 classes) -- but it is the
// only way to see a tune's live layout, so it stays.

lzx_stats.help:
"Measure pgStreamer LZX decompression (XMemDecompressStream): per-2s window stats "
    "appended to <exe>/lzx_stats.txt. For diagnosing streaming stutter (South Central)."

stream_trace.help:
"Log every resource the streamer is asked for whose path contains this "
    "text, and whether the file was found.\n"
    "\n"
    "The hook sits one instruction after pgStreamer::Open returns inside "
    "sub_821E2940, where the resolved path is still on the stack at r1+0x60 and "
    "r3 holds the handle -- minus one when the file was not found. That pair is "
    "the only thing that separates \"the game never asked for it\" from \"the "
    "game asked and the archive did not have it\", which is the question a car "
    "that loads forever comes down to.\n"
    "\n"
    "Empty turns it off. `resources/vehicle` is the useful setting for a car; "
    "`/` logs every file the game opens, which is thousands of lines."

segment_trace.help:
"Dump the segment table of every resource whose file name contains this "
    "text, as the streamer allocates it.\n"
    "\n"
    "A resource does not arrive in memory as one block. sub_821E58F0 walks a "
    "table of twelve-byte entries -- destination, size, and the address the "
    "resource was built for -- and either allocates them one by one (each landing "
    "wherever the heap had room) or sums them into a single allocation, with "
    "every size rounded up to 128 either way. Every pointer inside the resource "
    "is then resolved by finding which entry's range it falls in (sub_8217D828) "
    "and adding that entry's own delta.\n"
    "\n"
    "So a buffer that starts in one segment and runs past its end is read as if "
    "the next segment followed it, and from the boundary on the GPU fetches "
    "whatever the heap put there -- a mesh that is perfect on disk and blades on "
    "screen. This prints the boundaries so a rebuilt drawable's buffers can be "
    "held against them.\n"
    "\n"
    "Empty turns it off. `/` dumps every resource. `>N` dumps only the ones "
    "whose segments total N bytes or more, which is the setting that works: a "
    "resource read out of an archive has no name to match -- that is what the "
    "fixup error means by 'Unknown file in an archive' -- and a rebuilt car body "
    "is the only thing in the game past a megabyte. Anything else is matched "
    "against the name."

inflate_trace.help:
"Log every call into zlibInflater's decode step, for the first few hundred.\n"
    "\n"
    "A repacked resource that never arrives leaves no other trace: the streamer "
