    "opens the file, reads it, and then either spins in sub_821BC140 or asserts "
    "that the stream is not in XCompress format. Both of those follow from one "
    "number -- how much input the decoder actually consumed on a call -- and "
    "this prints it. Read consecutive lines: input left falling says it ate "
    "something, output left falling says it produced something, and a pair of "
    "identical lines is the decoder refusing to move."

fxc_probe.help:
"Write the bytes of the two static rage streams' buffer (the effect loader's, at "
    "0x82860C18 and 0x82860C40) to fxc_probe_<n>_<stream>_<count>.bin in the working "
    "directory, once per distinct content, for the first two hundred.\n"
    "\n"
    "Compares what the effect (.fxc) parser is handed on two platforms: the same file should "
    "give the same bytes. Observer only; off by default."

input_probe.help:
"Log what the SDK's input system hands the game for users 0 to 3 whenever it changes: "
    "the status, the packet number, the buttons and the sticks. Off by default. Polling it "
    "pumps the same input path the game uses, so it can only make a pad look better, never worse; "
    "if a pad shows nothing here, the game gets nothing either."

display_gamma.help:
"Display gamma ramp. tv: the console's for an HDTV (BT.709), as the game ships. pc: sRGB, "
    "for PC monitors, with brighter shadows. Live."

frame_pacing.help:
"1: every frame stays on screen for exactly the time step the game simulated it with -- the "
    "renderer holds a frame that is ready early until its planned time, and the game steps by the "
    "planned interval. Stops the camera's back-and-forth jumps when the game does not hold the FPS "
    "LIMIT, for a few milliseconds of latency. 0: the step is the measured frame time and frames are "
    "shown when ready, as before. Needs the Plume renderer, and is idle with mcla_gpu_vsync."

real_frame_delta.help:
"Feeds the simulation the measured frame time instead of the engine's fixed "
    "30 Hz timestep, and unlocks presentation from every-other-vblank. Required "
    "for correct physics, camera and traffic above 30 FPS. This is NOT a frame "
    "rate cap - see fps_limit for that."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Enable 60 FPS by default

fps_limit.help:
"Frame rate cap in FPS (0 = uncapped). The pause menu offers 30, 40, 45, 50, 60, 120 and 144. "
    "While frame generation runs the cap counts the frames the game renders (twice as many are "
    "shown) and mcla_gpu_frame_generation_fps_limit is the cap instead."
comments: // Default to 60 FPS: with vsync=false for low input lag and fast pacing,
// the precision frame limiter caps to 60 FPS out-of-the-box.

frame_limit_spin.help:
"Hit the frame-limit deadline with a PAUSE spin. Off restores the sleep-then-yield wait, "
    "which gives the core back instead of burning it."

vsync_fast_poll.help:
"Drive the SDK's gpu_vsync_fast_poll. With vsync off the guest vblank interval is 1 ms, so "
    "fast poll keeps the GPU VSync worker spinning a whole core. Off restores the 1 ms sleep."

intro_original_speed.help:
"Present the start-up legal screens and logos 30 times a second, as the console does. "
    "They are drawn by a loop that never runs the engine timer, so fps_limit never reached "
    "them and they played as fast as the host could present. The screens play before the "
    "pause menu can be opened, so a change made there is seen at the next start."

pace_at_swap.help:
"Hold each frame to the FPS limit right before it is presented instead of before the "
    "game's update: even present intervals (best on a variable refresh display), at the cost "
    "of up to one more frame of input latency."
comments: // Where the frame limiter waits. The game updates on its main loop
// (sub_82131508) and presents from "[MC] Render Thread" (sub_82306238), one
// frame behind. Waiting before the update leaves the present wherever the
// render work ends it, so frames reach the screen at uneven intervals; waiting
// just before the swap presents them evenly, and the queue between the two
// threads holds the update back to the same interval. The cost is latency: the
// update then runs up to a frame ahead of what is on screen.

render_cpu_mask.help:
"Which of the small render-thread CPU savings run, as bits: 1 the per-draw timers of the statistics read the "
    "clock on one draw in seven (instead of every draw), 2 the check whether a physical range of the guest's memory is "
    "readable asks the address alias that answered last first, 4 the lookups by device address in the constant banks "
    "and the constant upload keep their last answer, 8 the side-view rule check of a depth target keeps its last answer. "
    "0 runs all of them as they were (the A/B switch); 15 is the default. None of them changes a picture or a frame. "
    "Read at start."

fence_spin_throttle.help:
"Yield the host CPU inside the guest's D3D fence poll (sub_82412F98) instead of running "
    "its 32 pipeline-throttle NOPs. Off restores the stock guest spin."

comments: // Live: Patch_DisableMotionBlur reads this at the two sites that load the blur's enable flag, on
// every pass through them (nothing keeps a copy), and the pause menu's MOTION BLUR row flips it
// without a restart. It was tagged kRequiresRestart, which made the F4 panel and the launcher show
// it as a restart setting.

disable_imposter_shadows.help:
"Far trees are drawn as flat cards, and each casts a baked shadow silhouette into the sun's shadows. "
    "False refreshes those silhouettes, so far trees cast shadows; true skips the refresh, so they cast none. "
    "Daylight only, and only while perf_no_shadows is false (the pause menu's SHADOWS is on)."
comments: // Live: Patch_DisableImposterShadows reads this on every pass through its site in the imposter
// shadow submission (sub_8230C860) and nothing keeps a copy; the same hook is a plain, switchable
// toggle in the fork (its FOLIAGE SHADOWS row has no restart mark and was measured switching during
// play). It was tagged kRequiresRestart, and its pause row said "(RESTART)".
// CHECK: in daylight, FOLIAGE SHADOWS flipped in the pause menu shows after resuming, no restart.
// The row is on LIGHTING AND SHADOWS right after SHADOWS and is grey while SHADOWS is off (the sun's shadow maps are not drawn then).
// CHECK: the hook only skips the refresh, so flipped to true while playing the silhouettes already baked may stay in use (perf\LEGACY-GFX-AUDIT.md B9).

lod_traffic_scale.help:
"How far away traffic cars keep their detailed models, as a multiple of the original distance. "
    "0 (auto, the default) is 3.0 on a high-end graphics card, 2.0 on a mid-range one and 1.5 on integrated graphics. "
    "Higher keeps the detail longer and costs processor time; lower simplifies it sooner (0.1 to 10; the menu has "
    "auto, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3 and 5)."
comments: // 0 is auto (gpu/gpu_class.h): 3.0 on a high-end graphics card, 2.0 on a mid-range one, 1.5 on integrated graphics and until the
// card is known. The scale multiplies the game's own distances for a traffic car (Patch_ScaleTrafficLOD, at 0x827903E0 in the
// car's LOD pick): at 1.0 the most detailed model ends at about 40 m and the middle one at about 155 m, the coarsest goes on to
// the 500 m where the car is not drawn. 3.0 puts the steps at 120 m and 465 m; more only pushes the second step past the cull.

lod_city_scale.help:
"How far away buildings and other city scenery keep their detail, as a multiple of the original "
    "distance. 0 (auto, the default) is 2.0 on a mid-range or high-end graphics card and 1.0 (the "
    "original) on integrated graphics. 2.0 shows every loaded part of the city in full detail, so "
    "higher adds nothing and costs memory and speed; lower simplifies it sooner (0.1 to 10; the menu "
    "has auto, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2)."
comments: // 0 is auto (gpu/gpu_class.h): 2.0 on a mid-range or high-end graphics card, the game's own 1.0 on
// integrated graphics and until the card is known. A city sector is drawn in detail when it is loaded
// and nearer than 300 m times this scale times a camera factor (up to 1.5), and the city is loaded up to
// 600 m out, so 2.0 already shows every loaded sector in detail and more adds nothing.

aspect_ratio.help:
"Shape of the picture: auto fills the window at any shape (a 21:9 or 32:9 window gets a wider view, "
    "a 16:10, 4:3 or taller one more above and below; the HUD stays 16:9 in the middle), or 16:9, "
    "16:10, 21:9 or 32:9 whatever the window is, with black bars above and below where the window is "
    "narrower than that shape and at the sides where it is wider."
comments: // "auto" is the window's own shape, whatever it is (mc_engine/ultrawide.h): wider than 16:9 widens the
// view and keeps the HUD 16:9 in the middle (hud_width, below, moves its corner pieces out); taller than
// 16:9 (16:10 such as 1920x1200 or the Steam Deck's 1280x800, 4:3, 5:4, a portrait window) keeps the
// game's width and shows more above and below, the HUD again 16:9 in the middle. The others pick a shape
// whatever the window is: the picture lies in the largest frame of that shape in the window, centred,
// with pure black bars where the window is not that shape (mc_engine/frame_fit.h). Live: the pause
// menu's DISPLAY > ASPECT RATIO and the launcher write it while the game runs. The Xenia renderer
// always follows the window, and keeps 16:9 with bars in a window taller than that.

hud_width.help:
"On a wide picture, how far the HUD's corner pieces (the minimap, speedometer, race position, lap "
    "and time, and the phone) move out toward the screen edges, in percent: 0 (Centered) keeps the whole HUD in the "
    "middle 16:9, 50 (Wider) is halfway, 100 (Full) puts each piece as far from its edge as on a 16:9 "
    "screen."
comments: // Live, and only on a picture wider than 16:9 (mc_engine/ultrawide.h, "the HUD's corner pieces"): the
// guest hooks read it when a piece is drawn and the renderer when it squeezes the piece's draws.
// The pause menu (INTERFACE > UI, HUD WIDTH) and the launcher name three steps: CENTERED 0, WIDER 50,
// FULL 100.

single_tile.help:
"Render the scene in a single predicated-tiling tile instead of two. Halves draw calls "
    "and state traffic with MSAA on. Requires the enlarged virtual EDRAM (SDK >= this build)."

submit_on_primary_buffer_end.help:
"Drive the SDK's d3d12_submit_on_primary_buffer_end. Ends a D3D12 submission at every PM4 "
    "primary buffer end instead of batching the frame. Measured ~7% slower on a GTX 1650. "
    "With graphics_backend = vulkan the SDK's own vulkan_submit_on_primary_buffer_end (on by "
    "default) applies instead; not measured here, so it is left alone."
comments: // Off, because it was measured off. e0d9e94 turned the SDK flag on for the
// overlap it is supposed to buy, but on the bench (menu_cam slot 8, 40-116 s,
// three interleaved pairs against a build of ac2453d - the commit before that
// batch - with the same SDK DLLs) it costs about 7%:
//   this build, flag off           40.88 fps  (40.75 / 40.68 / 41.20)
//   this build, flag on            38.04 fps  (37.72 / 38.25 / 38.15)
// Ending a submission at every PM4 primary buffer end trades one batched
// submit per frame for many small ones; the driver overhead of the extra
// ExecuteCommandLists and fence signals outweighs the overlap here. It may
// still win on a faster GPU, which is why this stays a cvar instead of a
// deletion - set it true in larecomp.toml to measure that.

lowcpu_probe.help:
"Every 10 s, two lines in the log about a PC with few cores: how late the game's audio callback "
    "and its 1 ms clock tick were (counts of gaps over 8, 12 and 20 ms, clock staleness) and the "
    "CPU time of the audio worker and the timer-queue thread. Only reads. For crackling sound and "
    "stutter when the processor is busy: start the game with it, reproduce the problem, send the "
    "log."

lzx_native.help:
"Decompress the game's streamed resources (LZX) with native code instead of the recompiled "
    "XMemDecompressStream.\n"
    "\n"
    "The first streams are decoded by both and compared; any difference switches the native decoder "
    "off for the rest of the session. Read at start."

host_helpers_mask.help:
"Which of the game's small helper functions run as native host code instead of the recompiled "
    "version, as bits: 1 memcpy, 2 memset, 4 the row writer, 8 the shader-constant copy, 16 the "
    "constant-bank flush, 32 the C runtime's memcpy, 64 the fetch-constant bank flush, 128 the register block "
    "write. 0 runs all of them recompiled (the A/B switch); 255 is the default (63 = the first six only). A call "
    "the native version cannot reproduce exactly (overlapping ranges, register or physical-window "
    "addresses, a command-ring wrap) always goes to the recompiled code. Read at start."

lzx_native_check_all.help:
"Run the recompiled LZX decoder next to the native one for every stream, not only the first few, "
    "and compare every call. Slower than either alone: for validating a whole session. Read at start."

mcla_fast_exit.help:
"Fix: the game ends its process right after its orderly shutdown (saves, settings and logs written, the renderer "
    "and audio stopped), without running the destructors of its global objects. The SDK leaves a game thread that is "
    "slow to leave running while the game ends; a thread like that could still use an object the exit had just "
    "destroyed, and the game crashed a few milliseconds after it said it was exiting (about once in 1400 exits). On: "
    "the process ends at once, with the same exit code. Off: the old end through the C runtime's exit."

mcla_skip_gpu_teardown.help:
"Leave the final GPU objects for the OS to reclaim at process exit. Requires mcla_fast_exit. "
    "GPU validation, debug builds and device loss use full teardown. Read at quit."

mcla_fix_checkpoint_fade.help:
"Fix: the smoke of a closed race checkpoint dissipates over about half a second at every frame "
    "rate. The game fades it by dt x 25 at every update, which is 0.83 per update on the console's 30 updates a "
    "second but 0.42 at 60 FPS and 0.17 at 144 FPS, so above 30 FPS the smoke vanished with the checkpoint. On: the "
    "same decay per second as the console at any frame rate. Off: the game's own number at every update."

mcla_fix_neon_30hz.help:
"Fix: the neon underglow's pulse follows the console's 30 Hz clock, not every frame. A fast flash "
    "rate is a wave of about 30 Hz; the console sampled it 30 times a second and showed a slow throb, "
    "and at 60 FPS or more the same wave blinks about 11 times a second (a strobe). On: every frame "
    "rate shows the console's throb. Off: the pulse is worked out at every frame."

mcla_fix_neon_pulse_pin.help:
"Diagnostic (the neon underglow's pulse, for tests): a number from 0 to 1 that every flashing neon shows at every update, whatever the game's clock, so that two runs of a scene "
    "show the same underglow (the pulse is a function of the clock, and a picture A/B of the neon's light cannot be judged when it differs by run). Below 0 (the default): the game's own pulse. Live."

photo_album_keep_new_preview.help:
"Fix: while choosing the slot for a new photo, the album shows the photo you just "
    "took -- in the big picture and pulsing in the highlighted slot -- instead of the "
    "last saved photo the cursor passed over. The game decodes every photo into one "
    "shared preview image, and in the slot picker it let the slots overwrite the new "
    "one."

photo_ui_trace.help:
"Log the UI statechart while the photo album scene is up (photo mode, the album, "
    "the Rate My Ride snapshots): events posted and dispatched, delayed events, the "
    "UI.* and photoAlbum.* commands with the states they touch, and the paced movies' "
    "frame counts every 10 seconds. Silent everywhere else."

photo_album_export.help:
"The photo album's PUBLISH ALBUM button becomes EXPORT ALBUM: it saves every photo "
    "in the album as a JPEG in photo_album_export_dir instead of uploading the album to "
    "the Social Club (closed). Photos already in the folder are not written twice."

photo_album_export_dir.help: "Folder EXPORT ALBUM writes the photos to. Empty = Pictures\\LARecomp."

photo_auto_readback.help:
"Fix: photo mode previews show an old frame or garbage. The game takes its "
    "picture on the CPU, by locking the front buffer and JPEG-encoding it, so it "
    "needs the GPU resolve copied back to guest memory. This asks for a readback "
    "of just the two front buffers for a few frames around each shot, instead of "
    "the global readback_resolve cvar which stalls every resolve of every frame "
    "(on an SDK without the scoped readback, the global one for about a second "
    "around each shot). Leave ON."

photo_readback_debug.help:
"Diagnostics for photo_auto_readback: logs the photo album state machine's "
    "phase transitions and the front buffer addresses the readback is armed for. "
    "Pair with the GPU-side gpu_log_resolve_readback_misses to see whether the "
    "resolve that fills the front buffer actually lands in the armed range."

thread_qos.help:
"Windows 10 1709 or later. 0 = off (default). 1 = requests HighQoS for the game process "
    "(execution speed throttling off) while its window has focus. Windows manages process "
    "throttling again when focus is lost and always chooses which cores run the threads. "
    "2 = also requests HighQoS for the render thread, audio threads and frame generation pacer "
    "for the whole session. On hybrid CPUs, level 2 selects Pro Audio when audio_mixer_priority "
    "is automatic (-1). An explicit audio_mixer_priority overrides the Pro Audio choice. "
    "-1 = automatic (level 1). The log's [qos] lines say what was applied. "
    "Takes effect at the next start. See perf/HYBRID-QOS.md."

pump_wake_on_demand.help:
"The game's frame-pacing thread (it frees the draw command ring's slots and sleeps out "
    "7 ms a round) comes round at once when the main thread is waiting for a slot, instead of "
    "after its Sleep. Lifts the frame rate an uncapped game was held to when a frame takes "
    "less than 7 ms; changes nothing under a frame rate cap below that. Needs 4 or more "
    "logical processors, and a watchdog on the audio mixer turns it off if the audio runs "
    "dry. Off is the game's own Sleep."

rearview.help:
"Show the rear view mirror at the top right of the screen (a feature the retail game "
    "ships switched off). Takes effect immediately."

rearview_position.help:
"Where the mirror sits: stock (under the race position, top right), left_top, middle_top, "
    "left_down, middle_footer or right_down."

rearview_frame.help:
"Draw the mirror's frame. The retail game ships the frame meshes without their textures "
    "(black_small.dds and rearView.dds are gone), so the frame comes out solid white. Off hides "
    "it and leaves just the mirror view. Takes effect immediately."

rearview_cars.help:
"Show the racers' cars in the mirror. Retail's mirror phase leaves them out, and the game only "
    "treats a car as visible when the main camera sees it, so this runs the car's visibility test "
    "again with the mirror's camera and draws it with the colour pass. Don't combine it with "
    "rearview_traffic: traffic draws the same cars as black silhouettes. Needs rearview on."

rearview_traffic.help:
"Put ambient traffic back in the mirror's phase, where retail has it. It draws nothing useful "
    "there (cars show up as black silhouettes, or not at all) and a car close to the mirror's "
    "camera blacks the view out, so it is taken out of the phase unless this is on. Needs rearview on."

rearview_diag.help:
"Log, every couple of seconds, how many objects each render client holds when the mirror's "
    "phase begins. For working out why cars and traffic do not draw in it."

rearview_shift_x.help:
"Fine-tunes the mirror and its frame horizontally on top of rearview_position, in 1280x720 "
    "pixels. Negative is left."

rearview_shift_y.help:
"Fine-tunes the mirror and its frame vertically on top of rearview_position, in 1280x720 "
    "pixels. Positive is down."

rearview_window_dx.help:
"Offset of the scene viewport from the frame window's outer corner, horizontally, in pixels. "
    "The window's left and right edges lean, so the viewport rectangle has to start inside the "
    "narrowest part or its corner pokes out of the frame."

rearview_window_dy.help: "Offset of the scene viewport from the frame window's outer corner, vertically, in pixels."

rearview_window_w.help:
"Width of the scene viewport in pixels. The widest rectangle that fits inside the leaning "
    "window is 229 wide."

rearview_window_h.help:
"Height of the scene viewport in pixels. The widest rectangle that fits inside the leaning "
    "window is 44 tall."

perf_no_shadows.help:
"Drop every real-time shadow render phase. Largest single framerate win; the world "
    "loses cast shadows. Applied straight to the renderer's phase enable mask, so it "
    "takes effect immediately."
comments: // These reactivate the game's own dev command-line switches (see
// dev_options.cpp). They are not new code paths: the retail renderer still
// contains every branch, only the switch that reaches it was stripped.
// perf_no_shadows is the big one. sub_822E47E0 (the renderer ctor) reacts to it
// with `phase_mask &= 0xFFFF9E1F`, clearing render phase bits 0x20 0x40 0x80
// 0x100 0x2000 0x4000 in the enable mask at renderer+448. The phase loop in
// sub_822E6408 only dispatches a phase's draw lists when its bit is set, so
// those passes stop existing entirely: no shadow-map traversal, no
// shadowDepth/shadowAlphaDepth/shadowBlend technique draws, no shadow render
// targets. Restart-only because the mask is computed once, at renderer init.

perf_shadow_phase_bits.help:
"Render phase bits perf_no_shadows clears in renderer+448 (hex). 0x65E0 = sun cascades "
    "(0x61E0, what the game's own 'noshadows' clears) plus the night/blend shadow phase "
    "0x400 that it misses. 0x400 alone isolates the night path."

perf_no_race_shadows.help: "Drop the shadow pass during races only (dev switch 'noraceshadows')."

race_line_check_calls.help:
"With the native Race Line passes on: the first this many calls of each pass are also run by the recompiled function on the same "
    "input and the results compared; any difference switches that native pass off for the rest of the session (a "
    "warning in the log says where). 0 = no check. Read at start."

race_line_max_hz.help:
"The most often the game improves an AI racer's driving line (its Race Line job), per second and per racer. "
    "30 is the console's rate (it ran at 30 FPS); 0 runs the job every frame, as before. A job always runs in the frame "
    "where the racer's control points changed, so only the speed numbers along the line are older, by at most one "
    "interval. Live."

race_line_native_mask.help:
"Which of the Race Line's two hottest functions run as native host code instead of the recompiled version, as "
    "bits: 1 the backward speed pass (sub_8216CBC0), 2 the forward pass (sub_8216CDD0). 0 runs both recompiled (the A/B "
    "switch); 3 is the default. Their results are bit for bit the recompiled functions'. Needs FMA3; a call whose memory "
    "is not plain guest RAM always goes to the recompiled code. Read at start."

race_line_stats.help: "Log one line every 10 s about the Race Line: the jobs queued, skipped by the cap and run, and the time they took. Live."

race_line_record.help:
"Write the inputs of Race Line jobs to this file (a debug recording for the Race Line test: the planner's "
    "blocks, 61 KB a job; the format is at the top of hooks/race_line.cpp). Empty = off. Live; the file is opened by the first job."

race_line_record_every.help: "With race_line_record: record every this many jobs (1 = all)."

race_line_record_count.help: "With race_line_record: stop after this many records."

race_line_twin.help:
"Which version of the Race Line's two path functions runs (sub_8216E408 the headings, curvature and speed limits of the "
    "path's samples, sub_8216F900 the samples from the control points): 0 the recompiled functions (the default until a race has "
    "been checked), 1 the host twins (hooks/race_line_twin.h: the same instructions over a local register file, bit for bit the "
    "recompiled functions' results; the first race_line_check_calls calls of each also run the recompiled function on the same "
    "input and any difference switches that twin off), 2 check (every call runs both and compares; the game keeps the recompiled "
    "result; the log counts the differences and names the first). Needs FMA3; a call whose memory is not plain guest RAM runs "
    "recompiled. Read at start."

race_line_twin_mask.help:
"Which path functions take part when race_line_twin is 1 or 2, as bits: 1 sub_8216E408, 2 sub_8216F900. "
    "Read at start."

perf_fast_vehicle_shadows.help:
"Draw cars into the shadow passes with less detail (dev switch 'fastVehShadows'): the game "
    "skips the extra, more detailed draw it adds for each car's shadow. Use instead of "
    "perf_no_shadows to keep world shadows. Takes effect at the next frame that draws shadows: "
    "no restart."
comments: // Live. The one reader of the dev switch is sub_8235FA90, Vehicle::Draw's phase 0x10 / shadow-pass
// routine (feature-parity/GFX-UPGRADES-DESIGN.md 13.2). The recompiled code reads node+4 with
// `lwz r11,4(r9)` at 0x8235FB20 on every call and keeps no copy. The routine sets the car up at
// LOD 2 and, only while the switch is OFF, sets it up once more at the forced LOD
// (dword_827E624C, 1) before the draw: with the switch on the car is drawn at LOD 2. (That LOD 2 is
// the coarser one is the usual order of LODs, not checked.) ApplyLoadTimeDevOptions already keeps
// node+4 equal to this cvar every frame, so a flip reaches the game at the next shadow draw; the
// restart tag and "applies at the next start" came from the fork, which listed the switch among
// the options read at start-up (true for TREE IMPOSTORS and SCREEN BLUR, below, not for this one).
// CHECK: perf/scripts/chain-live3b.ps1 flips it in free roam in daylight and compares the car's
// shadow before and after. At night the 0x400 phase does not go through this routine, so nothing
// changes there.

perf_no_impostors.help:
"Do not allocate the foliage impostor render targets (dev switch 'noimpostors'). "
    "Distant trees lose their billboards. Applies at the next start of the game."
comments: // Load-time, not per-frame: sub_8230B778 skips allocating the ImpostorDepth /
// ShadowImpostor / ImpostorColor / ImpostorNormal render targets. node+4 is kept
// in sync with this cvar every frame, but the game makes these targets once, with
// the world, at start-up (the fork logged one world setup and 53 impostor setups
// at start-up and none when a race started or was quit: sub_82305230 ->
// sub_8230C388 -> sub_8230B778), so the change is seen at the next start. This
// said "the next load of that system" before, and the pause row "(ON RELOAD)".
// CHECK: toggled in the pause menu, then a district change: the impostors do not
// change until the game is started again.

perf_no_trees.help:
"Skip loading the prop/foliage set (dev switch 'notrees'). Last resort. Applies on "
    "the next district load."
comments: // Same shape: sub_82310478 skips the prop parse for $/city/<district> entirely.
// CHECK: when that parse runs. If it is part of the world's set-up at start-up, like the
// impostor targets, this too is seen only at the next start (tag, description and the pause
// row's "(ON RELOAD)" would then say restart).

perf_no_fullscreen_blur.help:
"Skip the full-screen blur pass (dev switch 'nofsblur'). Applies at the next start of "
    "the game."
comments: // Read once, at start-up. The recompiled code reads the switch in sub_82306860, the constructor of
// the post-effect object with vtable 0x820424B0: it stores `nofsblur == 0` as a byte at object+5
// (and `fastdraw == 0 && nomotionblur == 0` at object+4); no other reader of the node was found. The
// constructor is reached from the game's start-up chain (direct calls: sub_821305E8 -> sub_821BD7C0
// -> sub_82131790 -> sub_82131508 -> sub_822C2EA8 -> sub_823047D8; the same chain makes the other
// renderer clients), so ApplyLoadTimeDevOptions keeping node+4 equal to the cvar reaches nothing
// until the object is made again: a flip during play does nothing, as the owner saw, and a district
// load does not make it again. (An earlier survey read the harness's "applies on the next load of
// that system" as "applies at the next load"; the code says start.)
// Not a candidate for the phase mask (ApplyRenderPhaseMask): the fork's frame-structure survey puts
// the 0x2 phase on the 256x256 reflection view, and the blur passes (motion blur, the bloom blurs)
// are inside the post phase (0x08000000) with the bright pass and the luminance chain, so no phase
// bit drops a blur alone. A live switch would write object+5 of the live object (sub_823047D8
// stores the new object at `[r3 + 20]` of its argument) or hook the loads of that byte.
// CHECK: where the object is kept, which pass reads byte +5 and what it skips; none of that was
// run, and the row stays a launch argument until it is.

mcla_gpu_road_reflection_cars_test.help:
"Debug test, live, never saved: lets the game's own code draw cars into the wet-road reflection. 0 = off "
    "(the game as it is). 1 = the player's car. 2 = the player's car and the traffic. It opens the game's "
    "phase-2 vehicle draw (a camera mirrored about the player's ground height) only while a car is driven, "
    "not in a menu, the pause screen, the map or the garage. It may draw nothing (the car materials may "
    "have no reflection pass) and may thin out the other reflections while on; the log (\"[road refl cars]\") "
    "says how many vehicle draws went in."

disable_rubberbanding.help:
"Disable the AI RubberBand system outright. Note this also removes MinThrottle, the "
    "leash that slows the AI when it is AHEAD — so it makes races harder, not fairer. "
    "Prefer the rubberband_* scales under MCLA/Difficulty."

rubberband_dump.help:
"Write every RubberBandTune entry to <exe>/rubberband_dump.txt and flip back off. "
    "Read it before picking the scales below."
comments: // Applied on top of whatever $/tune/career/RubberBandTune00..10 loaded, to all
// 11 entries. 1.0 leaves the tune exactly as shipped.

rubberband_catchup_scale.help:
"Scales how hard the AI pulls when it is BEHIND: MaxThrottle, BehindMaxThrottle, "
    "HomeStretchBehindMaxThrottle, PlayerCloseMaxThrottle. Below 1 = less catch-up."

rubberband_holdback_scale.help:
"Scales MinThrottle, the throttle cap while the AI is AHEAD. Below 1 = the leader "
    "backs off harder; above 1 = it runs away more freely."

rubberband_level.help:
"Force which RubberBandTune level the AI races at: -1 leaves the game's own choice, "
    "0 = easiest, 10 = hardest. This is the direct way to make races harder — the tune "
    "index the game normally derives from your racer level and the race's base."
comments: // The 11 RubberBandTune entries are difficulty levels. sub_82743B30
// (RubberBandMgr_SetupRace) picks one into mgr+60: it starts from the race's
// base (mgr+56) and then, when the race got clipped down to the racer's own
// level, subtracts mgr+68 (2) — or adds mgr+72 (3) when the racer is below what
// the race asked for. The game's own `rubberband` dev switch (node 0x8290AC10)
// overrides that index outright, clamped 0..10, which is what this reproduces —
// written every frame so it also survives the restore path at the end of setup.

ai_difficulty.help:
"AI difficulty in percent: 0 = easiest, 100 = the game's hardest, each 10% one "
    "RubberBandTune level. -1 leaves the game's own choice. "
    "Ignored while rubberband_level is set."
comments: // The pause menu's AI DIFFICULTY row, in percent like Midnight Club 3's: the 11
// tune levels spread over 0..100, so each 10% is one level. -1 = the game's own
// choice. rubberband_level (the raw 0..10 index) wins when it is set.

rubberband_distance_scale.help:
"Scales the distance bands the rubberband reacts within: MinDist, MaxDist, "
    "BehindMinDist, BehindMaxDist. Larger = the band engages from further away."

rubberband_shortcut_scale.help:
"Scales DistBehindBeforeTakingShortcuts: how far behind you the AI must fall before "
    "it takes a track's alternate (shortcut) path. 0 = always takes them, above 1 = later."
comments: // AI nitrous policy. The tune gates nitrous on four distances; raising them
// makes the AI hold it instead of dumping the bottle off the line.
// Direction of each comparison is NOT confirmed by RE — the names and offsets
// are (parser registration sub_823990E0), and LoadTuning rescales two of them
// (+48 *= 2, +56 *= 2.5) after parsing. Read rubberband_dump.txt for the real
// numbers and try one knob at a time.
// Absolute, not a scale: measured across all 11 levels, UseNitroMinDistFromStart
// is a flat 100 at every one of them — the only field in the struct with no
// difficulty ramp. Scaling a constant tells you nothing about what you asked
// for, and 100 is short enough that even x8 lands inside the opening straight.
// Checked in IDA: the AI brain (sub_822BE670) takes a shorter alt path of the
// checkpoint list when its distance to the player is below -DistBehindBefore-
// TakingShortcuts (tune +40, racer+452). So the difficulty level DOES reach the
// checkpoints, through the shortcuts: a larger scale makes the AI wait until it
// is further behind before cutting, a smaller one makes it cut earlier.

rubberband_nitro_start_dist.help:
"UseNitroMinDistFromStart in world units: how far into the race the AI must be "
    "before it may touch nitrous. Stock is 100 at every difficulty level, which is why "
    "they empty the bottle off the line. -1 keeps stock."

rubberband_nitro_finish_scale.help: "Scales UseNitroMinDistFromFinish, the gate tied to the run-in to the finish."

rubberband_nitro_behind_scale.help:
"Scales UseNitroMinDistBehindPlayer and UnlimitedNitroMinDistBehindPlayer — how far "
    "behind you the AI has to be before it spends nitrous, and before it gets unlimited."

difficulty_preset.help:
"Whose AI rules races use: complete = the Complete Edition's, as shipped; original = the "
    "launch build's (December 2008), before the title update that eased it: the AI keeps its "
    "nitrous closer to the finish, the home-stretch hold-back is shorter, and the career "
    "difficulty starts at 3 and climbs and falls within the launch limits."
comments: // ── Difficulty preset: the launch build's rules ─────────────────────────────
// The disc build of December 2008 (title ID 545407F2, no title update) and the
// Complete Edition larecomp runs ship the same eleven RubberBandTune files and
// the same AI brain (mcBrainRacing, the throttle in sub_822BCFE0, the nitrous
// and shortcut tests in sub_822BE670 all match instruction for instruction).
// What the title update "improved AI balance" changed sits in mcRubberBandMgr,
// read side by side in both XEXs:
//  1. LoadTuning (sub_82743A10). The launch build uses the files as parsed. The
//     Complete Edition then doubles UseNitroMinDistFromFinish (+48) and
//     HomeStretchDistance (+64), multiplies UnlimitedNitroMinDistBehindPlayer
//     (+56) by 2.5 and moves BehindDistOffsets[2..7] down into [1..6]. The AI
//     stops spending nitrous further from the line, is held to
//     HomeStretchBehindMaxThrottle over twice the run-in, and needs to be 2.5x
//     further behind before nitrous turns unlimited.
//  2. The race-result step (sub_82742F28): a win adds points to mgr+64, 18 of
//     them raise the base level mgr+56 by one, up to a ceiling picked by the
//     race's tier (0..3); a loss takes points away down to a floor. The launch
//     ceilings are 5, 6, 8, 10 and the floors 0, 2, 4, 5; the Complete Edition
//  3. The base level a new career starts from: 3 in the launch constructor,
//     0 in the Complete Edition's (sub_82742DF8). mgr+56 is stored in mc4.sav,
//     so a save keeps whatever it had reached.
//  4. The script native RubberBandMgr_SetDifficulty wrote mgr+56 and mgr+60 in
//     the launch build and is nullsub_1 in the Complete Edition, whose career
//     script no longer makes the call that restored the base to 3 after the
//     hookman race that drops it to 0. Not reproduced: reviving the native with
//     the newer scripts would leave the base at 0.
// "original" reproduces 1-3: the raw parsed tune goes back into the table, the
// race-result step runs with the launch ceilings and floors, and a base below 3
// is lifted to 3 at the first race set up after the game starts or the preset
// is switched on (the launch build's starting point; a career that has climbed
// past 3 is left where it is). "complete" is the game unchanged.

script_pad_latch_ms.help:
"A script that asks whether a button was pressed only every few updates (the title screen's "
    "Start above 30 FPS) misses a press that comes in an update it does not look in. It is told "
    "about that press, at its next look, if its previous look was at most this many milliseconds "
    "before. Without it the button has to be pressed several times. 0 = the game's own "
    "behaviour: a press is seen only by a script that looks in the update it happened in."

showroom_unlimited.help:
"The garage's showroom lists every vehicle on sale. Off = the game's own showroom: 70 rows, "
    "and a picture for at most 7 vehicles past the game's own."

left_stick_deadzone.help:
"Dead zone of the left stick, in percent of its range: a stick that rests off centre (drift) "
    "reads as centred inside it. 0 = none."

right_stick_deadzone.help:
"Dead zone of the right stick, in percent of its range: a stick that rests off centre (drift) "
    "reads as centred inside it. 0 = none."

mcla_gpu_traffic_shadows.help:
"Traffic and the other AI cars cast into the sun's shadow map like the player's car, so the "
    "ground under them is dark (the game only draws the player's car into it). off: the game's own "
    "picture. near: the nearest few cars within a short distance of the camera. all: every car "
    "within a long distance (costs more graphics and processor time). auto (the default): near on a "
    "discrete graphics card, off on integrated graphics. Daylight only (the game has no sun shadow "
    "at night and in rain). Live: it applies to the next frame, to the cars already on the road."

mcla_gpu_traffic_shadows_radius.help:
"Diagnostic: how far from the camera a car may be and still cast into the sun shadow map, in "
    "metres. 0 is the setting's own (near 40, all 150). Live."

mcla_gpu_traffic_shadows_cars.help:
"Diagnostic: the most cars that cast into the sun shadow map at once (the nearest ones). 0 is "
    "the setting's own (near 4, all 16); at most 24. Live."

mcla_gpu_traffic_shadows_cascades.help:
"Diagnostic: the cars are drawn into the first this many of the four sun shadow cascades "
    "(each one costs the cars' draws again). 0 or 4 is all four. Live."

skip_intro.help: "Skip the intro videos to prevent graphical issues."

speed_units.help:
"Speedometer / distance units. Drives the game's own metric formatter "
    "(sub_8238DDF0): game = console profile default (mph on NTSC), kmh = metric "
    "(km/h, km, m), mph = imperial (mph, miles, ft). Converts both the number and "
    "the unit label; the analog dial tick art stays as authored.\n"
    "kmh also converts the live HUD speedometer, which does NOT go through that "
    "formatter: the HUD movie multiplies m/s by 2.237 in its own ActionScript, so "
    "hud_units.cpp rewrites that constant (and the per-glyph unit label) in guest "
    "memory. The radar detector's speed-limit sign follows it too, through the game's "
    "own km/h branch for it (rounded to the nearest 5), which the game never takes."

button_prompts.help:
"On-screen button glyphs. auto = the glyphs of what you used last, on every screen at once: "
    "PlayStation glyphs after a Sony controller, Xbox glyphs after any other, key caps after the "
    "keyboard or the mouse (the menu's keys while a menu is open, the driving keys on the road). "
    "xbox = A/B/X/Y + LB/RB/LT/RT, playstation = cross/circle/square/triangle + L1/R1/L2/R2, "
    "keyboard = key caps, whatever you use. Every set is drawn into the same button bitmaps "
    "(keyboard_native.cpp), so a change reaches a screen that is already open on the next frame; "
    "the UI movies' own 'platform' flag stays on Xbox (see prompts_live)."

prompts_live.help:
"Button prompts follow the device in use on screens that are already open (the garage, a pop-up, the pause menu). The UI movies are told they run on an Xbox, "
    "and the PlayStation set and the key caps are painted over the Xbox button bitmaps; a screen picks a changed 'platform' flag only when it is built again, "
    "so the flag cannot do this alone (KBM-P0). Off = the older way: the flag shows the PlayStation set, screens already open keep their glyphs until reopened, "
    "and only the keyboard's key caps are painted. A debug switch."

language.help:
"UI text language. The disc has five full translations in its own "
    "ui/mc4stringtable*.strtbl files: English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. "
    "The game picks its language from the console's user language, which here is "
    "the SDK's user_language setting (English unless it says otherwise); at start-up "
    "LARecomp sets that from this choice (en, es, fr, de, it), so the game's own "
    "language code, its achievement list and the Discord status all follow it. "
    "The setting itself is not saved to larecomp.toml, only this one. auto leaves "
    "user_language as it is.\n"
    "Switching in-game reloads the text table at once and tells the game its new "
    "language, but screens already drawn keep their old text until they are "
    "reopened (the pause menu itself too: the game resolves a row's label once when "
    "the row is built), and the few things the game reads only at start follow after "
    "a restart.\n"
    "pt (Portuguese) works only with a mod that supplies the text: the disc's string "
    "tables carry an empty Portuguese block, and on the disc it starts where the "
    "Japanese block does, so it would show Japanese text. A mod can fill it with its "
    "own ui/mc4stringtable*.strtbl files (modloader/<mod>/files/ui/): every string "
    "table the game loads from ui/ (mc4stringtable, _0001 to _0003, _tms) needs a "
    "Portuguese block with text. Until then pt is used as auto, with a line in the "
    "log, and the setting stays in larecomp.toml for when the mod is installed. pt "
    "leaves user_language alone: only the text changes, the game's own language "
    "code stays what auto gives.\n"
    "Not offered: Japanese (its UI movies, jp_*.xsf, are not on the disc, and asking "
    "for them is a hard crash)."

ui_movie_pacing.help:
"Flash movies advanced at the console's 30 frames a second instead of one frame "
    "per rendered frame. The game steps every UI movie exactly one frame per update, "
    "which on the 360 was 30 times a second; above 30 FPS those movies play faster "
    "-- the photo album twice as fast at 60. Comma-separated movie names "
    "(PHOTOALBUMMOVIE, POPUPMOVIE, PAUSEMOVIE, GARAGEMOVIE, NAVSYSMOVIE, ...), '*' "
    "for every movie, empty for none. The HUD is two movies, HUDMAPMOVIE and "
    "HUDGAUGE (needles, song ticker, race countdown); it is left out by default: "
    "stepping 30 times a second it would visibly lag a 60 FPS world, unless the "
    "frames between the steps are drawn (ui_interpolate, which paces every movie "
    "and ignores this list). Only movies the game steps one frame per update are "
    "paced."

ui_countdown_fix.help:
"Keep the race countdown (3, 2, 1, GO) in time when the HUD's gauge movie steps "
    "less often than the game updates (HUDGAUGE or '*' in ui_movie_pacing, or "
    "ui_interpolate on). The "
    "movie's script adds the last update's time to the "
    "countdown's clock on every step, so with 30 steps a second at 120 FPS the "
    "countdown ran at a quarter of its speed and a race began on the 2 or the 3. "
    "On, the clock is given the time of all the updates since the movie's last step."

ui_input_repeat_30hz.help:
"Menu cursor auto-repeat at the console's pace. The game repeats a held "
    "direction or button by counting frames -- the first repeat after 7, then one "
    "every 6 -- which on the 360 meant 233 ms and then 200 ms. Above 30 FPS it "
    "repeats faster with every frame: at 144 FPS a quick tap moves a list or the "
    "photo album's slot cursor two places, and holding it scrolls ~24 items a "
    "second. On, the count advances once every 1/30 s."

ui_advance_on_input.help:
"Menus answer a key press on the update it arrives in. A menu movie paced to 30 "
    "steps a second (ui_movie_pacing) would otherwise show the highlight moving up "
    "to 33 ms after the press, 17 ms on average. On, a menu key event (a press, or a "
    "repeat of a held direction) makes each menu, pop-up and map screen take one "
    "extra step in the update it comes in, and its 30 Hz schedule starts again from "
    "it, so the animations keep close to the console's speed. The HUD is not "
    "stepped for it."

ui_interpolate.help:
"Smooth UI. Every UI movie (menus, pop-ups, map panels and the HUD) steps at the "
    "console's 30 a second, so they run at the console's speed at any frame rate, and "
    "what moved in the last step is drawn between where it was and where it is: "
    "needles, the song ticker, the menus' lists and highlights, page changes and "
    "fades glide instead of stepping. The picture is one step (up to 33 ms) behind the "
    "game; nothing is blended below about 47 FPS. Off, only the movies named in "
    "ui_movie_pacing step at 30 a second and nothing is blended. A developer switch (the hidden debug "
    "menu's FIXES page): it is on for everyone and is never saved."

ui_interpolate_camera.help:
"With ui_interpolate: also draw the pause menu's 3D between the movie's last two "
    "steps: the camera that swings in when the menu opens, between its pages and out "
    "again, and the place, size and turn of the 3D panels. Off leaves them in 30 Hz "
    "steps."

ui_theme_accent.help:
"Replaces the blue/teal that every menu uses (selection bar, highlights, "
    "arrows) with this color, as RRGGBB hex. Empty keeps the game's own. "
    "Shades of the original keep their brightness relative to it."

ui_theme_title.help:
"Replaces the yellow of the menu titles and the spinning globe, as RRGGBB "
    "hex. Empty keeps the game's own."

ui_theme_frame.help:
"Replaces the gray of the menu frame, as RRGGBB hex. Empty keeps the "
    "game's own."

ui_theme_skip_movies.help:
"Comma-separated Flash movie names the theme leaves alone. The HUD movie "
    "shares the menus' teal and yellow in its speedometer; empty themes every "
    "movie."

ui_color_log.help:
"Log every distinct Flash UI color (movie, draw site, ARGB, bound texture) "
    "with a running count, to measure the families ui_theme_* recolors."

break_pairwise_collision.help: "Disables pairwise collision resolution. Live: the game's collision function is skipped " "or run again at its next call."

unlock_ride_height.help: "Allow the full stock ride-height table in the shop (down to rh_800 / -8)."

unlock_wheel_fit.help: "Allow every stock rim size, tire profile, tire width and ride height regardless of the car's clearance metrics."

smooth_chassis_depth.help: "Fix: Smooth vehicle chassis suspension and ground depth damping at 60 FPS."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Vehicle chassis suspension damping & ground depth continuous filter

smooth_vehicle_physics.help: "Fix: Continuous-time tire slip filter at 60+ FPS."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Continuous-time vehicle physics filters at 60+ FPS

smooth_bike_gyro.help:
"Fix: Step the motorcycle gyro's smoothing in continuous time, so bikes lean and settle "
    "the same at any frame rate."

vehicle_records_relocate.help:
"Keep the parts bought for each car model in a table sized to the roster, so the game "
    "takes more than 77 vehicles. Off = the game's own 77-slot table: past 77 vehicles it "
    "overwrites other profile data, and a large roster crashes the boot."

controller_vibration.help:
"Controller vibration. Off keeps the game's rumble from reaching any controller and stops a "
    "motor that is running."

extra_vinyl_layers.help:
"Raise the front/rear BUMPER vinyl caps from 16 to 31 layers each "
    "(64/64/64/31/31). Top and side caps stay at 64 because MCLA's vinyl "
    "composite pipeline hard-caps a single surface at 64 layers (fixed-64 "
    "work-area buffers; >64 overflows and crashes). Bumpers stay <=64 and keep "
    "their 5-bit save field, so existing garage/online cars are 100% compatible."

export_vinyl.help:
"Export the current car's vinyl layers to a .vgp file in <exe dir>/vinyls/ "
    "(auto-named vinyl_<car>_<timestamp>.vgp). Toggle ON while in the garage with "
    "a car loaded; it fires once and flips back OFF. Share the file; import later."

import_vinyl.help:
"Import a .vgp vinyl package onto the current car. Type the file name (found "
    "in <exe dir>/vinyls/, with or without the .vgp extension) and press Enter "
    "while in the garage with a car loaded. It overwrites the car's current vinyl "
    "layers and re-composites, then clears the field. Layers past the active "
    "per-surface cap are dropped (enable extra_vinyl_layers first for 31 bumper "
    "slots)."

vinyl_auto_readback.help:
"Fix: car vinyls only load outside the Vinyl Editor when GPU readback is on "
    "(the game builds the decal texture on the CPU from a GPU composite). This "
    "briefly enables the emulated GPU's resolve readback (d3d12_ or "
    "vulkan_readback_resolve) for ~1.5s around each vinyl (re)composite "
    "(garage entry / edits) so decals appear everywhere, while keeping readback "
    "OFF during racing for full performance. Leave ON."

dump_vinyl_shapes.help:
"Dump the vinyl shape catalog (every ShapeIdx -> source bitmap filename + "
    "texture header) to <exe dir>/vinyls/vinyl_shapes.json. Enter the Vinyl editor "
    "once so the shape library loads, then toggle ON; it fires once and flips back "
    "OFF. Used to build the image->vinyl decomposer's brush set."

capture_vinyl_shapes.help:
"Hands-free: force-load every vinyl shape a few at a time, hash each, and "
    "build the full ShapeIdx->hash map in vinyls/vinyl_shape_hashes.txt (+ .json) "
    "— no manual browsing. Enter the Vinyl editor (main menu, not a picker grid), "
    "then toggle ON; it sweeps all ~894 shapes over a few seconds and logs when "
    "done. Join the hashes to the DDS the texture dumper already wrote."

warp_transition_fix.help:
"Finish a cinematic warp (pause menu -> garage from far away) whose camera "
    "flight ended between two frames. Without it the game can sit on the garage "
    "facade forever: the warper only notices the flight's end by predicting it one "
    "frame early from a duration measured at a fixed 1/30 s step, and real, varying "
    "frame times slip past that prediction."

warp_transition_trace.help:
"Log every frame the warper spends waiting on a cinematic warp transition: the "
    "transition's time, duration, active flag and the frame delta."

warp_transition_test_miss.help:
"Testing aid: hide the running transition from the warper's own end check, so "
    "every cinematic warp ends the way the stuck ones do -- the transition finishes "
    "and reports it while the warper is not looking. With warp_transition_fix off "
    "this reproduces the stuck garage facade on demand."

enable_ambient_tuning.help: "Enable ambient traffic and pedestrian density tuning."
comments: // BadassBaboon's Recomp Adjustments: Ambient traffic & pedestrian density tuning for city performance

traffic_unspawn_dist.help:
"How far from you traffic cars are kept, in metres: a car further away is removed. "
    "0 (auto, the default) is 400 (the game's own) on a high-end graphics card, 300 on a mid-range one and 250 on "
    "integrated graphics. Less is faster (100 to 600; the menu has auto, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500 and 600)."
comments: // 0 is auto (gpu/gpu_class.h kScales): 400 (the game's own) on a high-end graphics card, 300 on a mid-range one, 250 on
// integrated graphics and until the card is known. A value set by hand is held to 100 to 600.

ped_density_scale.help:
"How many people walk the streets, as a multiple of the game's own amount (0 = none, 1 = the game's). "
    "-1 (auto, the default) is 1.0 on a high-end graphics card, 0.75 on a mid-range one and 0.5 on integrated "
    "graphics. Fewer is faster (0 to 2; the menu has auto, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5 and 2)."
comments: // Below 0 is auto, as for parked_car_scale.

parked_car_scale.help:
"How many cars are parked along the roads, as a multiple of the game's own amount (0 = none, 1 = the game's). "
    "-1 (auto, the default) is 1.0 on a high-end graphics card, 0.75 on a mid-range one and 0.5 on integrated "
    "graphics. Fewer is faster (0 to 2; the menu has auto, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5 and 2)."
comments: // Below 0 is auto (gpu/gpu_class.h kScales): 1.0 (the game's own) on a high-end graphics card, 0.75 on a mid-range one, 0.5 on
// integrated graphics and until the card is known. 0 is none, so it cannot be the sentinel as it is for the LOD scales.

global_max_draw_distance.help:
"fragTuneStruct::GlobalMaxDrawingDistance — draw distance for breakable props "
    "(poles, signs, fences). 0 = keep the tune file's value (3000); the engine's own "
    "constructor default is 250."
comments: // Both values live in the fragment tune the game parses out of
// $/tune/types/fragments (fragment = breakable prop: poles, signs, fences,
// barriers). They are patched in the parsed struct at runtime, so no RPF edit
// and no decryption is involved. 0 keeps whatever the tune file loaded.

breaking_frame_rate_limit.help:
"fragTuneStruct::BreakingFrameRateLimit — framerate floor under which the engine "
    "stops spawning new fragment breaks. 0 = keep the tune file's value (10); the "
    "engine's own constructor default is 30."

model_mods.help:
"Load model replacements from <exe>/modloader/<mod>/<asset>.obj (or mods/, "
    "models/). Each .obj is "
    "baked into a native drawable and packed into xarchive_mods.rpf, which is "
    "appended to the archive list -- the engine's own last-mounted-wins rule "
    "makes it override per file. Game archives are never modified."

model_mods_bone.help:
"-1 keeps a skinned mesh's own weights (glTF with JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0), "
    "matching its joints to the driver's bones by bind-pose position, so the "
    "model follows the seated pose. Any value >= 0 ignores the weights and "
    "rides the whole mesh rigidly on that one bone, which is all a .obj can do."

model_mods_offset_y.help:
"Extra height for the replacement model, in metres, on top of the automatic "
    "lift onto its bone. Positive raises it. Use this if the model still sits "
    "below or above the seat -- it takes a restart but no rebuild."

model_mods_offset_x.help: "Sideways nudge for the replacement model, in metres."

model_mods_offset_z.help: "Forward/back nudge for the replacement model, in metres."

model_mods_yaw.help:
"Turns the replacement model about the vertical axis, in degrees. Source "
    "models rarely face the same way the game does -- 180 turns a model that "
    "sits with its back to the wheel."

model_mods_pitch.help: "Tips the replacement model forward or back, in degrees."

model_mods_roll.help: "Rolls the replacement model sideways, in degrees."

model_mods_scale.help:
"Size multiplier on top of the automatic fit, which matches the model's "
    "height to the driver's. 1.0 leaves it alone."

model_mods_submeshes.help:
"Spread the replacement mesh across every submesh of the character instead "
    "of the largest one alone. The resource cannot be made bigger, but the "
    "driver is fifteen submeshes holding 8208 vertices and 37512 indices "
    "between them, against 2320 and 12957 in the biggest -- so this raises what "
    "a mod can bring by three and a half times, and most characters then arrive "
    "with no welding at all. Every submesh borrowed this way is repointed at "
    "the shader whose textures were replaced. Turn it off to go back to filling "
    "one submesh, which is the conservative path if a model renders oddly."

model_mods_decimate.help:
"Whether a replacement mesh larger than the slot it has to live in may be "
    "welded down to fit: a character, a rim, or a part replaced on a shipped "
    "car. A car built on a donor is always welded to its ceilings "
    "(model_mods_car_budget for the body) and ignores this. The slot is fixed "
    "-- for a character, the drawable's largest submesh, around 2300 vertices, "
    "and a few hundred on the low LOD -- and the welding is a blunt instrument: "
    "vertices that share a cell of a spatial grid are merged and averaged, "
    "which on a detailed model rounds off faces and hands. Off, a mesh still "
    "too big is refused with the reason in the log and that variant keeps the "
    "shipped model, so what a mod shows is what it brought; decimate it "
    "yourself in a modelling tool, where you can see what you are giving up. "
    "Expect the low LOD to be refused first, so the original driver reappears "
    "at a distance. On welds it in instead."

model_mods_proportions.help:
"How much of the replacement model's own build to keep when it is reposed "
    "onto the driver's skeleton, 0 to 1. At 0 every joint lands exactly on the "
    "bone it was matched to, which is what the game's skinning expects and what "
    "a human-shaped model wants. A model built to other proportions gets "
    "stretched to reach those bones -- a cartoon character with a six centimetre "
    "neck has it pulled out to the driver's twenty-six -- and raising this "
    "keeps its own bone lengths instead, taking only the pose from the "
    "skeleton. The cost is that limbs no longer end where the game thinks they "
    "do, so hands drift off the wheel as it goes up. Try 1 for anything that is "
    "not roughly human."

model_mods_textures.help:
"Use the replacement model's own textures. The images embedded in a .glb "
    "(one per material) are packed into a single atlas, each primitive's UVs "
    "are remapped into its own cell, and the result is written over the "
    "character's diffuse map in place -- same address, same size, same format. "
    "Off leaves the mesh wearing the original driver's skin."

model_mods_car_textures.help:
"Give a replacement car body its own textures. A car is drawn by several "
    "shaders of one drawable and each of them samples at most one image, so the "
    "mod's materials are grouped by the shader they were mapped to, packed into "
    "one atlas per shader with their UVs remapped, and written over that "
    "shader's colour map in the car's material packs (.xtl and .xtp) in place.\n"
    "\n"
    "Only shaders that sample anything get one. CarPaintCustomizable, CarGlass, "
    "BlackMatte and Chrome read no texture at all -- the effect decides that, "
    "not the data -- so their materials keep the UVs they came with, which is "
    "what paint needs for its vinyls to sit right.\n"
    "\n"
    "Off ships the donor's packs exactly as the game holds them, and the body "
    "comes back wearing the donor's own artwork."

model_mods_rim_autoalign.help:
"Put a replacement wheel on the game's axle, in two steps. First the turn: "
    "every shipped wheel spins about X and is half as wide as it is tall, so the "
    "thinnest axis of the model is taken to be its axle and rotated onto that "
    "one -- a wheel exported lying flat comes in standing up without anyone "
    "having to work out which ninety degrees it needed. Then the depth: a wheel "
    "is not centred in its own bounding box, it keeps its hub and spokes in the "
    "negative half of the axle with only a thin lip at the far edge, so a bare "
    "rim left centred sits sunk inside the tyre. Its face is pushed out flush "
    "with the shipped wheel's instead, turning the model around first if it came "
    "in facing inward. The manual rim angles and nudge below are applied on top. "
    "Turn this off to place a wheel entirely by hand."

model_mods_rim_keep_badge.help:
"Leave the wheel's badge quad as it shipped instead of silencing it.\n"
    "\n"
    "It is nine vertices on its own material, and that material is the only "
    "one on the wheel that samples a texture -- so silencing it, which is what "
    "the geometry rewrite did to every unused submesh, takes the badge off the "
    "car and leaves a mod's paint read by nothing.\n"
    "\n"
    "Off restores the old behaviour. Only mods that bring an image of their own "
    "reach this at all, so a wheel mod with no texture behaves the same either "
    "way -- which makes this the switch to try first when a textured wheel mod "
    "misbehaves and an untextured one on the same build does not."

model_mods_rim_shade_profile.help:
"Rebuild a replaced wheel's baked shading from the template instead of "
    "flooding it with one average.\n"
    "\n"
    "A shipped wheel carries its ambient occlusion per vertex, and it is not a "
    "small effect: measured across five of them the lane runs the full 0..255 "
    "with a deviation above fifty. Carrying it over vertex by vertex prints the "
    "old rim's spoke shadows onto the new one, so it was replaced by a single "
    "average -- which removes the shadows and every cavity with them. What is "
    "left is a rim shaded only by its material's specular, and because that is "
    "pinned to the geometry it sweeps around as the wheel turns and blows out "
    "as soon as the rim is painted.\n"
    "\n"
    "On, the lane is read from the template through coordinates that cannot "
    "carry a spoke: distance from the axle, depth along it, and how the surface "
    "faces in each. The shipped lane predicts itself that way to R^2 0.82, and "
    "read with a mod's own coordinates it gives structure of the right kind at "
    "about 60% of the shipped amplitude.\n"
    "\n"
    "It is not a reconstruction. Fitted on one wheel and scored against "
    "another's bake it reaches R^2 -0.09, no better than the flat average, at "
    "every grid size tried -- half of a wheel's bake is its own spokes, and "
    "there is no bake for geometry the game never saw. Off restores the flat "
    "average, which is featureless but is not a guess."

model_mods_rim_texture_mode.help:
"Where a wheel mod's own image is applied: -1 auto, 0 the hub cap, 1 the "
    "whole rim.\n"
    "\n"
    "A shipped wheel keeps no skin. Its metal is the shader and the baked "
    "per-vertex shade, and its texture is a decal sheet -- the maker's logo "
    "plus a few lug nuts and valve stems, most of it transparent -- sampled by "
    "a nine-vertex quad sitting on the hub. So there are two sensible things a "
    "mod's image can be, and they want opposite treatment.\n"
    "\n"
    "Auto decides on the image's own alpha, which is what tells the two apart: "
    "a badge is a logo on transparency, a skin has nothing to be transparent "
    "for. An image with real transparency goes to the cap alone, on the quad "
    "the game already draws there. An opaque one is taken for a rim skin, and "
    "the body is pointed at the textured material so it lands across the whole "
    "wheel.\n"
    "\n"
    "Either way the badge quad is left as it shipped, so the cap is never "
    "blank. Force the choice with 0 or 1 when a mod's alpha does not say what "
    "it meant."

model_mods_rim_band_profile.help:
"Carry the template wheel's material bands onto the replacement instead of "
    "flooding one."
    "\n"
    "texcoord1.x is the rim's material selector: xRimMain's VS_Common indexes "
    "materialHookups and tintColors with it, and PS_Multi then reflects a "
    "dual-paraboloid environment map through whatever material came out. A "
    "shipped wheel's body uses FOUR bands, and two unrelated ones put them in "
    "the same places -- band 1 is a ring at 0.82..0.88 of the radius two "
    "thirds of the way in, band 2 the outer lip past 0.93, band 0 the face and "
    "spokes, band 3 scattered accents. Flooding the dominant band gives the "
    "whole rim one material, and one material over a mirror is a mirror ball: "
    "the highlight sweeps round as the wheel turns. The bands are rings, so "
    "they are carried by nearest neighbour in radius and axial depth, each "
    "normalised to its own mesh. Only the band moves -- the colour does not, "
    "which is what separates this from model_mods_rim_inherit_shade."
    "\n"
    "OFF, because it does not beat doing nothing. Validated against ground "
    "truth by predicting one shipped wheel's bands from another's and counting "
    "per-vertex agreement: flooding the dominant band alone already scores 59% "
    "on the skyline and 57% on the bbs, and the transfer scores 61%/51% "
    "matching on absolute depth and 57%/70% matching on each mesh's own depth "
    "span. Neither normalisation wins in both directions, so the bands are in "
    "the same PLACES on every wheel without being predictable per vertex from "
    "where a vertex sits. Kept, off, so the next idea has something to beat."

model_mods_rim_shade_occlusion.help:
"Bake the wheel's shade lane from occlusion measured on the replacement."
    "\n"
    "A shipped wheel carries a baked lane: measured on three of them it runs "
    "0..252 with a deviation near fifty (bbs_ch 0..252 mean 155 dev 52, "
    "amer_razor 5..254 mean 186 dev 45, 5zigen_5zr 0..249 mean 144 dev 55). "
    "A modded wheel had none: flooding one average gives a deviation of ZERO, "
    "and the only shading left is the material's specular, which is pinned to "
    "the geometry and sweeps round as the wheel turns. That is what \"the "
    "normals change with rotation\" is, and it is not the normals."
    "\n"
    "The other answer -- model_mods_rim_inherit_shade -- carries the "
    "template's lane across by proximity, and lights the wheel NEON: the lane's "
    "colour is 0x000000 on every shipped wheel, so what moves is the UV1 band "
    "beside it, and a band picks a material (RimMaterialA..E). Scattered across "
    "a shape that does not share them, some vertices land on the emissive one."
    "\n"
    "So the lane is measured instead of copied or invented. Validated before "
    "being switched on: this car's rim comes out 0..255 mean 156 deviation 77 "
    "against a target of mean 155 deviation 52 -- the mean lands on its own, "
    "and only the contrast is pulled in. Off falls back to the flat fill."
    "\n"
    "Takes precedence over model_mods_rim_shade_profile, which guesses the same "
    "lane from statistics and which its own comment scores at R^2 -0.09 across "
    "wheels -- no better than the flat average it replaces."

model_mods_rim_inherit_shade.help:
"Diagnostic. Copy the shipped wheel's per-vertex shading onto the "
    "replacement, vertex by vertex from whichever original vertex is nearest. "
    "This is what a character replacement does, and it works there because the "
    "mesh has been reposed onto the very skeleton it replaces. A wheel shares "
    "nothing with the wheel it replaces, so what arrives is the old wheel's "
    "baked shadows printed onto the new spokes, and its four material bands "
    "scattered by proximity across a shape that does not have them. Off, which "
    "is the default, gives the whole wheel one band and that band's own average "
    "shade, both read off the template."

model_mods_rim_offset_x.help:
"Nudge for a replacement wheel along its axle, where one unit is the "
    "wheel's own diameter. Positive pushes it further into the tyre, negative "
    "pulls it out. Only needed when the automatic flush above lands slightly "
    "off for a particular model."

model_mods_rim_yaw.help:
"Turns a replacement wheel about the vertical axis, in degrees. Separate "
    "from the character angles because a wheel and a driver never want the same "
    "correction."

model_mods_rim_pitch.help: "Tips a replacement wheel forward or back, in degrees."

model_mods_rim_roll.help: "Rolls a replacement wheel sideways, in degrees."

model_mods_rim_scale.help:
"Size multiplier for a replacement wheel, on top of the automatic fit to "
    "the shipped wheel's own bounds. 1.0 leaves it alone."

model_mods_car_yaw.help:
"Turns a replacement car about the vertical axis before its parts are "
    "placed, in degrees. 180 is the normal value and the default: glTF has a "
    "model face +Z and MCLA has it face -Z, which is checked rather than "
    "assumed -- the shipped cars keep their headlights at negative Z and their "
    "tail lights at positive Z, and an exported car has it the other way round."

model_mods_car_scale.help:
"Size multiplier for a replacement car, on top of the automatic fit. The "
    "fit matches the length of the mod's body to the length of the body it "
    "replaces, and every part of the car is then moved by that one factor -- "
    "scaling each part into its own slot instead would leave a hood a size "
    "larger than the doors beside it. 1.0 leaves it alone."

model_mods_grow.help:
"Give a replacement wheel or car part buffers of its own instead of welding "
    "it down into the ones the shipped resource came with. The resource is made "
    "longer and the submesh is pointed at the new space; nothing already in it "
    "moves. This is what removes the detail ceiling -- a wheel slot holds 3,701 "
    "vertices and a modern wheel model is fifty times that -- and it was thought "
    "impossible until the streamer's read budget turned out to be what had been "
    "corrupting grown resources. 65535 vertices per submesh remains, because a "
    "submesh counts and indexes its vertices in sixteen bits. Characters are not "
    "affected: a skinned submesh also caps its bone palette, which is a separate "
    "allocation, so they stay on the path that already works. Turn this off to "
    "go back to welding everything into the shipped buffers."

model_mods_car_budget.help:
"The largest a replaced car body may be grown to, in bytes for LOD 0; the "
    "lower LODs get a quarter of it. Anything the mod brings beyond what fits "
    "is welded away, whatever model_mods_decimate says. It is a ceiling, not a "
    "size: a body that needs less is grown only to what it needs.\n"
    "\n"
    "Growing a drawable has no natural limit -- the mod hands over whatever it "
    "modelled and the resource follows -- but the game has one in practice. "
    "Counted over the 8849 vehicle drawables the game ships, the largest "
    "declares 1,163,264 bytes and the median 45,056; counted over body_lod_0 "
    "alone the largest is 884,736 and the median 266,240. The default used to "
    "sit just under that largest, so a mod could be as heavy as the heaviest "
    "thing the engine already streams and no heavier.\n"
    "\n"
    "It cannot any more. Each large buffer now starts on a block boundary and "
    "the padding counts against the ceiling; the shader passes are dealt their "
    "share in order, so by the last ones the padding has eaten the room: at "
    "4,194,304 the BMW came back with Chrome at 4 of 7353 triangles, CarLight "
    "at 124 of 2660 and CarGlass at 112 of 830. At 16,777,216 every pass "
    "arrives whole, a 7,340,032-byte body_lod_0, and the car drives "
    "correctly.\n"
    "\n"
    "0 lifts the ceiling entirely, which is the setting to try when you want to "
    "know whether size is what a car is failing on."

model_mods_car_pack_write.help:
"Write the mod's atlases into the car's material packs."
    "\n"
    "A probe, not a feature. model_mods_car_textures gates TWO things at once: "
    "the atlas, which rewrites the mesh's UVs, and the pack rewrite, which "
    "unpacks .xtl/.xtp, drops the atlases in and repacks them through "
    "BuildRsc5File instead of shipping the donor's bytes as they came. "
    "Switching that cvar off made a broken car whole again, which says the "
    "fault is in one of those two and not which."
    "\n"
    "Off keeps the atlas and its UV rewrite and ships the packs untouched. The "
    "car then wears the donor's artwork through the mod's UVs, which looks "
    "wrong on purpose -- what is being read is the GEOMETRY. Whole means the "
    "pack rewrite is at fault; in pieces means the UV rewrite is."

model_mods_share_images.help:
"Let two materials that name the same picture share one cell of the atlas."
    "\n"
    "A textures/ folder is keyed by material name, so a car whose three lamp "
    "materials all draw 750i_taillight ships three identical files and they "
    "take three cells. Collapsing them by content is free resolution -- the "
    "lamp shader went from six images in a 1024 atlas to two in a 512, which is "
    "128 pixels a material against 256."
    "\n"
    "OFF, because it is not free. Turning it on is the ONE change between the "
    "last build of this car that drew correctly and the one that came back as "
    "flat slabs, isolated by switching model_mods_car_textures off: with the "
    "atlas gone the geometry was whole again and the car merely wore the "
    "donor's artwork. Sharing a cell makes that cell cover the UNION of what "
    "every part sharing it asks for, which is the only thing here that changes "
    "a UV by more than a texel -- and something downstream of that is not "
    "surviving it. Until that is understood this stays off and each material "
    "keeps its own cell."

model_mods_cabin_light.help:
"Give a replacement car's cabin (the car-space part slots, interior0) the "
    "donor's per-vertex interior lighting, read off the donor's cabin vertex "
    "nearest each new one, instead of one flooded average.\n"
    "\n"
    "The colour word of a cabin vertex is how much of each of the car's three "
    "interior lights (siColor0..2: the interior neon among them) reaches it. "
    "Flooded with one average the BMW's cabin barely answered the interior neon "
    "being switched on. Off restores the flood."

model_mods_car_lod1_copy.help:
"Ship a replacement car's LOD 1 as a byte copy of the LOD 0 just built, for "
    "the body and for every part slot the donor gives a LOD 1.\n"
    "\n"
    "The garage draws LOD 1 close up. Measured on the BMW e38: the crumpled "
    "bonnet, the V cut into the plate and the bent grille in the garage are "
    "body_lod_1 exactly -- rasterised offline, LOD 0 is smooth and LOD 1 is that "
    "picture. LOD 1 was rewritten on a quarter of the budget, and a quarter "
    "buys 12,075 of the paint's 21,706 triangles through a clustering "
    "decimator, which is what crumples a panel. interior0's LOD 1 was worse: "
    "the donor has no paint there at all, so 10,138 triangles of shell were "
    "simply missing from it.\n"
    "\n"
    "A copy is what the game itself does for the Caprice -- its body_lod_0 and "
    "body_lod_1 are the same file, md5 and all -- and here it costs nothing: "
    "block rounding already makes both LODs of the body 2 MB.\n"
    "\n"
    "OFF rebuilds LOD 1 from the donor's own LOD 1 on a quarter budget, the "
    "old behaviour."

model_mods_part_probe.help:
"TEMPORARY diagnostic: every second, while the player's car is waiting to "
    "reattach its parts (car+6467) -- which is when the game draws none of it, "
    "wheels included -- log which selected part is not resident yet and the "
    "state of its stream (object, resource, handle, flags, state, refcount). "
    "See PartProbeLoop."

model_mods_glass_band.help:
"Give a replacement body's glass the pane number of the donor glass nearest "
    "each piece of it, instead of the dominant pane of the submesh it is written "
    "into. texcoord1.x on CarGlass says which pane a vertex is -- 0 windscreen, "
    "1 rear, 2/3 doors -- and the window film tints 1-3 only, so a body flooded "
    "with 0 takes no film at all. See MeshOffset::band_by_piece. Read at archive "
    "build time."

model_mods_part_growth.help:
"How much larger than the donor's own a replacement PART may be, as a "
    "multiple of the shipped resource.\n"
    "\n"
    "A part is not a body and does not need the body's machinery: the Impala's "
    "front bumper is 1731 vertices where its shell is three thousand-odd, and "
    "the whole of a car's sixty parts together weigh less than one of its LODs. "
    "Eight times the shipped size is room for a part modelled far more finely "
    "than the one it stands in for, and still small enough that nothing has to "
    "be dealt out between shaders the way the body's room is.\n"
    "\n"
    "1 keeps every part at exactly the size the donor shipped, which is the "
    "setting to try when a car loads without its parts."

model_mods_car_verbatim.help:
"Diagnostic, cars only. Copies each part's shipped file into the mod "
    "archive exactly as it lies in the game's own -- same bytes, same "
    "compressed length, same flag -- instead of decompressing it and packing it "
    "back. Everything else about the mod archive stays as it is, so this "
    "separates the two halves of a failure: if the game is happy with the "
    "verbatim copy, what it dislikes is the repack; if it still refuses, the "
    "repack is innocent and the problem is in serving a vehicle resource from a "
    "second archive at all. `model_mods_passthrough` cannot answer that on its "
    "own, because it still re-encodes the stream -- and an LZX of stored blocks "
    "is larger than the compressed original it replaces."

model_mods_passthrough.help:
"Diagnostic. Repacks the original character resource without touching its "
    "geometry, so the .obj is ignored. If the driver still renders correctly "
    "with this on, the packing path (LZX, archive, mount, flags) is sound and "
    "any breakage belongs to the mesh rewrite; if it breaks, the packing path "
    "is at fault."

model_mods_anchor_bones.help:
"Whether the repose plants each of the mod's joints on the bone it was "
    "matched to. On (the default) a hand lands exactly on the bone the game "
    "drives a hand with, and the body pays for it: a model's chest joint sits "
    "lower than the driver's chest bone, so the chest is hauled up and back "
    "while the collarbone barely moves, and the flesh between them loses 21 mm "
    "of shape -- the crease across the chest, the angular shoulder, and the "
    "belly pulled in behind a spine bone that sits at the back of a torso where "
    "the model's sits down the middle. Off, joints keep the offsets they were "
    "authored with and only turn: measured on the driver mod that halves the "
    "distortion, 5.7 mm to 2.8 mm averaged over every bone, at the cost of the "
    "wrist landing 38 mm and the foot 96 mm off their bones, which swings them "
    "on the wrong lever once animation starts. Standing still, off looks "
    "better; in motion is what only the game can answer."

model_mods_weight_smoothing.help:
