                    "wait for it with a timeout. The draw whose shader spins forever (the "
                    "DEVICE_HUNG TDR) is the one that times out; its vs/ps identity is written "
                    "to native_gfx_hang.txt. Extremely slow — a one-shot to name the culprit."

mcla_native_gfx_own_swapchain.help:
"Use NativeSwapChain (FLIP_DISCARD, tearing, frame latency waitable object) "
                    "presenting directly to the HWND backbuffer, eliminating intermediate blits "
                    "and enabling full ReShade / Reno DX DevKit visibility. Off by default: it "
                    "bypasses rex::ui::Presenter, so present_effect (FSR) and every ImGui overlay "
                    "(console, F3, toasts) are gone and the frame is stretched bilinearly. Needs "
                    "mcla_native_gfx_own_device."

mcla_native_gfx_disable_occlusion.help:
"Select the guest's no-occlusion path (byte_8288D5D1 = 0) while the native "
    "backend is active. "
    "MCLA gates a vehicle's body on an occlusion query: sub_82323808 keeps one "
    "slot per object, answers 'occluded' whenever a slot exists, and refreshes "
    "the very timestamp the reaper ages slots by -- so a slot survives only "
    "until the query completes and releases it. This backend has no command "
    "processor and cannot run the query, so the slot is refreshed forever and "
    "the body is never submitted again. Measured: the body block in "
    "sub_8235D500 is reached exactly once and never after, while the wheels, "
    "discs and exhaust keep drawing because their submit paths consult no "
    "query, and traffic shows only its contact shadow for the same reason. "
    "The game itself supports running with occlusion off (sub_82323808 returns "
    "'draw' immediately when this byte is zero), which is where a backend "
    "without query support belongs. Cost: geometry that is genuinely hidden is "
    "still drawn -- GPU time, never a missing object. "
    "Turn off only to reproduce the vanishing body, or once real queries exist."

mcla_native_gfx_own_textures.help:
"Resource ownership, step two: who allocates the 52-byte D3DTexture header. "
    "0 = the guest, as always. "
    "1 = mirror and validate: the runtime allocates the header out of its own guest-visible "
    "heap, copies the guest's bytes in, checks the guest VA translates back to the same bytes, "
    "then frees it. Nothing the game can observe changes -- this is the proof that objects the "
    "runtime allocates are addressable from guest code. "
    "2 = hand over: grcTextureXenon+16/+28 are repointed at the runtime's copy, so every guest "
    "read of that texture header reads runtime memory. The guest's original block is left "
    "untouched and restored at destruction, so its allocator only frees what it allocated. "
    "Covers only textures born in grcTextureXenon::Init; streamed ones are deserialized with "
    "the header embedded in the resource and stay with the guest."

mcla_native_gfx_own_heap_kb.help:
"Size of the guest-addressable block the runtime allocates its D3D objects out of, in KiB. "
    "0 uses the built-in default (4096). Rounded down to a power of two -- o1heap only uses the "
    "largest power-of-two span of its arena. "
    "Taken from the guest VIRTUAL window, never from a physical one: the physical windows are "
    "views of the console's 512 MiB of RAM, and taking 32 MiB of it killed the title during "
    "loading with 'PhysicalHeap::Alloc unable to alloc physical memory in parent heap'. "
    "Raise this if the exhaustion report fires."

mcla_native_gfx_texture_registry.help:
"Record every texture the game creates: name, dimensions, format, and "
                    "which road built it (a header placed over streamed resource memory, or a "
                    "real D3DDevice_CreateTexture). Observation only -- the guest still owns "
                    "and creates everything, the hook just reads the result. Answers what the "
                    "address-keyed texture cache cannot: which asset a given guest address is. "
                    "Overwrites mcla_native_gfx_textures.txt every 600 frame boundaries, so "
                    "the file always reflects the current state rather than the boot state."

mcla_native_gfx_vblank_probe.help:
"Read-only probe of the guest's vblank and flip machinery, for the port to a runtime with no "
    "command processor. Reports the vblank counter, the flip counter and the pending-flip queue "
    "indices in the D3DDevice, so the offsets the replacement will drive are proven while the "
    "emulated path still works. Writes nothing."

mcla_native_gfx_nocp_vsync.help:
"Frame pacing for the no-command-processor mode: on = the guest video mode's refresh rate, "
    "off = 1000 Hz, matching what the emulated path does with vsync off. "
    "This exists because the SDK's `vsync` cvar is defined in "
    "src/graphics/command_processor.cpp, so it lives in the GPU plugin and is simply ABSENT once "
    "that plugin is not loaded -- a `vsync` line in larecomp.toml is an unknown key in this mode, "
    "and querying it by name would silently answer false whatever it was set to."

mcla_gfx_probe.help:
"Milestone 0: passive D3D9-Xenon probe. Renders nothing, changes nothing. "
                    "Writes mcla_gfx_probe_*.csv next to the executable."

mcla_gfx_probe_frames.help:
"Milestone 0: number of guest frames to capture before the probe dumps its "
                     "report and goes idle (0 = never stop)."

profile_auto_select.help:
"Start with the save named by user_name and never show the save picker, even when several "
    "saves exist. The picker's 'Always use this save' box sets it; hold Shift while the game "
    "starts to see the picker once anyway."

skip_save_import.help:
"Skip the save import wizard shown on first launch and start with no save. "
    "The wizard is skipped automatically anyway when no Xenia or RPCS3 save is "
    "found on the machine."

mcla_gpu_car_chrome_occlusion.help:
"Fix: the chrome of the player's car (the tailpipes, the rims, the badges and trim) is not lit by what the car's own body covers. "
    "The game's chrome shader looks up the sky in the environment map and adds the sky's ambient colour wherever the surface "
    "points, and nothing in it knows the bumper over a tailpipe, so the tips, which sit 2 to 7 cm under and behind the parts "
    "that cover them, glow as if lit from above. This marches two short rays from each chrome pixel through the picture of the "
    "car from the frame before (the car self-reflection's image): one along the reflection, one towards the sky, and darkens the "
    "reflection and the ambient where they hit a part of the car, by up to 90 percent. It runs wherever the car "
    "self-reflection runs (mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl) and needs the shader pack's variant file. Off: the game's own chrome. Live; "
    "the first time it shows, the graphics card builds its shader (a short stutter)."

mcla_gpu_vram_budget_mb.help:
"Test (debug): pretend the video memory budget is this many MiB when the adapter's own is larger "
    "(0: the adapter's). Everything that asks the budget sees the smaller number against the real use: "
    "the caches' trimming (vram_budget.h), the room checks of frame generation and of the FidelityFX "
    "upscaler's contexts (vram_room.h). The way to see the NO ROOM paths and the trimming on a card "
    "that has plenty (a 4 GB card is 3900). Live."

fullscreen_resolution.help:
"With fullscreen and fullscreen_exclusive on: the size the display is switched to, as \"WxH\" "
    "(the nearest mode the display lists). Empty, the default: the display's own size, no switch. The "
    "window's size is `resolution`, which FULLSCREEN does not use: a size chosen for a window was once "
    "taken as the display mode and put the display in 1280x720. Windows only."

mcla_gpu_traffic_shadows_rotation.help:
"Diagnostic (the fix's own switch): the sun shadow of a traffic car is turned with its car. The game's shadow "
    "shader draws a car without its bone matrices, so the shadow of a car it was never meant to draw kept the "
    "model's own heading and only followed the car's position. off: the game's transform, as before the fix. Live."

mcla_gpu_traffic_shadows_log.help:
"Diagnostic: every this many frames print, for each traffic car drawn into the sun shadow map, a "
    "`[traffic-shadows] yaw:` line (the body's heading, the heading of the transform the shadow draw used, their "
    "difference and the car's turn rate) and, for each soft decal made, a `[traffic-shadows] decal:` line. "
    "0 is off. Live."

mcla_gpu_contact_shadows_car_sun.help:
"Diagnostic: where a car's pixel takes the sun's visibility from when the contact shadows work out the "
    "sun's share of its light. 1: from the game's own car sun image, the 256 m wide top-down image of the "
    "ground's sun visibility that every car shader reads for its colour (contact_trace.h), so a car in a "
    "building's shade gets no contact shadow of the sun's and a car half in it gets half; a frame without "
    "that image (6 h, 18 h, rain, night) takes 1. 0: always 1, which is a lit car's term wherever the car "
    "stands (the first fix for the comb under the R34's wing, for comparing). The game's screen sized mask "
    "is never used on a car: it is made before the cars are drawn and holds the world behind them. Live."

mcla_scene_seed.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT repeatable scenes: while a scene runs, the game's random generators (the simulation's, the cosmetic one, the car configuration's) are given a state "
    "from this seed and the scene's update number at the start of every update, and the renderer's noise (the occlusion's, the contact shadows', the sun shafts', "
    "the shadow filter's, the temporal upscalers' jitter) follows the scene's update number (while the clock is held by mcla_scene_t, the number of the held time): the same scene gives the same pictures in every run. 0: off, the "
    "game's own random numbers and the renderer's frame count. Read at every update of a scene."

mcla_scene_seed_each_frame.help:
"TRAILER TOOLKIT repeatable scenes: true: the generators are given their state at every update of the scene (a thread that draws a different number of times in "
    "one run cannot carry the difference into the next update); false: once, at the scene's first update. Read at every update of a scene."

mcla_traffic_probe.help:
"Debug, live, never saved: every this many updates log the ambient (traffic) cars one by one (model, position, heading, speed, the rail, "
    "the LOD), the ambient and layout pools (capacity, live count, free slots), the opponent and racer pools and the police patrols, and one "
    "SUMMARY line, all as '[traffic-probe]' lines. It reads the game and changes nothing. 0 = off."

mcla_traffic_probe_detail.help:
"Debug: how much of each traffic probe sample is logged. 0 = the pools, the census and the SUMMARY line; 1 = and the 20 nearest cars; 2 = "
    "and every car (up to 200). The census always counts all of them."

mcla_traffic_probe_spawn.help:
"Debug, live, never saved: a set to a number other than 0 (and other than the last one acted on) makes ONE call to the game's "
    "AmbientMgr_AddAmbientToLayout, asking it to place an ambient car of mcla_traffic_probe_model mcla_traffic_probe_ahead metres in front "
    "of the player, and follows what comes of it in the log for two minutes. Free roam only, with a layout slot free, at most three calls "
    "in a run of the game; a refusal is logged with its reason. 0 = off and re-arms (the same number again does nothing)."

mcla_traffic_probe_model.help:
"Debug: the ambient type (the car's model name in the game's own list, logged by the traffic probe as 'types') the spawn test asks for. "
    "Empty = the first regular car type of the game's list."

mcla_traffic_probe_ahead.help: "Debug: how far in front of the player's car, in metres, the spawn test places the car."

traffic_density_scale.help:
"Moving traffic density scale (0.0 = no new traffic cars, 1.0 = the game's own, 2.0 = double). It scales the "
    "zones' density at low and at high speed, so it holds at every speed. Live, for the cars that spawn from the "
    "next frame on; cars already on the road stay until they leave by the unspawn radius (traffic_unspawn_dist). "
    "Needs enable_ambient_tuning (on by default). Debug setting: trailers and repeatable tests, where the road is "
    "to stay empty (with ped_density_scale and parked_car_scale at 0)."

mcla_ui_minimap_scale.help:
"Draw the HUD's and the menus' small views (the minimap, the phone screen, and the page of the pause menu, the garage and the GPS map, which the game always draws at "
    "fixed sizes and the screen stretches) at the render scale, as the images of the screen are, so that the minimap and the menus' text come out as sharp as the rest of the "
    "picture at 1080p and 4K. At 720p (render scale 1x) it is the game's own either way. Off: the game's own sizes. Costs video memory while a menu is up (about 50 MiB at "
    "4K for the pause menu and the map). Live."

mcla_ui_sharp.help:
"Sharper HUD and menu art where the game's bitmaps are blown up (a render scale above 1.25x of the console's 720p "
    "picture: 1080p and 4K windows). The game's buttons, icons, panels and text are bitmaps made for the console's "
    "1280x720 picture, drawn with a bilinear filter, so at 4K every texel is three pixels of soft edge. This reads them "
    "with a sharper filter (Catmull-Rom on the colour) and steepens the alpha across a bitmap's edges so that glyphs and "
    "icon outlines stay about one pixel soft, like a distance-field font. Off is the game's own picture, bit for bit; at "
    "720p (render scale 1x) it is the game's either way. Needs the shader pack's variant file (ui_sharp). Live; the "
    "first time it shows, the graphics card builds its shaders (a short stutter)."

mcla_ui_sharp_strength.help:
"Debug: how hard mcla_ui_sharp works. 1 is full Catmull-Rom on the colour and an alpha edge about one pixel wide; "
    "0.5 is half of it; 2 doubles the edge gain (a harder edge, more aliasing). Live."

mcla_ui_sharp_census.help:
"Debug: every 600 frames, log the textures the HUD and menus read (the draws after the scene is composed, the "
    "menus' render-to-texture views, and the frames that have no scene: loading, title, movies): the pixel shader, the "
    "texture's format, size, name and dictionary, the sampler's filters, the render scale of the target and how many "
    "reads were magnified. What the UI sharpening (mcla_ui_sharp) is tuned from. Live."

menu_mouse.help:
"Use the mouse in the game's menus: moving the pointer over a row highlights it, a left click is A on it (on the left or right part of a settings row, the arrow: it "
    "steps the value), the right button is B, the wheel moves the highlight. The pointer stays on screen while a menu is up and the mouse is what you last used. Off, "
    "the mouse does nothing in menus."

menu_mouse_row_width.help:
"Debug: the width of a menu row for the mouse, in the 1280 x 720 stage's pixels. 0 = from what the row holds (never under 320). Rows the pointer is said to be on but "
    "is not (or the reverse) at the right edge of the list: set this and look again."

menu_mouse_row_offset.help:
"Debug: moves every menu row's place for the mouse up or down, in the stage's pixels (a row hangs from the origin of its slot; if the highlight lands half a row off "
    "from the pointer, this is the number: about -12 puts the origin in the middle of the row)."

menu_mouse_dump.help:
"Debug: log what the mouse sees of the menu that is up, once, and again each time this is set to true: the movie (its frame, the display state, the scale onto the stage), the candidates (the "
    "list and the UIMenu the game rendered last, their fields and counters), the clip tree's outline and every clip that holds slot0..slotN with each slot's local, world and stage "
    "place. For a menu that falls back: this is how its rows are found."

menu_mouse_dump_new.help:
"Debug: the same dump (menu_mouse_dump) once for every new menu the mouse meets (a new movie, list or UIMenu, or one that is read differently than before), fallbacks included, up to "
    "24 a run. For the tours: set it before the first menu opens."

menu_mouse_trust_layouts.help:
"Debug: use the rows read from the clip tree of a movie other than the pause menu (the garage's other pages, dialogs) for the hover and for clicks on rows. The garage's first menu and its two-row pop-ups do not need it "
    "(their card is fitted to pictures). Off: those menus are read and "
    "logged (`[menu-mouse] menu ...: FALLBACK (the layout ... is not checked against a picture yet ...)`) but treated as a fallback menu: no hover, a left click presses the highlighted row, "
    "the wheel and the right button work. Every page of those movies is a quad in the game's 3D menu scene whose size follows its list, so a scale and offset read from the clip tree "
    "cannot be assumed right (round 1: the garage's first row at stage (39.8, 75.3), in the picture at about (860, 233), rows 22.7 apart, not 35); a page gets a card of its own when its pictures are measured."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars.help:
"Debug: how many OTHER cars (opponents, traffic, parked cars) the ray traced car effects see besides your own: your car's paint and chrome "
    "reflect a car driving alongside. -1 (the default): the graphics card's class decides (the nearest 4 within 20 m of your car on the High class, 2 within 14 m on "
    "the Mid class, none on the Low class); 0 turns the other cars off (your car alone, as it was); 1 to 8 asks for that many. Each car is built "
    "once into ray tracing structures (8 to 10 MiB at full detail) and a new car appears in parts over a few frames. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_radius.help:
"Debug: how far from your car, in metres, another car may be to be seen by the ray traced car effects (0, the default: the graphics card's "
    "class decides, 20 m on the High class, 14 m on the Mid class). The reflection reaches another car 18 m (High) or 12 m (Mid) away (mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_reach) and a car's half length is 2 m, so a car whose centre is farther than the radius cannot show in it. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_rt.help:
"Diagnostic: the ray traced part of the ambient occlusion and the contact shadows, where the graphics card can ray trace (Direct3D 12 with ray "
    "tracing 1.1, or Vulkan with ray queries): a few short rays from the pixels near your car and the cars beside it, against their real shape, "
    "darken what the camera does not see (the far side of a wheel well, the body over a tyre, the road at the foot of a car and between two cars) "
    "and shadow the cars' own parts and the road from the sun exactly. "
    "auto (the default): both, where the ambient occlusion or the contact shadows are on; off: the screen-space passes alone, to compare with; "
    "ao: the occlusion's rays only; contact: the sun's ray only. A graphics card that cannot ray trace uses the screen-space passes whatever this "
    "says. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_rt_length.help:
"Diagnostic: how far the ray traced occlusion's rays reach, in the game's world units (about metres): what your car blocks within it darkens "
    "the pixel, less the farther it is, nothing at the reach. A longer reach darkens more of the road round the car. Live."

mcla_gpu_ao_rt_rays.help:
"Diagnostic: the ray traced occlusion's rays a pixel, 1 to 4; 0 (the default) is the occlusion's level (high 2, ultra 4). The occlusion's own "
    "history averages the frames, so a few rays a frame are enough. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_chrome_rt_others.help:
"Diagnostic: where the graphics card can ray trace and the car self-reflection runs, the chrome of the OTHER cars (opponents, traffic: the tailpipes, "
    "badges and trim) is darkened under their own bodies from their real shape, as your own car's chrome is (mcla_gpu_car_chrome_occlusion): two "
    "short rays a chrome pixel against the cars in the ray traced scene (mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars), traced where the picture of the frame before shows "
    "the chrome. Off: their chrome takes the marched version (the picture of the car of the frame before), as before this. Needs "
    "mcla_gpu_car_chrome_occlusion and the other cars in the scene. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_model_walk.help:
"Debug: every N-th guest frame (0 = off) reads the model data of every car the game has (the player's vehicle, the renderer's list of vehicles, every vehicle "
    "the game's draw call is made for: the cars the camera does not see too) straight from guest memory, down to each geometry's vertex and index buffer "
    "(address, stride, declaration, count, position element), bone index and bone palette, part matrix source and paint colours, and logs under [car model walk] "
    "how it compares with the draws of the frame: for a car the camera sees, how many of its walked geometries are a draw of the frame (matched), have no draw "
    "(walked-only) or how many draws of its have no geometry (drawn-only); for a car it does not see, how many geometries the walk found and whether their "
    "buffers look resident. Reads only, nothing is built from it and nothing is written in the guest. With this on the car draws are collected in every frame, "
    "whether a car effect asks for them or not. Never saved. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_paint_gamma.help:
"Debug: the game's paint colours (what the player picks: an orange is 0.90, 0.49, 0.20) are raised to this power to be the colour the paint's light makes of them, for the "
    "colour another car shows in the ray traced reflection where the camera does not see the car (its paint, from the game's customisation record). 2: about what the "
    "game's own paint does (a car of colour 0.22 is black). 1: the colours as they are (paler, more grey). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_paint_lit.help:
"Debug: how bright a paint of colour 1 is lit in the open, in the paint's units (a shader's output), for the colour another car shows in the ray traced reflection where "
    "the camera does not see the car; the reflection's own shade (0.4) is applied to it for a part in shade. 0.8: the estimate from the pictures. Larger makes the "
    "neighbouring cars brighter in the reflection. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_memory.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the ray traced car effects also see the cars the camera does not (the car beside yours, out of the picture): a car that was "
    "drawn while it was near is remembered, and while it is not drawn it is placed again from the game's own list of cars. The same class limits apply "
    "(nearest cars, by distance to your car). off: only the cars drawn this frame. The reflection shows a remembered car in its paint where the model data gave it "
    "(mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_model), else in a fixed grey in shade (its colour is not known while the camera does not see it). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_model.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the ray traced car effects see the cars the camera does not draw built from the cars' OWN MODEL DATA in the game's memory (the part "
    "table, each part's vertex and index buffers, the part matrices, the paint), not only from the draws a car once made. 0: off. 1 (the default): a car built from its "
    "model data only where no car placed from memory (mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_memory) stands, and the paint colour of the car for the cars placed from memory. 2: the model "
    "data first: a car built from it wherever it is, a car placed from memory beside it is dropped. The same class limits apply (nearest cars, by distance to your car). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_match.help:
"Debug: how near, in metres, the centre of a car the camera sees must be to a car of the game's own list to be that car, for the cars the camera does not see "
    "(mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_memory). 0, the default: 3 m. A fast car's draws lag its record, so a larger number matches it; cars side by side are 3.5 m apart. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_traffic.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): how many TRAFFIC and PARKED cars the ray traced car effects see built from their own model data (mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_model), besides the racers: the cars "
    "of the game's ambient list (the renderer's traffic client) that the camera does not draw this frame, ranked by their distance to your car within the class's radius. -1 (the "
    "default): the class's count (4 on the High class, 2 on the Mid class); 0 leaves the traffic out; 1 to 8 asks for that many. A traffic car's model is a fraction of a racer's "
    "(one low detail drawable), so the count is cheap. A traffic car is placed only after its bone matrices have been checked against the draws of a traffic car the camera sees. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_wheels.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): a racer the camera does not draw is built WITH its four wheels (the tyre and the rim from the game's wheel manager, placed by the vehicle's own wheel "
    "matrices, steer and spin included), not the body and the parts alone. The wheels are placed only after their placement has been checked against the draws of the cars the "
    "camera sees. off: no wheels. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_opp_refl.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): where the graphics card can ray trace and the car self-reflection runs, the OPPONENTS' cars (the cars beside yours that the game draws with the same paint "
    "shader: mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars says how many are in the scene) reflect the cars round them (yours, the other opponents and their own wings and mirrors) from their real shape, as "
    "yours does. Off: their paint takes the screen-space version, as before. Needs the ray traced car self-reflection (mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt) and the other cars in the scene. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_opp_refl_texels.help:
"Debug: the work the opponents' ray traced reflection may spend a frame, in thousands of image texels of the cars' screen rectangles at the full cone of rays (0, the default: "
    "the graphics card's class decides: 500 on the High class, 200 on the Mid class, none on the Low class). Over it the pass casts fewer rays a texel (up to twice it: 2, over that: 1) "
    "and leaves the smaller cars out. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_opp_refl_rays.help: "Debug: the rays a texel of an opponent's paint casts: 0 (the default) by the budget (mcla_gpu_car_rt_opp_refl_texels), 4 the whole cone, 2 the outer pair, 1 the mirror ray. Live."

rearview_cars_lod.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md D): the least detailed level of the racers' models in the mirror: 0 (the default) the level the game chose for the main view, 1 at least the middle one, 2 only the coarsest. Only makes a car coarser, never finer; the main view's choice is put back after the mirror. Needs rearview_cars. Live."

rearview_cars_max.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md D): the most racers drawn in the mirror a frame: the first this many, in the game's own list order, that the mirror's camera sees. 0 (the default) draws every one it sees. Needs rearview_cars. Live."

rearview_every.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md E): the mirror's view is drawn every this many frames (1, the default, every frame). A frame that skips it asks for no mirror phase at all, so it costs nothing. The held picture is not made yet (it needs the host to keep the stamp's pixels): until it is, a skipped frame shows the main view in the mirror's rectangle, so this is a measuring switch. A camera cut (the eye jumps more than 20 m between frames) draws the mirror at once. Live."

rearview_far.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md B): the far plane of the mirror's camera in metres; the game uses the main camera's. 0 (the default) leaves it. Only ever pulls the plane in (never beyond the main camera's), and never under 20 m. Takes effect when the game next builds the mirror's camera (every frame the mirror is up). Live."

rearview_fov_scale.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md B): a multiple of the mirror camera's field of view (the stamp is 5.2:1, so the game's own is very wide). 1.0 (the default) leaves it; 0.5 shows roughly half the angle, so the game's own culling keeps fewer draws. Only narrows (0.1 to 1.0); the picture changes. Live."

rearview_lod_distance.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md C): while the mirror's phase runs, a city sector is drawn in detail only within this many metres (the game's own radius is 300 m times lod_city_scale); the rest is the coarse one-model-a-sector city. 0 (the default) leaves it. Only ever shrinks the radius. CHECK: it works only if the game walks the city's sectors inside the mirror's phase (rearview_diag and the log's mirror draw count say). Live."

mcla_gpu_mirror_class.help: "Debug, the cheap mirror (perf/MIRRORS-SURVEY.md A): the rear view mirror's draws (the ones whose viewport is the mirror's rectangle, rearview_window_*) are their own class: they skip the per-draw work of the main view's effects (ambient occlusion, contact shadows, sun shafts, volumetric light, car reflections, the car dump and frame, the headlights, the light shadows), which would otherwise see a second camera's draws. The scene line of the log always counts them (mirror: N draws/frame), on or off. Live."

mcla_gpu_mirror_glass.help: "Debug, the side mirrors without ray tracing (perf/MIRROR-VIEW.md MV3 and MV6): runs the glass finder on any card, whatever the SIDE MIRRORS row says (the row runs it by itself while its view runs). It finds the car's two mirror glasses among its draws by their shape (a small flat patch, a pair across the car at one height facing back and inward, as the ray traced side mirrors do) and publishes whether a side mirror is on the picture and wide enough to be worth a view. Nothing is drawn by it. While it is off and the row's view is not running nothing is read and nothing is published. Live."

mcla_gpu_mirror_view.help: "Debug, MIRROR-VIEW (perf/MIRROR-VIEW.md, packages MV1 and MV6): forces the shared rear view on, whatever the SIDE MIRRORS row (mcla_gpu_side_mirrors) and RT SIDE MIRRORS say (the A/B arms of the cost chain). The rear view mirror's phase draws into a small view of its own instead of the 229x44 rectangle of the main picture, and the picture is stamped into the rectangle afterwards (the HUD mirror's look, with the world behind it left whole). 0 (the default): no force, the SIDE MIRRORS row decides (its off is the game's own mirror). 1: on, the view's size is the graphics card's class (Low 384 wide, Mid 512, High 768). 2, 3, 4: on at the Low, Mid or High size, whatever the card; a forced view is redrawn every frame and runs the glass finder only with mcla_gpu_mirror_glass. The draws of the phase that cannot go into the view (they carry the G-buffer's planes, or other formats) are left out and counted in the log's mirror view line. The markers that scope the phase come from the guest hooks of package MV2: without them nothing changes. Live."

mcla_gpu_mirror_overlay.help: "Debug, MIRROR-VIEW (perf/MIRROR-VIEW.md, package MV4): the car's two side mirror glasses are drawn again at the end of the scene, after the HUD mirror, showing the shared rear view where each pixel's reflected ray goes: a mirror that shows the street behind on a graphics card that cannot ray trace. The SIDE MIRRORS row turns this on by itself while its view runs; this switch is for a forced view (mcla_gpu_mirror_view 1 to 4, which leave the overlay to it). Off (the default): the row decides. Needs the view and mcla_gpu_mirror_glass on (the row runs both) and the guest half of the shared view (the mirror camera's field of view); where the ray traced side mirrors are on they win and this does nothing. Live."

mcla_gpu_mirror_view_t0.help: "Debug, MIRROR-VIEW (perf/MIRROR-VIEW.md, section 2.3): the distance in metres beyond the mirror glass at which the glass overlay's lookup is exact (the glass is ahead of the eye the rear view is drawn from, so what is nearer or farther than this is shifted: 20 is the design's). Between 3 and 200. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_shading.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): where the graphics card can ray trace and the car self-reflection runs, a reflection ray that hits ANOTHER car shows the part in its own material: its paint "
    "colour (the gradient of the paint's constants, the livery over it), its diffuse texture, the sun and the sky's light on it, the environment map's reflection, and the lamps lit at night. Where "
    "the camera sees the part its own colour in the picture is used as before. Off: a part the camera does not see takes the stand-in colour (the colour the camera sees of that car, in shade, or "
    "its paint), as before. Needs the other cars in the scene (mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_shadow.help:
"Debug: the shaded hit on another car casts one ray towards the sun against the cars of the scene, so that a car's own shadow falls on itself and on its neighbour (the world's shadows "
    "come from the game's cascades: mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_cascade). Off: the sun lights every part that faces it, but for the world's shadows. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_gain.help:
"Debug: the brightness of the shaded hits on other cars against the colours the camera sees (1, the default). A flank that is too bright or too dark against the part of the same car "
    "the camera sees: move it. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_ambient.help: "Debug: the share of the frame's ambient light (the cars' own pixel constants) in a shaded hit on another car (1, the default). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_spec.help:
"Debug: the share of the environment map's reflection (the game's own 512x256 map, read at the reflected direction and scaled by the fresnel) in a shaded hit on another car (1, the "
    "default). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_detail.help:
"Debug: the detail of the shaded hit on another car (the car the reflection shows): the sky's openness (one ray from the hit towards the sky: a flank between two cars is darker), the contact with the ground "
    "(the lowest half metre of the car is darker), the clear coat's image of the sun by day and of a street lamp at night (a bright streak along a shoulder or a roof edge), and what each kind of part "
    "keeps of the ambient light. 1, the default; 0 is the shading as it was, above 1 makes the glints stronger. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_reach.help:
"Debug: how far, in metres, the ray traced car reflection reaches to find ANOTHER car (0, the default: by the graphics card's class, 18 m on the High class and 12 m on the Mid class; at most 20). "
    "The weight of a hit falls over this from three quarters of it (0.7 on the Mid class). Your own car's parts keep mcla_gpu_car_selfrefl_rt_length (4 m). A car is in the scene only within this reach and two metres of yours "
    "(mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_radius moves that). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_clearcoat.help:
"Debug: the clear-coat ray of the ray traced car reflection: one more ray along the exact mirror direction (no cone, no filter) beside the glossy cone, added to it by a share that follows the paint's "
    "fresnel, so that a car beside yours reads sharp in its paint (the way a clear coat does) on top of the glossy base. -1 (the default): by the graphics card's class (on the High class, off on the Mid class); "
    "0 off; above 0 on at that strength (1 is the High class's). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_coat_layer.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the paint adds the clear coat's layer over the reflection of ANOTHER CAR in the ray traced image: the car's colour by the coat's own fresnel "
    "(0.07 at N.V 0.5, 0.20 at 0.3, 0.36 at 0.2), so that a car beside yours reads in your door at the strength a real clear coat gives it (the game's own paint reflects a few percent of what it "
    "reflects at a grazing view). Off: the car replaces the environment's reflection as before, which is as weak as the environment's. Your own car's parts are untouched either way. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_calibrate.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the shaded colour of another car's hidden parts is brought to the game's own exposure: where the reflection ray hits a part of another car's paint that the "
    "camera sees, the pass also shades it by its model and compares the brightness with the game's colour there, and the shading's gain follows (about a window of twenty frames: it follows the hour). Off: the model's own "
    "light, which does not follow the hour. The census line in the log ([car rt refl] hits) says the difference either way. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_cascade.help:
"Debug: the shaded hit on another car also reads the game's own sun shadow map (its cascades) at the point, so that the reflected car stands in the light of the scene: the shade of buildings, trees "
    "and bridges falls on it as it falls on the road. Off: only the cars' own shadows (mcla_gpu_car_rt_hit_shadow). Needs the volumetric light on (it reads the cascades the game draws). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_lamps.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the lenses of the other cars in a ray traced reflection (the tail lights of the car beside yours, the headlights of the car behind) glow as the game's own lamps say: "
    "each lamp's light point (19 kinds a car: head, brake, tail, turn, reverse, police) says whether it is on and how strongly, and the lens it stands in glows by it, so a brake lamp, a lamp that is off and "
    "a turn signal's dark half-period are told apart, and nothing glows by day. A lens no lamp stands in keeps the old guess from the colour of the sun. Off: every lens at that guess. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_traffic_refl.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the paint of the TRAFFIC and parked cars (the cars of the city's streets, drawn with the game's cheap ambient paint) reflects the cars and the street round it in a ray traced "
    "reflection from their real shape, as the opponents' paint does: the car beside yours at a red light shows yours in its door. -1 (the default): by the graphics card's class (on the High class with 40 percent of the "
    "opponents' ray budget and cars up to 45 m away, on the Mid class with 25 percent and 30 m, off where there is no ray tracing); 0: off, the traffic's paint keeps the game's reads; 1 to 100: on at that percent of the "
    "budget (a car beside the player is always traced). Needs the ray traced opponents' reflection (mcla_gpu_car_rt_opp_refl). Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_parked.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): a traffic or PARKED car that the camera sees but no draw claims (the game gives a vehicle stencil ID to a car that moves; a parked car has none, so the draw path never takes it) is built into the ray traced "
    "car scene from its own model data like a car the camera does not see, so the player's reflections show the parked cars in front of the camera as well as the ones behind it. "
    "Within the traffic count of mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_traffic and the radius of the graphics class, nearest first. Needs mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_model. off: a car the camera sees is left to the draw path, as before. Live."

mcla_gpu_car_rt_parked_paint.help:
"Debug (the fix's own switch): the PARKED cars' own ray traced paint reflections. A parked car writes no vehicle stencil ID, so its paint kept the game's reflections "
    "while the player's paint reflected it. With this on, the car's texels in the car history image are marked by its box and depth (a negative distance), its parts carry the traffic paint's bit, and its paint draw is "
    "given the constants of a still car, so the opponents' ray traced pass traces the parked car's paint like a moving traffic car's and the player's reflections show its exact colour. Within the traffic count of "
    "mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_traffic and the share of mcla_gpu_car_rt_traffic_refl; needs mcla_gpu_car_rt_cars_parked. off: a parked car is reflected but keeps the game's paint, as before. Live."
